docs.title: What DFO Online is
docs.summary: DFO Online is a browser-played reimplementation of Daggerfall that uses your own game data and adds shared online play.
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - DFO Online is a reimplementation of the 1996 role-playing game The Elder Scrolls II: Daggerfall.
> - You play in a browser at the DFO site; the game itself is served from /play/.
> - You need your own copy of Daggerfall's original game data. DFO does not include it.
> - Online play adds shared systems and rules to the port. Your interface and many personal settings remain yours.

## A shared Daggerfall world

DFO Online began as a port of Daggerfall Unity, but it has developed into its own game. Daggerfall Unity remains a
reference for its data and logic; DFO rebuilds the presentation in WebGL2 and adds its own online systems. You explore
the familiar world alongside other players, with rules that can differ from offline Daggerfall Unity.

You play it at daggerfalljs.dev, and the game itself opens from the site's
Play page. The project is open source at
Lattymoy/daggerfall-js-source, and players compare notes on the
DFO Discord.

The game reads original Daggerfall data from your own copy. Those files are required and are not part of the DFO
repository or download. See Playing in the browser for the client and data requirements.

## Your first character

New characters begin in Privateer's Hold, a dungeon that introduces movement, interaction and survival. Your early
route leads out to Gothway Garden. The guide follows that same order: your first minutes,
then moving and fighting.

## Online rules

Some rules are shared so everyone in a room meets the same world; other choices belong to you. For example, the online
lane forces selected world systems on, while your interface skin is a personal setting. Where this guide describes a
system that differs online, it explains the online rule in that page.

## Next

- Playing in the browser
- Interface skins

docs.title: Playing in the browser
docs.summary: Open the web client, provide your own Daggerfall data when prompted, and get past the common startup problems.
headings: If the screen does not appear
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Open DFO Online at daggerfalljs.dev and choose Play to reach /play/.
> - Have your own Daggerfall copy ready. The browser game does not ship the original ARENA2 data.
> - On your first visit the game asks you to pick your ARENA2 folder once; on a phone you can hand over a zip instead.
> - The client uses WebGL2; a current Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari works.

## Get the game data

DFO needs the original Daggerfall data files — the project calls the folder ARENA2. They are not bundled with DFO and
stay on your device. The official site recommends any of these free sources:

- Steam
- GOG
- DaggerfallGameFiles.zip

On a Steam installation the folder is usually DF/DAGGER/ARENA2. The guide's
first-launch page covers what happens after you press Play.

## Open the client

The project's landing page is separate from the game. Choose its Play link to open /play/. DFO draws its
presentation with WebGL2 in the browser.

## Provide the original data

When the play page asks for the folder, select your ARENA2 folder (or drop the zip on the page on a phone). The game
remembers that choice; you are not asked again on that browser.

> [!note] Your files stay yours
> The desktop build also reads ARENA2 from your own Daggerfall folder. DFO's repository does not contain those game
> data files.

## If the screen does not appear

Work through these in order:

1. Reload the page. A first WebGL2 start can fail while the browser builds its graphics context.
2. Try a current browser. The official site lists Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari; an old browser or a disabled
   WebGL2 may refuse the client.
3. Check the data folder. If you picked the wrong folder, or moved Daggerfall after picking it, the client cannot
   read ARENA2. Pick the folder again from the installation's ARENA2 directory.
4. Report it. If it still fails, say what you did on the project's
   issue tracker or the
   DFO Discord.

The source does not specify a supported-browser list or a minimum graphics-card requirement; the official site is the
authority for what the project currently supports.

## Common mistakes

- Picking the Daggerfall install folder instead of ARENA2. The client reads the data folder, not the installer.
- Moving or reinstalling Daggerfall after the first pick. The remembered path stops working; pick the folder again.
- Using an old browser and blaming the game. WebGL2 support is the usual cause of a blank start.
- Expecting the browser to store a backup. Browser storage belongs to that browser; the desktop app keeps real files.

## Next

- Your first launch
- Your account
- Interface skins

- Your first 90 minutes
- Offline and online

docs.title: Offline and online
docs.summary: What DFO's two modes share, what each keeps, and what solo play gives up.
headings: Choose a world at the front door
What a solo online player gives up
Moving a character between the modes
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - The enhanced front door asks which world you want: Online, the shared world, or Offline, your own game kept on this device.
> - Offline play is free of accounts. Online play needs an account, either a guest account or a registered one.
> - Offline keeps classic Daggerfall's rules plus your own settings. Online forces the shared ruleset and adds Renown, Marks, the market, player guilds, events and questlines.
> - An offline DFO character can be brought online once; an online character can be copied to offline. Classic Daggerfall and Daggerfall Unity saves cannot be imported yet.
> - Your two characters do not share a save: local slots live on the device, an online character's checkpoints live on the account service.

## Choose a world at the front door

The enhanced front door opens on a question about which world you are entering, not which character you are loading. Online leads to the shared world and the account service's characters. Offline leads to the doors the game keeps on this device: Continue, New Game and Load Game (src/ui/enhanced/enhancedMenu.js: SECTIONSBOOT, HOMEOFFLINE, the two-question door). The game's own comment records why the question exists: players had created offline characters while believing they were making online ones.

The two modes are not difficulty levels of one character. They are two separate games that share a client, the same Daggerfall data, and many of the same systems.

## What offline play is

Offline is DFO running as a single-player game. You supply your own Daggerfall data, as for online play, and the game uses the classic Daggerfall rules with the enhancements you choose (src/systems/online/onlineLane.js: the offline path reads the player's own settings; src/systems/features.js: offline declarations are the player's). Offline single-player allows saving and loading, with F9 for a quick save and F11 for a quick load; online, loading during play is disabled (src/systems/save/saveSlots.js; src/scenes/dungeonContext.js: ONLINE-LOAD1).

Offline characters earn no Renown XP (src/net/renown.js, renownTracker.js), so the Firmament has no currency to spend offline; the Firmament is in force only online (src/systems/firmamentLive.js: firmamentInForce requires the online page). Account-held things do not exist offline either: Marks, the market, player guilds, city seats and the shared events are account-service or shared-world systems.

Offline still has the single-player content: the classic quests and main quest, the guilds and temples, dungeons, survival and horses, and whatever overhauls you switch on. Some questlines are gated on online play or a registered account, so not every line is available offline (src/systems/questlines/qlLines.js: each line's opens carries online and account flags).

## What online play is

Online is the shared world. You need an account; a guest account can play, but many account systems are limited until you register (see Your account). Your character's progress is checkpointed by the account service, so it follows the account to another device rather than staying in one browser (src/scenes/world.js: online checkpoints and exit autosave).

Online also changes the rules. Every shared rule is forced at its shipped value, balance mods are locked whole, and only looks-and-sound switches stay yours (src/systems/online/onlineLane.js; see Which rules apply online). Death is not a load: online you respawn at a safe place after a countdown, with a gold cost, while offline death is classic Daggerfall's load-a-save (src/ui/deathScreen.js: DEATH4; docs/23-playing-online.md line 209).

The shared systems are online-only: other players, the market, player guilds and city control, town raids and gates, the Arena, Starfall and the other events, Renown and the Firmament, and the questlines whose deeds the account service records.

## What a solo online player gives up

Online play does not require a party. You can fight, quest, gather and trade alone. What solo play gives up is the party layer:

- The Renown party bonus: every member of a party in the room earns the whole kill's Renown plus 10% per extra member (src/net/renown.js: RENOWNPARTYBONUSPCT, renownPartyXp; docs/23-playing-online.md, "Group up with the strong players").
- Mentor mode, which lets a high-level friend play beside a low-level character without trivialising the content: it switches on automatically in a party whose reference level is at least three below yours (src/systems/mentorMode.js: MENTORMINGAP).
- Shared travel, party rests and party-facing content such as quest instances taken together.

None of that blocks access. It is a speed and company difference, not a gate.

## Moving a character between the modes

The game supports two one-time doors. An offline DFO character can be brought online once through the Online menu; the offline character stays as it was (src/ui/enhanced/enhancedMenu.js: the Realm page, "Bring an offline character in (once)"). An online character can be copied to offline as a new local character, and nothing you do on the copy comes back online (same file, copyToOffline).

These doors move a DFO character, not a save from another game. The official site says plainly that you cannot import classic Daggerfall or Daggerfall Unity saves yet (index.html, the "Not finished" section). For the save mechanics, see Saving and returning.

## Desktop or browser

The browser client stores its local saves in that browser's storage. The desktop app keeps real save files, works offline, finds your Daggerfall install and updates itself; it is available for Windows, Apple-silicon macOS and Linux, and it is not code-signed yet, so the first launch warns (https://daggerfalljs.dev/, "The desktop app" and "Saves"). On a phone, the browser client takes the Daggerfall data as a zip and shows touch controls (Playing in the browser).

For online characters the choice matters less than for offline ones: the account service holds the character. For offline characters it matters a great deal, because a browser's local store does not follow you to another browser or to the app.

## Common mistakes

- Starting offline by mistake. The front door asks Online or Offline for a reason. An offline character does not earn Renown or Marks, and cannot join the shared world's systems.
- Expecting account rewards offline. No Renown, Marks, market, player guild or shared event runs in an offline game.
- Clearing browser data to "fix" the game. For a browser offline character, that can remove local slots. Online characters live on the account service, but a guest's session can be lost with the browser.
- Expecting a mid-session load online. Online loading is disabled; the offline save-and-load loop does not apply there.
- Importing a DFU save. Import is not available yet. Character creation in DFO is how a character begins.

## Next

- Your first launch
- Your account

docs.title: Your first launch
docs.summary: What happens from the play page to your first character, and how to get back in later.
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Choose Play on the official site.
> - Pick your ARENA2 folder once to supply the game files.
> - An account is optional offline; you need one to play online.
> - Your first character wakes in Privateer's Hold.
> - Closing the tab does not end your online character. Browser-storage saves belong to that browser.

## Press Play

Open the official site and choose Play. This opens the play page at /play/.

You need your own copy of The Elder Scrolls II: Daggerfall, which has been free since 2009. Your game files stay on your device.

On your first visit, pick the ARENA2 folder or drop it onto the page. For a Steam installation, look under DF/DAGGER/ARENA2. Pick that folder itself, rather than its parent. On a phone, supply the zip instead. The page remembers your selection, so you do not repeat this on each launch. See Playing in the browser for setup help.

## Your first character

Enter character creation and follow the prompts. The creation screens guide explains the choices as you meet them.

Online, you are asked which leveling system to use. Only classic Daggerfall leveling is available online: the Oblivion-style option is visible but unavailable. Seeing that option does not mean you can select it for an online character.

After the character summary, you wake in Privateer's Hold. Follow Your first minutes when you arrive. On a phone, touch controls appear automatically. On a computer, use WASD and the mouse, F6 for your pack, and Esc for the other menus.

## Coming back

Open the site and choose Play again. Your online character is tied to your account; see Your account for account guidance. Closing the tab does not delete that character.

Browser saves live in browser storage. Clearing the site's data removes those local saves, and another browser does not share them. The desktop app keeps real save files that you can back up. An online character's progress is held by the account service, so it follows the account rather than one browser; that is why registering before you invest time matters (see Your account).

Online, the game saves as you go and on exit. Loading a save during play is disabled, so do not plan around saving before a decision and loading to undo it. Offline single-player allows saving and loading; F9 quick saves and F11 quick loads there.

## If nothing appears

Reload the page first. Use a current version of Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari with WebGL2 support. If your game files have moved, pick the ARENA2 folder again.

If the problem remains, use the issue tracker or ask in the official Discord.

## Common mistakes

- Picking the wrong folder. Supply ARENA2 itself, not the Steam library or the enclosing DAGGER folder.
- Clearing browser data. This removes local saves. Keep that consequence in mind before clearing site storage.
- Expecting to load mid-session online. The online game blocks loading during play; the offline save/load loop does not apply.

## Next

- Playing in the browser
- Your account

- Your first 90 minutes

docs.title: Your first 90 minutes
docs.summary: A suggested first session from the Play page to your first town quest and questline letter.
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - This page is a route, not a rulebook: each step links to the page that explains the system.
> - Expect the first half hour to be setup and character creation, the middle to be Privateer's Hold, and the last part to be your first town.
> - Decide on an account before you invest time. A guest can play, but several systems stay closed until you register.
> - Questline letters arrive only in a town, outdoors, by day, about one new line per hour of your character's clock.

## Before the clock starts

Two decisions shape the session, and both are easier before you are in the game.

1. Browser or desktop app. The browser needs a current Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari with WebGL2. The desktop app keeps real save files, works offline and reads your Daggerfall install from disk; it is not code-signed yet, so the first launch warns. Both are opened through daggerfalljs.dev, and the desktop downloads are listed there. On a phone, the browser client takes a zip of the game data and adds touch controls.
2. Guest or registered account. A guest account can connect, fight, chat and quest. It cannot use professions or Stores, the market, player guilds or Marks, and questline deeds are not recorded for it. Registration adds a username and password to the same account and keeps what you have already done. If you plan to play past an evening, decide to register now; recovery codes are shown once. See Your account.

You also need your own copy of Daggerfall. The client asks for the ARENA2 folder once (or the zip on a phone). On Steam it is usually under DF/DAGGER/ARENA2. Picking the enclosing folder instead is the first common failure; see Playing in the browser and Your first launch.

## Suggested pace

The times below are a pace, not a requirement. A first session that reaches town with a banked purse and one quest started is a success.

| Minutes | What you are doing |
|---|---|
| 0–10 | Choose the client, supply ARENA2, decide guest or registered |
| 10–25 | Create the character |
| 25–55 | Learn the controls in Privateer's Hold and leave it |
| 55–70 | Walk the road to Gothway Garden |
| 70–90 | Bank, shop, find work, join a guild, read the questline list |

## 10–25: create the character

Character creation is a sequence of screens, and its choices are explained in The creation screens. The short version:

- Race and class. Races are in Choosing a race; the eighteen standard classes are in Classes; mixing your own is Custom classes.
- Attributes and skills. Your class fixes the three skill groups that decide how you level. Attributes and skills explains what each attribute does.
- The rest of the wizard. Reflexes, background questions and starting gear follow, then appearance and the character summary.
- Online leveling. Online characters use classic Daggerfall leveling only; the Oblivion-style option is visible but unavailable (src/systems/chargenSession.js: withLevelingChoice, LEVEL-ONLINE-2).

A first character does not need to be optimal. It needs a weapon skill you will use, enough Endurance to survive, and a class whose restrictions you can live with. The page Choices that are hard to undo is worth two minutes.

## 25–55: Privateer's Hold

You wake in Privateer's Hold. The welcome tutorial has five short subjects: Welcome, Moving Around, Using Things, The Bars and the Compass, and The Menu and Saving (src/systems/tutorialCatalogue.js: TUTORIALTOUR). Read them; they are the game's own explanation of controls and interface.

Your task is to look through your pack, find the dungeon's exit door, and head for town. The source does not define the Hold's internal layout, so use the compass and map rather than expecting a fixed route. Useful pages while you are inside:

- Your first minutes: the welcome guidance, the journal (L) and notebook (N).
- Moving through the Hold and Fighting: movement, attack directions and the first fights.
- Loot and inventory: containers, weight and identifying.
- Health, fatigue and rest: why you should not fight on an empty fatigue bar.
- Dying online: where you return and what a death costs.

Leave through the dungeon's exit door. Outside, the Julian LeFay monument stands beside the landing; the road ahead leads to Gothway Garden, the first town (src/scenes/worldModes.js: tryExitDungeon, returnLanding; src/world/lefayMonument.js).

> [!warning] The public Hold is one way online
> Once you leave the public online room, it refuses re-entry. Finish anything you want to do inside before you take the exit. Your own private instance of the Hold is a separate copy you can re-enter later (src/scenes/instanceDoor.js, src/net/instanceRoom.js: HOLD-ONCE).

## 55–70: the road to town

Follow the road to Gothway Garden. The short walk is your first look at the Overworld: weather, travel pace and the difference between roads and wilds. If something chases you, do not stop to fight it in the open; a town gate and its watch are ahead.

When you arrive, the first thing to do is not to shop. It is to read the town: Reading a town explains the map, building kinds and opening hours.

## 70–90: your first town

1. Bank what you carry. Death online costs part of the gold you carry; banked gold is safe (Banks; docs/23-playing-online.md, "A plan", step 1: a tenth of the carried gold). The Bank of the Empire account is one account across the regions.
2. Sell the loot you do not need and buy the one thing you lack. Shops and prices covers haggling and town prosperity. Food, a cure or a better weapon are reasonable first purchases.
3. Check the notice board. The board's bounty and Work tabs give a first paid task without a guild (Notice boards).
4. Join a guild. The Fighters Guild is the simplest first guild for a new fighter; it trains, repairs and sends you to a private dungeon, and its quests give a gear choice. See The NPC guilds and Mages Guild services if you cast.
5. Look at the questline list. Pause-window Quests tab lists every line with what it waits on. The first introductions open at level 2 (The Court Crafter) and level 3 (Written in the Stars) (src/systems/questlines/qlLines.js: introCrafts, introFirmament).
6. Wait for the courier if you must. Letters arrive only in a town, outdoors, by day, at most one new line per hour of your character's clock (about seven real minutes), and never while another first letter is in flight (docs/23-playing-online.md: "Letters arrive slowly"; docs/32-questions.md: "Why haven't my questline letters arrived?"). If a step needs a building your town lacks, it waits and retries after a day of character time.

That is enough for one session. End in town, banked and rested, with one quest started and the next letter understood.

## What success looks like

- You know which mode you are in and which account you are on.
- You have left Privateer's Hold and reached Gothway Garden.
- Your gold is banked, not carried.
- You have one guild or board task and have read the Questlines list.
- You know where your save lives and how to return.

## Common mistakes

- Spending the first session in character creation. A workable character beats a perfect one; creation pages are here for later characters.
- Carrying all your gold. A death online costs part of the carried purse; bank it first.
- Waiting in a dungeon for a questline letter. Letters need a town, the outdoors and daylight.
- Buying a profession's first rank before registering. Professions and Stores are closed to guests.
- Treating the public Hold as a place to come back to. Online, it is one way.

## Next

- Your first minutes in Privateer's Hold
- Reading a town

docs.title: Saving and returning
docs.summary: Know where your progress lives, what closing the tab does, and how to return safely.
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Browser save slots live in that browser's storage; the desktop app keeps real save files.
> - Your online character is held by the account service.
> - F9 quick save and F11 quick load are the offline save/load controls; loading during online play is disabled.
> - Return through the Play page with the same account for your online character.

## What is saved where

Your character save records the character and their adventure: position, possessions, equipment, quests and other
session state. Offline browser slots live in browser storage. The desktop app uses real files instead, which you can
back up. The official site's Saves section describes this browser/app distinction.

An online character has a separate home: the account service holds its checkpoint. Local browser slots and your
online character are therefore different records. Opening an offline save is not a way to rewind an online session.
The game explicitly refuses loading during online play, including quick load.

Marks, Renown and questline deeds also have account-service records. They are not all contained in an
offline save slot. Guest restrictions differ between these systems; see Your account before
investing time in account rewards.

Recovery codes are credentials for getting back into your account. They are not character backups. Keep the codes
somewhere you can reach without opening the game or relying on this browser's storage.

## Closing the tab

Online progress saves as you go and on exit: the source has online checkpoints, an unload save, and a final checkpoint
when leaving through the menu. It also checkpoints an online character when the page is hidden.

That describes the save paths the game attempts. The source does not establish a guaranteed tab-close delay or promise
that every last change survives a browser crash or interrupted connection. Read any save failure the game reports.
For offline play, use your save controls before leaving rather than assuming the online checkpoint rules apply.

## Coming back

Open the Play page and sign into the same account. The Online menu lists
Your online characters from the service; choose the character's Play button. For installation and game-file
setup, follow Your first launch.

Local browser saves belong to the browser storage where you made them. Changing browsers or installing the desktop
app does not move those slots automatically. The app's files are a separate store; keep file backups if you use it.
Optional cloud backups are another separate operation, not an automatic copy of every local save.

## If you lose access

Use your saved recovery codes if you cannot sign into a registered account. Each code is spent separately, so preserve
the unused set. A guest relies on the device's stored session rather than a registered username and password.
Clearing that browser's data can remove your way back to the guest account. Your account explains
registration and recovery.

## Common mistakes

- Clearing site data without accounting for local saves and a guest session.
- Expecting a mid-session load to undo an online mistake.
- Playing as a guest for days before checking which rewards require registration.
- Keeping only one recovery code and discarding the remaining unused codes.

## Next

- Your first launch
- Your account

- Mods, saves and wipes

docs.title: Your account
docs.summary: Play as a guest straight away, then register before you invest in professions, trade, guilds or event rewards.
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - You can start playing at once as a guest; your progress lives on a guest account.
> - Register before you gather, craft, trade on the market, join a player guild, or collect festival and event rewards.
> - Registering keeps everything you have already done: it adds a username and password to the same account.
> - Registration gives you eight recovery codes, shown once. Save them somewhere safe.

## Guest play

When you first open DFO Online you enter as a guest with a generated name. A guest can connect, explore, fight, chat
and complete quests. Guest play is not a time-limited trial.

A guest account belongs to the device and browser it was made on. The account service treats a guest as "a device":
anything it would store for a guest could be lost with cleared browser data, so it refuses to keep the things below
for guests at all.

## What a guest can't do

| System | Guest | Registered |
|---|---|---|
| Professions (gathering and crafting) and Stores | Refused | Yes |
| The global market | Refused | Yes |
| Player guilds | Can't found or join | Yes |
| Marks (the account currency) | No balance | Yes |
| Witches' Festival Soul Cakes and offerings | Refused | Yes |
| Starfall claims | Thanked, never counted | Counted toward rewards |
| Questline deeds and rewards | Steps can start, but deeds and rewards aren't recorded; some lines require registration | Recorded |
| Renown | Tracked by account | Tracked by account |

The practical rule: if you plan to play for more than an evening, register early. Nothing you did as a guest is lost
when you do.

## Registering

1. Open the Account screen and choose Register.
2. Choose a username and password. An email address is optional.
3. The game shows your recovery codes: eight of them, displayed once and never again. Each code can open your
   account if you forget your password.

> [!warning] Save your recovery codes
> The service stores only a scrambled form of each code, so nobody (including the game's staff) can show them to you
> again. Write them down or keep them in a password manager before you close the screen.

The Account screen later shows how many unused recovery codes you have left (a count, never the codes themselves).

## Common mistakes

- Playing for days as a guest. Gathering, crafting, market trades and event rewards you earned as a guest were
  never recorded, and can't be claimed after you register.
- Clearing browser data while still a guest. The guest account is tied to that browser.
- Not saving recovery codes. Without them and without your password, there is no way back in.

## Next

- Interface skins and menus
- Creating your character

docs.title: Menus and screens
docs.summary: Find your journal, growth pages, possessions, settings and maps without searching every menu.
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Esc opens the pause menu when no overlay is open; it also backs out of overlays.
> - L opens your journal, N your notebook, and F6 your pack.
> - M opens the local AutoMap; V opens TravelMap. The separate Overworld TravelView action ships unbound.
> - F opens social interaction.
> - In the enhanced pause menu, start with Quests, Growth or Holdings for those subjects.

## Choose a door

Enhanced pause tabs and selected destination doors

The table describes the enhanced pause menu. Its tabs are Quests, Stats, Growth, Holdings, Family,
Tutorials and System. The Family tab appears only when its Legacy conditions are met. Other pages can depend
on the current host, enabled systems or what your character has to show.

Classic uses a different pause window. Direct Professions and Legacy Family actions open enhanced pages on either skin.

| Door | Key/path | What it holds |
|---|---|---|
| Journal and quests | L; pause → Quests | Accepted quests, questlines and pending quest reward choices |
| Notebook | N | Your notebook |
| Pack | F6; pause → Stats → Pack when offered | Inventory and equipment |
| Character | F5; pause → Stats | Character, attributes, skills, advantages, standing and effects |
| Firmament | Pause → Growth → Firmament | Your online star tree |
| Specialisations | Pause → Growth → Specializations | The mastery-path guide; the UI uses the spelling “Specializations” |
| Masteries | Growth's Master Skills door; Stats → Master Skills button | Master Skills state and choices; the resulting page belongs to Stats |
| Professions | Down Arrow off a ship's helm; pause → Stats → Professions | Profession progress and pages online |
| Stores | Pause → Holdings → Stores | Profession storage online |
| Mounts and carts | Pause → Holdings → Stable | Horse and wagon status and available management actions |
| Ships | Pause → Holdings → Fleet | Your ships and available fleet actions |
| Companions | Pause → Holdings → Companions | Sworn companions and their management |
| Homes | No general Homes page in the checked Holdings rail | Do not search Holdings for a home-management screen |
| Legacy family | Pause → Family; Numpad / when enabled | Family tree, house and Hall of Ancestors; a separate tab from Holdings |
| Settings | Pause → System → Settings | Controls, Accessibility, Graphics, Gameplay and other settings tabs |
| Local map | M | AutoMap for your nearby surroundings |
| Travel map | V | TravelMap for travel destinations |
| Overworld | TravelView action; no default key | The separate Overworld Travel View |

## The two maps

Use AutoMap for local orientation. Its default action is M. Use TravelMap, bound to V, when choosing places
across the Bay. The map and danger explains how to read places and danger before
you set out.

The Overworld Travel View is separate. Its TravelView action ships unbound. Check Controls for your assigned
binding, then follow Overworld travel for route planning. Open map windows have their
own controls.

## Settings

Open System → Settings → Controls → Key bindings to inspect and change your bindings. These pages describe
shipped defaults; saved personal bindings may differ.

Accessibility groups its options under Motion, Readability, Danger shapes and Large status bar.
The source includes head bobbing, camera recoil and reduced motion under Motion, and font rendering and health/fatigue
colour swapping under Readability.

Interface skins live under Overhauls → UI Overhaul, rather than Controls. Follow
Interface and skins for the available looks and the reload involved in changing one.

## Common mistakes

- Pressing Esc expecting to quit: it opens pause, or closes the overlay already in front of you.
- Confusing M and V, or expecting V to open the unbound TravelView action.
- Looking for the Firmament on Stats or Holdings instead of Growth.

## Next

- Interface and skins
- Controls and settings

docs.title: Interface and skins
docs.summary: Choose a Classic or Enhanced Plus interface, then find the menus and quickbar controls you will use most.
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Choose the interface under Overhauls → UI Overhaul.
> - The two base skins are Classic and Enhanced Plus; GrimoireUI and DFO Grimoire are additional looks.
> - In the enhanced interface, choose a hotbar or diamond quickbar layout.
> - The pause menu's Settings opens the settings screen; controls are a tab inside it.

## Choose an interface

Open Overhauls, then its UI Overhaul panel. Choose Classic for the original interface or Enhanced Plus
for DFO's enhanced interface. The panel also offers GrimoireUI, which dresses Classic, and DFO Grimoire, which
dresses Enhanced Plus. Changing the interface reloads the game.

Your interface choice stays yours online. The online lane does not force a skin, and the chat, friends, party and
trading panels are available with either interface.

## Find the menus

In the enhanced interface, Settings is available from the main menu and during play. Controls is a tab inside
Settings, with Key bindings in that tab; it is not a separate menu.

## Quickbar layouts

The enhanced interface lets you choose a ten-slot hotbar or a diamond quickbar. Classic uses the diamond
quickbar. This layout is a personal preference online too.

## Interface skin and character appearance

The interface skin changes menus and HUD presentation. It does not change your character's appearance. Character
appearance is chosen separately; see Appearance when you reach character creation.

## Next

- Controls and settings

docs.title: Controls and settings
docs.summary: Learn the default movement and combat bindings, choose a swing mode, and rebind actions from Settings.
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Move with W/A/S/D, jump with Space, and run with Left Shift by default.
> - Right click swings a weapon; Z readies or sheathes it; H switches hands.
> - DFO defaults to Click or Hold swings (random direction). Change the swing mode in Settings → Controls.
> - Rebind actions under Settings → Controls → Key bindings.

## Default movement controls

| Action | Default |
|---|---|
| Move | W/A/S/D |
| Turn | Left and right arrow keys |
| Look up/down | Insert/Delete |
| Centre view | Home |
| Jump | Space |
| Crouch/sneak | C |
| Run | Left Shift |
| Auto-run | Middle mouse button |

These are the shipped keyboard and mouse bindings; you can rebind them. The game also has a secondary binding set for
gamepads.

## Combat controls

| Action | Default |
|---|---|
| Ready or sheath weapon | Z |
| Swing weapon | Right mouse button |
| Switch hands | H |
| Weapon technique | Mouse3, the mouse's back side button |

On a touch screen, the technique action is a hold button labelled Tech. Gamepad technique input has no default
secondary binding in the source, so bind it if you want to use it.

## Choose how swings work

DFO's default Weapon Swing Mode is Click or Hold: a click swings, and holding the button keeps swinging, each
swing in a random direction. Click swings once per press. Gesture (single-player Daggerfall Unity's default)
makes you hold the button and drag the mouse, and the drag direction chooses the swing. Choose a mode under
Settings → Controls.

Your swing-mode setting is not forced online. The online lane forces Allow Magic Repairs, but it does not force a
weapon swing mode.

## Rebind an action

1. Open Settings.
2. Choose Controls → Key bindings.
3. Select the action and assign its primary binding; assign a secondary gamepad binding if useful.

The settings screen also has Graphics, Gameplay, Combat, World, Interface, Audio,
Accessibility, and Mods & files tabs.

## Next

- Moving through the Hold
- Fighting

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.summary: Check startup, performance and save problems, then report what you can reproduce.
headings: When the game will not start
When the screen is difficult to read
When a save or character seems missing
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Check whether the problem is game startup, online sign-in or a missing local save.
> - Confirm that you supplied ARENA2 before changing graphics settings.
> - Read the error beside a cloud action; a failed backup is not a completed backup.
> - Record what happens before clearing browser data or changing devices.

## When the game will not start

Start with playing in the browser. The game needs your original ARENA2 data and uses WebGL2 for rendering. 

If the picker appears, select the ARENA2 folder rather than its parent installation directory. The browser data source imports and remembers files in its own storage. That is different from the desktop app reading your folder on disk: moving the original folder is not, by itself, proof that an already imported browser copy has broken.

If startup still fails, record the visible message and the point where loading stops. Try reloading or a current browser. The source gives no universal blank-canvas fix or minimum graphics-card specification. If you try another browser, expect it to have a separate data store and to need its own game-data setup.

Do not use clearing site data as your first diagnostic step. The same browser can hold imported game data, local save slots and a guest session.  The source does not establish a recovery method for a local save whose only stored copy has been erased.

## When performance is poor

Open Settings > Graphics. The source groups controls under Quality, Display, View distance & detail, lighting, sky and water, plants, shadows and post effects. Start with the graphics preset and inspect the controls that remain available online.

Render scale, land view distance and cloud quality are useful settings to investigate because they change what your device draws. Compare the same place after each adjustment. Some settings are governed by online policy; a disabled or forced setting does not mean your browser failed to remember it.

The enhanced and classic lanes also need care. Online play enforces shared gameplay and world rules, while the interface skin remains your choice. Choosing a Classic interface does not turn off the online world's enhancements or change shared combat balance.  See interface skins.

The source does not promise a frame-rate gain from a particular setting, nor does it identify one preset that suits every device. If performance remains poor, report where it happens: a crowded town, outdoors, underwater and a dungeon can present different workloads. 

## When the screen is difficult to read

Open Settings > Accessibility. The tab contains these sections:

| Section | What you can inspect |
|---|---|
| Motion | Head bobbing, camera recoil, technique motion, reduced motion, motion blur and vignette controls |
| Readability | Health/fatigue colour swapping, dim strength and SDF font rendering |
| Danger shapes | Danger palette and telegraph fill |
| Large status bar | Enable, docking, scale, alignment and weapon/horse offset controls |

The danger palettes include Standard, High contrast, Deutan-Protan and Tritan. Their implemented uses include the Elite Breach's danger shapes; do not assume they recolour every object in the game. Reduced motion likewise changes supported animations rather than promising to remove all motion. 

For an action that appears unresponsive, check the active binding before assuming it is broken. Keys and commands helps you distinguish a control problem from a quest or network problem.

## When a save or character seems missing

First establish which record you expect. An online character checkpoint belongs to the account service. Local browser save slots belong to this browser's storage. Optional cloud backups of local slots are a third record.

For an online character, sign into the same account and inspect Online > Your online characters. Online checkpoints are attempted during play, on page hiding and on exit. A crash or connection failure can still lose recent progress. Loading an offline save cannot rewind your online character.

For a local slot, return to the browser or device where you saved it. Cloud backup is an explicit action, not an automatic upload whenever you save. On another device, sign into the same account and inspect its available cloud cards. A cloud-only card can be downloaded; a newer backup can be restored over its corresponding older local copy through the offered action.

Read refusals literally. “Load this save once” means an older local card needs a character identity before backup. “No room” concerns the local import. Refresh the listing after a changed-backup refusal.  The cloud code imports the replacement before removing the older matching local copy, so a failed download does not intentionally delete it.

## Known issues and reporting

The snapshot contains fixes for earlier field reports, not a complete current known-issues list. Check the game's issue tracker for an existing report, or use the DFO Discord for help identifying the problem. 

Use /bug for the private developer report form, especially for exploits or account-security problems. /report concerns player conduct. The project's README asks you to report exploits privately.

Include these details in a bug report:

- Browser and version, operating system, and browser or desktop app.
- Online or offline play, interface skin, relevant settings and visible game version if available.
- Steps from a working state to the failure, with expected and actual results.
- Exact error wording, location, quest title or affected save action, and approximate time.
- Whether it happens again, and which changes you tried with their results.

## Common mistakes

- Erasing browser storage before identifying which saves and credentials it contains.
- Expecting an account sign-in to copy every local slot automatically.
- Posting an exploit publicly instead of using the private report route.

## Next

- Saving and returning
- How this guide is checked

- Stuck and recovery

docs.title: The creation screens
docs.summary: Character creation is a short wizard, from race to a final summary; this page walks through each screen and what it decides.
headings: Three ways to choose a class
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Creation runs in a fixed order: race, gender, class, biography, name, face, attributes, skills, reflexes, then a
>   summary.
> - Your class decides most of your character: its attributes, skills, health per level and how fast you level.
> - Race decides your look and, for three races, a resistance or immunity. It does not change your attributes.
> - New online characters always use the classic levelling system.

## The order of the screens

Twelve creation screens from race to summary

| Step | Screen | What you decide |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Race | One of eight races. See Choosing a race. |
| 2 | Gender | Your character's body and portrait set. |
| 3 | Class method | Answer questions to be given a class, pick one from the list, or build a custom class. |
| 4 | Class | One of the eighteen classes, or the Custom row. See Classes and Custom classes. |
| 5 | Biography method | Answer background questions, or skip them. |
| 6 | Biography | Questions about your past; some answers adjust your starting details. |
| 7 | Name | Your character's name. |
| 8 | Face | One of ten faces for your race and gender. |
| 9 | Attributes | Your eight attributes, with bonus points to place. See Attributes and skills. |
| 10 | Skills | Your starting skill values, with points to place in each skill tier. |
| 11 | Reflexes | How quickly enemies react to you, from Very High to Very Low. |
| 12 | Summary | Check everything, then enter the world. |

The interface skin changes how these screens look, not what they ask. Classic and Enhanced skins run the same steps.

## Three ways to choose a class

- Questions: answer a short set of situational questions and the game proposes the class that fits your answers.
- List: pick any of the eighteen classes directly. Each has fixed attributes, skills and special abilities.
- Custom: design your own class: choose its skills, health per level, advantages and disadvantages. The game
  measures how strong the result is and makes a stronger class level more slowly.

If you already know the playstyle you want, the list or custom route gives you the most control.

## Attributes: rolled, then placed

Each attribute starts from your class's base value plus a random 0 to 10. You then get a pool of 6 to 14 bonus points
to place, one at a time, within the screen's limits. Reroll until you like the starting spread, then place the pool on
the attributes your playstyle relies on.

> [!online] Online rule
> New online characters always use classic levelling. Single-player Daggerfall Unity also offers an
> Oblivion-style levelling option; it is not available online.

## Skills: three tiers

Your class sorts skills into three tiers. Each tier starts higher than the one below, and each tier gives you 6 points
to place on the skills in it:

| Tier | Skills | Starting value |
|---|---|---|
| Primary | 3 | 28 to 31 |
| Major | 3 | 18 to 21 |
| Minor | 6 | 13 to 16 |
| Everything else | the rest | 3 to 6 |

Your tiered skills also drive your character level: you level up when they have risen far enough. See
Attributes and skills.

## Reflexes

Reflexes are a difficulty setting for combat. There are five settings, from Very High to Very Low; the default
is Average. Higher reflexes make fights harder:

| Reflexes | Time between an enemy's melee attacks | Chance a monster lands each of its extra attacks |
|---|---|---|
| Very High | 0.9 seconds shorter than Average | 70% |
| High | 0.45 seconds shorter | 60% |
| Average | the base timing | 50% |
| Low | 0.45 seconds longer | 40% |
| Very Low | 0.9 seconds longer | 30% |

Online, enemies also telegraph many of their attacks (a glint and a marked shape on the ground; see
Fighting). A telegraphed attack lands when its wind-up completes, not on the timer above, so
reflexes mostly change the pace of an enemy's ordinary swings and how many of a monster's extra attacks connect.

The setting is fixed at creation. If you are new to Daggerfall-style combat, Average or Low is a comfortable start.

## Next

- Choosing a race
- Classes

docs.title: Choosing a race
docs.summary: Race sets your look, gives three races a resistance or immunity, and online gives six races bonuses with particular weapons.
headings: How much the racial effects matter
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Race sets your look, a defence for three races, and, online, weapon bonuses for six races.
> - Defences: Breton (resistance to magic), Nord (resistance to frost), High Elf (immunity to paralysis).
> - Weapon bonuses: Redguard, Nord, Dark Elf, Wood Elf, Khajiit and Argonian each hit harder and more accurately with
>   certain weapons. Khajiit and Nords also fight better bare-handed.
> - Race does not change your attributes or skills; your class sets those. See Classes.

## What race decides

Race sets your character's appearance: portrait, face set and body shape. It sets one defensive trait for three races,
and online it adds combat bonuses with certain weapons for six. It does not add to attributes at creation (they
come from your class plus a roll), and it does not raise skills.

## The eight races

| Race | Body | Defence | Weapon bonuses (online) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Breton | Human | Resistance to Magic | None |
| Redguard | Human | None | Long Blade, Blunt Weapon, Axe, Archery |
| Nord | Human | Resistance to Frost | Axe, Blunt Weapon, bare hands (damage only) |
| Dark Elf | Elf | None | Long Blade, Short Blade |
| High Elf | Elf | Immunity to Paralysis | None |
| Wood Elf | Elf | None | Short Blade, Archery |
| Khajiit | Khajiit | None | Short Blade, bare hands |
| Argonian | Argonian | None | Short Blade |

No playable race carries a weakness: none has low tolerance or critical weakness to anything.

## Racial weapon bonuses

> [!online] Online rule
> These bonuses come from the Physical Combat and Armor Overhaul, which DFO forces on for every online player. Each
> bonus is worked out from your attributes, so it grows as they rise.

The table shows each bonus for a character with 50 in every attribute, as an example. Higher attributes raise
them.

| Race and weapon | Damage | To hit | Driven mostly by |
|---|---|---|---|
| Redguard, Long Blade | +2 | +9 | Agility |
| Redguard, Blunt Weapon | +2 | +5 | Strength |
| Redguard, Axe | +4 | +3 | Strength |
| Redguard, Archery | +2 | +4 | Agility |
| Nord, Axe | +4 | +3 | Strength |
| Nord, Blunt Weapon | +4 | +4 | Strength, Endurance |
| Nord, bare hands | +2 | +0 | Strength, Endurance |
| Dark Elf, Long Blade | +4 | +4 | Agility, Strength |
| Dark Elf, Short Blade | +2 | +3 | Agility, Speed |
| Wood Elf, Short Blade | +2 | +4 | Agility |
| Wood Elf, Archery | +4 | +9 | Agility, Strength |
| Khajiit, Short Blade | +2 | +4 | Agility |
| Khajiit, bare hands | +4 | +6 | Strength, Endurance, Agility |
| Argonian, Short Blade | +2 | +5 | Agility |

A matching race and class weapon add up: a Wood Elf archer gets the racial archery bonus and any bonus their class
gives for archery.

## How much the racial effects matter

When a hostile spell or effect reaches you, you get a saving throw: a chance to shrug it off, starting at 50%.
Racial effects change that chance:

| Racial effect | Effect on your saving chance |
|---|---|
| Resistance (Breton: magic; Nord: frost) | +30 points (50% becomes 80%) |
| Immunity (High Elf: paralysis) | Set to 100%: the effect never lands |

- Immunity to Paralysis (High Elf) is the strongest of the three. Paralysis stops you acting entirely. A class
  can undo it, though: a custom class with low tolerance or critical weakness to paralysis cancels the racial
  immunity (see Custom classes).
- Resistance to Magic (Breton) applies to spells that carry the magic flag, which covers a wide range of hostile
  magic.
- Resistance to Frost (Nord) applies to frost spells and effects.

Class traits add on top. A custom class can buy a resistance (+25 points) or an immunity (+50 points), and these add to
the racial bonus, so a Breton with a class resistance to magic saves at 50 + 30 + 25. The chance always stays between
5% and 95% unless something grants full immunity.

> [!note] Looks and armour
> Race also picks the body used to show your worn armour (Layered Gearing). See
> Appearance.

docs.title: Classes
docs.summary: The eighteen ready-made classes, grouped into casters, rogues and fighters, with the skills each one starts strong in.
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - A class gives you your attributes, your skill tiers, your health per level, how fast you level, and
>   any built-in advantages and disadvantages.
> - DFO Online revised every ready-made class's skill lists so each one can fight from level one and no skill
>   slot is wasted on a language.
> - Casters, rogues and fighters each have six classes. Pick by how you want to play, not by name.
> - Want something else? Build a custom class.

## How the classes changed online

Single-player Daggerfall's ready-made classes spent some skill slots badly (a Barbarian whose major skills were
Jumping, Running and Swimming; casters with two languages as minor skills). DFO Online re-chose every class's skill
lists by four rules:

1. Every class can fight from the first level: a primary or major skill in a weapon it may use, or in Destruction.
2. Movement skills (Jumping, Running, Swimming, Climbing) take a primary or major slot only where the movement is the
   class's identity: the Acrobat's Jumping and Running, the Burglar's Climbing, the Monk's and Barbarian's Running.
3. No language takes a skill slot. Languages are still learnt, as miscellaneous skills.
4. A pure fighter's primaries are two weapons and Critical Strike, which helps whichever weapon it carries.

Everything else about each class (attributes, health per level, levelling speed, spell points, advantages and
disadvantages) is unchanged from the class files. One equipment fix: the Burglar is now forbidden chain and plate
armour, instead of leather and chain.

## Casters

| Class | Primary | Major | Minor |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mage | Destruction, Alteration, Mysticism | Illusion, Thaumaturgy, Restoration | Medical, Short Blade, Blunt Weapon, Dodging, Etiquette, Mercantile |
| Spellsword | Long Blade, Restoration, Alteration | Axe, Blunt Weapon, Destruction | Illusion, Thaumaturgy, Mysticism, Short Blade, Dodging, Archery |
| Battlemage | Destruction, Long Blade, Axe | Thaumaturgy, Alteration, Restoration | Illusion, Mysticism, Dodging, Archery, Short Blade, Blunt Weapon |
| Sorcerer | Destruction, Mysticism, Alteration | Thaumaturgy, Illusion, Blunt Weapon | Restoration, Short Blade, Dodging, Medical, Mercantile, Streetwise |
| Healer | Restoration, Medical, Dodging | Blunt Weapon, Alteration, Mysticism | Thaumaturgy, Destruction, Illusion, Etiquette, Streetwise, Short Blade |
| Nightblade | Illusion, Stealth, Short Blade | Destruction, Backstabbing, Dodging | Alteration, Thaumaturgy, Critical Strike, Lockpicking, Restoration, Mysticism |

## Rogues

| Class | Primary | Major | Minor |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bard | Etiquette, Streetwise, Short Blade | Illusion, Mercantile, Stealth | Pickpocket, Lockpicking, Alteration, Restoration, Destruction, Archery |
| Burglar | Lockpicking, Stealth, Short Blade | Climbing, Backstabbing, Dodging | Critical Strike, Pickpocket, Mercantile, Streetwise, Archery, Running |
| Rogue | Long Blade, Stealth, Dodging | Pickpocket, Backstabbing, Streetwise | Critical Strike, Short Blade, Lockpicking, Archery, Blunt Weapon, Running |
| Acrobat | Dodging, Jumping, Short Blade | Running, Archery, Stealth | Climbing, Hand-to-Hand, Critical Strike, Backstabbing, Pickpocket, Swimming |
| Thief | Pickpocket, Stealth, Short Blade | Backstabbing, Lockpicking, Dodging | Critical Strike, Climbing, Running, Streetwise, Mercantile, Archery |
| Assassin | Short Blade, Critical Strike, Stealth | Backstabbing, Long Blade, Archery | Dodging, Lockpicking, Climbing, Pickpocket, Streetwise, Blunt Weapon |

## Fighters

| Class | Primary | Major | Minor |
|---|---|---|---|
| Monk | Hand-to-Hand, Critical Strike, Dodging | Medical, Blunt Weapon, Running | Archery, Short Blade, Stealth, Jumping, Climbing, Swimming |
| Archer | Archery, Dodging, Critical Strike | Short Blade, Long Blade, Stealth | Axe, Blunt Weapon, Hand-to-Hand, Running, Climbing, Swimming |
| Ranger | Archery, Long Blade, Stealth | Axe, Critical Strike, Dodging | Climbing, Swimming, Running, Medical, Short Blade, Blunt Weapon |
| Barbarian | Axe, Blunt Weapon, Critical Strike | Long Blade, Dodging, Running | Medical, Climbing, Jumping, Swimming, Archery, Hand-to-Hand |
| Warrior | Long Blade, Axe, Critical Strike | Blunt Weapon, Archery, Dodging | Short Blade, Hand-to-Hand, Medical, Climbing, Running, Swimming |
| Knight | Long Blade, Blunt Weapon, Etiquette | Axe, Critical Strike, Medical | Archery, Short Blade, Dodging, Mercantile, Running, Swimming |

## Attributes, health and levelling speed

Each class also has its own base attributes, health gained per level, levelling speed and spell-point multiplier.
These come from the game's class files:

table classes.base


A class's advancement multiplier sets how many uses each skill needs to improve: a higher number means slower
skills and slower levels, in exchange for a stronger class. See Attributes and skills.

## Choosing

- Want to cast spells? Look at the casters, or the Nightblade and Bard for magic with stealth. Spell points come
  from Intelligence times the class multiplier.
- Want to fight up close? Warrior, Barbarian, Knight, or the Monk for bare hands.
- Want range? Archer or Ranger.
- Want stealth? Thief, Burglar, Assassin or Nightblade.
- Want to talk and trade? Bard and Knight carry the social skills (Etiquette, Streetwise, Mercantile).

Your skill tiers matter beyond the start: your character level rises as your primary, major and best minor skills
rise, so a class whose tiered skills match how you actually play levels faster.

docs.title: Custom classes
docs.summary: Design your own class from skills, health, attributes, advantages and disadvantages; the stronger it is, the more slowly it levels.
headings: The parts of a custom class
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Pick 3 primary, 3 major and 6 minor skills, your health per level (4 to 30), and your attributes.
> - Add up to seven advantages and seven disadvantages. Advantages make the class stronger; disadvantages make
>   it weaker.
> - The difficulty dagger shows the total. A stronger class needs more skill uses per improvement, so it levels
>   more slowly. The game refuses a class outside its difficulty limits.
> - Disadvantages you will never notice (a forbidden material you'd never wear, say) are free strength. Ones you will
>   notice every day are real costs.

## The parts of a custom class

| Part | Choice |
|---|---|
| Skills | 3 primary, 3 major, 6 minor; a skill can sit in only one tier |
| Health per level | 4 to 30, default 8 |
| Attributes | each starts at 50; move points between them, each staying within 10 to 75 |
| Advantages | up to seven |
| Disadvantages | up to seven |
| Name | your choice |

Attributes on the custom screen are a zero-sum budget: raising one lowers the pool, and the pool must balance before
you continue.

## The difficulty dagger

Every choice adds or subtracts difficulty points:

- Health per level: +1 for each point above 8, −2 for each point below 8.
- Each advantage adds its cost; each disadvantage subtracts its cost (tables below).

The total must be between −12 and +40. It sets your advancement multiplier:

> advancement multiplier = 0.3 + 2.7 × (difficulty points + 12) ÷ 52

So a class at −12 has a multiplier of 0.3 (fast levelling), a class at the default 0 has about 0.92, and a class at +40
has 3.0 (slow levelling). Every skill improvement needs a number of uses proportional to this multiplier.

> [!example] Example
> Health 12 per level (+4), Resistance to Fire (+5), Forbidden Material: Steel (−10): 4 + 5 − 10 = −1 point, a
> multiplier of about 0.87. The class is a little sturdier and still levels slightly faster than the default, at the
> price of never using steel.

## Advantages

| Advantage | Choice | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| Acute Hearing | | +1 |
| Adrenaline Rush | | +4 |
| Athleticism | | +4 |
| Bonus to Hit | Animals / Daedra / Humanoids / Undead | +6 / +3 / +6 / +6 |
| Expertise In | a weapon group | +2 |
| Immunity | Disease, Fire, Frost, Magic, Paralysis, Poison or Shock | +10 |
| Increased Magery | spell points of 1×, 1.5×, 1.75×, 2× or 3× Intelligence | +2 / +4 / +6 / +8 / +10 |
| Rapid Healing | General / in darkness / in light | +4 / +3 / +2 |
| Regenerate Health | General / in darkness / in light / while immersed | +14 / +10 / +6 / +2 |
| Resistance | Disease, Fire, Frost, Magic, Paralysis, Poison or Shock | +5 |
| Spell Absorption | General / in darkness / in light | +14 / +12 / +8 |

What some of them do:

- Acute Hearing: you hear enemies from farther away (1.25 times the distance).
- Adrenaline Rush: +8 to hit while your health is below one part in 6 of your maximum (and enemies with it are harder to hit then).
- Athleticism: jump speed +10%.
- Expertise In: bonus damage and accuracy with that weapon group, worked out from your attributes. With 50 in
  every attribute it is about +4 to +5 damage and +10 to +11 to hit, depending on the weapon. It works for
  Hand-to-Hand too.

> [!online] Online rule
> Online, Adrenaline Rush and Expertise In use the Physical Combat and Armor Overhaul's versions, which DFO forces on.
> Single-player Daggerfall Unity's versions differ (Expertise there grows with your level instead of your attributes).
- Resistance / Immunity: see the saving-throw table in Choosing a race.
  A class immunity adds 50 points to the save; a class resistance adds 25.
- Increased Magery: raises your spell points above the custom default of half your Intelligence. Only one magery
  choice is allowed.

## Disadvantages

| Disadvantage | Choice | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| Critical Weakness | an effect | −14 |
| Damage | from holy places / from sunlight | −6 / −10 |
| Darkness-Powered Magery | lower magic in daylight / no magic in daylight | −7 / −10 |
| Forbidden Armour Type | leather / chain / plate | −1 / −2 / −5 |
| Forbidden Material | Iron −1, Daedric −2, Orcish −3, Adamantium −5, Ebony −5, Mithril −6, Silver −6, Dwarven −7, Elven −9, Steel −10 | as listed |
| Forbidden Shield Types | shield types | −1 |
| Forbidden Weaponry | a weapon group | −2 |
| Inability to Regen Spell Points | | −14 |
| Light-Powered Magery | lower magic in darkness / no magic in darkness | −10 / −14 |
| Low Tolerance | an effect | −5 |
| Phobia | Animals, Daedra, Humanoids or Undead | −4 |

> [!online] Online rule: Inability to Regen Spell Points
> Offline, this stops resting from restoring spell points. Online, resting restores spell points for every class,
> including this one, so for an online character it is worth −14 points with a much smaller drawback than its name
> suggests.

Some picks block each other: you can't take the same choice twice, Bonus to Hit and Phobia against the same enemy
group, Expertise In and Forbidden Weaponry for the same weapon, or an immunity and a resistance to the same effect.

## Spells for custom classes

A custom class starts with spell points equal to half its Intelligence, raised by Increased Magery. If any magic
school is among its primary or major skills, it starts with the Spellsword's starting spells; otherwise it starts with
none.

## Designing well

- Take disadvantages you won't feel. A fighter who will wear leather and steel loses nothing by forbidding
  Daedric weapons it may never find; forbidding Steel, the most common good metal, is a real cost early on.
- Check late consequences. Forbidden materials also rule out reward gear made of them later, such as seasonal
  event sets. Read a reward's material before you buy it.
- Don't max difficulty for its own sake. A very strong class that levels at 3× takes far longer to reach the
  levels where the game's introduction questlines open.
- Match your tiers to how you'll play. Your level rises from your primary and major skills (and your best minor),
  so put the skills you'll use constantly there.

## Next

- Attributes and skills
- Classes

docs.title: Attributes and skills
docs.summary: What each of the eight attributes does online, how skills improve with use, and how your skills raise your level.
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Attributes run from 0 to 100. Each feeds specific formulas, such as carrying capacity, spell points, health per
>   level and hit chance.
> - Skills improve only by using them. There are 35, including nine languages.
> - Your level rises as your primary and major skills (and your best minor skill) rise: about every 15 points of
>   improvement in them.
> - Online, every level gives 5 attribute points to spend, and a health floor keeps your maximum health from
>   falling behind an average roll.

## The eight attributes

| Attribute | What it does online |
|---|---|
| Strength | Damage with weapons and fists: +1 for every 10 points above 50 (−1 per 10 below); carrying capacity (1.5 kg per point); part of your fatigue pool |
| Intelligence | Spell points: Intelligence times your class's spell-point multiplier |
| Willpower | Resisting spells: every 10 points add 1 to your saving throw |
| Agility | Hitting what you swing at: +1 to hit for every 4 points you have above your target's Agility (and −1 per 4 below) |
| Endurance | Health gained each level: adds (Endurance ÷ 10) − 5 to each roll; part of your fatigue pool; health recovered while resting |
| Personality | How people react when you talk to them; part of shop prices, with Mercantile |
| Speed | How fast you move and how fast your weapon swings; also +1 to hit for every 8 points above your target's Speed |
| Luck | +1 to hit for every 10 points above your target's Luck; a target with high Luck is harder to hit; part of your critical-hit chance |

> [!online] Online rule: one combat ruleset
> Online combat always uses the Physical Combat and Armor Overhaul's formulas (a mod DFO forces on for every player),
> not classic Daggerfall's. Under it, your chance to hit compares your Agility, Speed and Luck with your target's,
> and the final chance is kept between 3% and 97%: no blow is ever certain to land or to miss.

Your fatigue pool is Strength plus Endurance; your carrying capacity is one and a half times your Strength in
kilograms. Your starting health is 25 plus your class's health per level.

> [!note] Live values
> Spells, potions, gear and curses can raise or lower an attribute for a while. Formulas use the live value, kept
> between 0 and 100 unless an effect lifts the ceiling.

## Skills

There are 35 skills. Every character has all of them; your class decides which start high (see
The creation screens).

| Group | Skills |
|---|---|
| Weapons | Short Blade, Long Blade, Hand-to-Hand, Axe, Blunt Weapon, Archery, Critical Strike |
| Magic | Destruction, Restoration, Illusion, Alteration, Thaumaturgy, Mysticism |
| Stealth | Stealth, Backstabbing, Lockpicking, Pickpocket |
| Movement | Running, Jumping, Climbing, Swimming, Dodging |
| People | Etiquette, Streetwise, Mercantile, Medical |
| Languages | Orcish, Harpy, Giantish, Dragonish, Nymph, Daedric, Spriggan, Centaurian, Impish |

Skills improve by doing the thing: swinging a weapon, casting a spell of that school, sneaking, trading, talking,
running. Languages improve when you speak with creatures of that kind (or fight them).

### How quickly a skill improves

Each improvement needs a number of uses that grows with:

- the skill's current value (high skills need more uses);
- the skill's own rate (some skills are naturally slow: Running and the languages need many uses, Medical and
  Critical Strike quite a few);
- your class's advancement multiplier (see Custom classes);
- your character level (about 4% more per level).

Skills don't rise the moment you've done enough. They are checked when at least six game hours have passed since the
last check, typically when you rest or travel. The enhanced character sheet shows how close each skill is.

## Levelling up

Your level is worked out from a skill sum: your three primary skills, plus your major skills except the lowest,
plus your highest minor skill. Each time that sum rises about 15 points above where you started, you gain a
level.

When you level up online:

- you get 5 attribute points to place (offline Daggerfall Unity rolls 4 to 6);
- you gain health: a roll based on your class's health per level, plus your Endurance bonus, at least 1;
- the health floor applies: your maximum health is never lower than what an average roll at every level would have
  given, at your current permanent Endurance. Raising Endurance later lifts the floor for past levels too.

> [!tip] Spend points where they pay
> Points in Endurance raise health for every level you've had, through the floor. Points in the attributes your
> playstyle uses most (Strength and Agility for fighters, Intelligence and Willpower for casters, Agility and Speed for
> stealth) pay off in every fight.

## Next

docs.title: Appearance and Layered Gearing
docs.summary: Race, gender and face choices set your character's starting appearance; Layered Gearing displays worn armour online.
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Race determines the character's body morphology and race-specific art; gender and face are separate creation choices.
> - You select a face during character creation; the source provides ten face indices for each race and gender set.
> - The profile's Look choice switches between Skins and Layered Gearing (WIP).
> - Choose for the look you want: appearance does not replace your class, attributes or skills.

## Choices during creation

Character creation asks for race and gender before the face selection later in the wizard. The race table maps the human races to a human body, the three elf races to an elf body, and Khajiit and Argonian to their own morphologies. Your selected race also chooses its portrait and face set.

The face picker offers ten indices within each race-and-gender set. This controls the appearance chosen at creation; the source does not establish that changing a later interface skin changes your character's race or saved face choice.

For the gameplay effects of race, see Choosing a race. Race does not supply the chargen attribute roll: each attribute is your class's base value plus a random 0 to 10, and you then spend a separate bonus pool.

## Skins and Layered Gearing

The Look control on your player profile separates Skins from Layered Gearing (WIP). Skins lets you choose the on-foot and mounted appearance sets. Layered Gearing draws the on-foot body in the helmet, chest and leg armour it wears; you can choose a female or male body, or use your character's own body. The default is Layered Gearing with your own body. A rider has no layered gear art, so the mounted appearance remains its own choice.

This is visual presentation. It does not change what the character can equip or how armour protects them. The race table describes race morphology and race-specific creation art; the Layered Gearing choice is a separate profile appearance setting.

Your interface skin is a separate preference. You can change UI Overhaul through Overhauls without treating that as a new character-creation choice.

## Common mistakes

- Assuming race changes your attribute roll mixes appearance and race effects with class-based creation.
- Treating the face picker as a gameplay specialization adds a rule the chargen source does not define.
- Treating Layered Gearing as an armour rule: it presents worn pieces; your class and item rules decide what you can equip.

## Next

- Choosing a race
- Choosing a playstyle

docs.title: Choosing a playstyle
docs.summary: Compare warrior, mage, thief and hybrid playstyles, then place the skills and resources each uses into creation.
headings: Compare what each style asks of creation
Make your class tiers do useful work
Check the trade-offs before you commit
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Put frequently used skills in your class tiers so the raises normal play earns also count toward your character level.
> - A warrior needs dependable weapon skills and enough survival capacity to stay in a fight.
> - A mage needs the magic schools it will cast and a plan for spell points.
> - A thief needs the movement, stealth and access skills it expects to use; a hybrid must budget for both sides.

## Compare what each style asks of creation

These are planning lenses, not exclusive classes or a recommended build. The eighteen standard classes and the custom builder give different ways to cover the same needs. Online combat uses the port's active combat layer, so do not build around offline formula claims.

| Playstyle | Creation needs to consider | Trade-off to think through |
|---|---|---|
| Warrior | Place the weapon skill you expect to use, plus practical support such as Dodging, in a high class tier. Consider attributes and starting health that support staying engaged. | More room for combat skills means fewer high-tier slots for magic or social and utility skills. |
| Mage | Place the schools you plan to cast in high tiers. Check the class's spell-point basis and starting spell set before relying on a broad school list. | Spell points support spell use, but you still need a way to handle situations when a spell is unavailable or ineffective. |
| Thief | Prioritize the skills used for stealth, locks, movement and social access in the class tiers that match how often you will use them. | Skill breadth competes for the limited primary and major slots; a narrow focus leaves some situations to other tools. |
| Hybrid | Pick a main weapon or magic approach, then reserve high tiers for the second role's most-used skill rather than trying to cover every skill equally. | You gain flexibility but split class advancement focus and may need to manage more equipment or resources. |

## Make your class tiers do useful work

Your class has three primary, three major and six minor skills. Every skill improves with use, but only class skills move your character level: under the classic levelling every new online character uses, the level counts all three primaries, your two best majors and your best minor. A skill outside the class still rises; it just does not level you. Each tier also starts at a different value at creation, primaries highest and minors lowest, for stock and custom classes alike.

For magic, check whether a custom class places a school in primary or major: with at least one magic school there, it starts with the Spellsword's spell set, and with none it starts with no spells. A class's spell-point multiplier and your Intelligence set its base spell-point pool. For physical combat, choose a weapon family you are willing to keep using and consider the skill's class tier alongside the character's attributes.

## Check the trade-offs before you commit

Creation asks you to choose a race, gender, class, biography, name, face, attributes, skills and reflexes. A custom class also sets health per level, skill tiers and special advantages or disadvantages. Think about how the disadvantages will matter in ordinary play; a restriction on gear you expect to use is a recurring cost.

No archetype needs one fixed stat spread or class. Use Classes, Custom classes, and Attributes and skills to check the exact mechanics for the class you choose.

## Common mistakes

- Choosing skills for a theme alone can leave the abilities you use most in low tiers.
- Giving a hybrid every appealing skill can dilute its advancement focus.
- Assuming a mage's school list automatically provides every starting spell overlooks the class's starting-spell rules.
- Copying offline combat numbers into an online plan can misstate hit and damage formulas.
