docs.title: Beginner online builds
docs.summary: Three safe starting archetypes and the decisions that matter under online combat and levelling.
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Online play forces PCAAO's combat formulas: hit chance stays between 3% and 97%, and Strength adds damage at one point per ten past 50.
> - Each online level pays a fixed pool of five attribute points, with no roll, and maximum Health has a floor tied to Endurance.
> - Build around one damage skill and one defence plan, not a spread of six.
> - A custom class's forbidden materials and skill tiers cannot be undone, so check them before you confirm.
> - Masteries are permanent and you have two primary, two major and one minor slot; plan them before investing.

## What is different online

Online combat is not classic Daggerfall's formulas. The room forces PCAAO for everyone (onlineLane.js ONLINEROOMMODKEYS.pcaao), and PCAAO changes the parts a build leans on:

- To-hit is bounded. A roll lands between 3% and 97%, so no build becomes unhittable or unable to miss. Weapon skill, enemy armour and fatigue decide where in that band you sit.
- Strength adds flat damage. PCAAO's damage modifier is one point per ten Strength above 50, doubled for two-handed weapons. That makes Strength a real damage stat without making it the whole build.
- Low health is a bonus, not a plan. Adrenaline Rush gives +8 to hit (+12 improved) while you are below one sixth of maximum health. It rewards a losing fight; do not build around staying there.
- Armour reads in pieces. A blocking shield is checked first, then the struck body part's armour, then natural resistance, and blunt and edged attacks read different reduction rows. Wearing a full suit matters more than one heavy piece.
- Online levels are fixed. Online uses the classic leveling system only, and each level gives a fixed pool of attribute points (levelEven.js ONLINEBONUSPOOL) with a Health floor tied to Endurance. A low Health roll cannot leave you below that floor, so Endurance is never wasted. See Levelling online.

Two more systems shape the build from above:

- Firmament caps. One weapon-family damage channel is capped together at +30%, and the whole blow is capped at +50%. A build that feeds one channel reaches the cap; a build that spreads across three reaches none of them. See The Firmament.
- Threat grows. After character level 10 and Renown 15, foes gain health and damage, so a build is never finished at creation; gear and stars have to keep up. See The hero's threat.

## Three beginner-safe archetypes

These are starting shapes, not a ranking. Each has a clear resource loop and a clear weakness.

### The weapon-and-shield fighter

A weapon skill in your primary or major tier, the heaviest armour your class allows, and a shield. Its loop is Health and fatigue: you close, trade blows, block the telegraphed ones and rest. It teaches the combat system without a second resource bar.

- Safe because: every ready-made class can fight from level 1 (Classes), and gear upgrades improve it directly.
- Weakness: no ranged answer and no built-in heal unless you take Restoration, potions or a temple service. Archers and casters can kite it.
- Decisions that matter: which weapon family (one, not three), whether to raise Endurance early for the Health floor, and whether your class forbids the metal you want to wear.

### The destruction caster

Destruction in a primary or major tier, Willpower and Intelligence for spell points and casting, and a backup weapon for the moments magic runs dry. Its loop is magicka: range, burst, then recover.

- Safe because: range avoids the melee damage race, and Destruction is a straightforward damage skill.
- Weakness: magicka is a second resource to manage, and a silenced or drained caster is a common death. A caster needs a fallback attack and a way to restore spell points.
- Decisions that matter: one spell school rather than several, a weapon skill you will actually train as backup, and enough Endurance that a missed fight does not end the character.

### The stealth archer or thief

Archery, Stealth and Lockpicking, light armour and a short blade for when the fight closes. Its loop is positioning: hit from range or from stealth, avoid the fight, and use doors and distance.

- Safe because: you choose most fights, and Lockpicking and Stealth pay outside combat as well.
- Weakness: dungeons force close fights, and a missed opening shot leaves a lightly armoured character in melee. It rewards patience more than reflexes.
- Decisions that matter: Archery as the damage channel, one melee fallback, and whether to spend a major tier on Stealth or Lockpicking.

## Decision rules

1. Pick a damage skill your class trains from level 1. Every ready-made class was revised online so it can fight from the first level; a custom class should keep at least one weapon or Destruction skill in a primary or major slot.
2. Choose one defence and commit. Armour and a shield, range and avoidance, or a heal source — a little of each is worse than one done properly.
3. Decide your healing before level 5. Restoration, Alchemy and potions, or paid temple services. A build with no heal spends its gold on cures instead.
4. Read the fatigue cost of your plan. Techniques and heavy swings cost fatigue, and an exhausted character cannot land blows; a build that needs two techniques back to back needs the fatigue to pay for them.
5. Check custom-class restrictions first. A forbidden weapon, armour type or material can rule out the loot you will actually find, and there is no general undo. See Choices that are hard to undo.
6. Plan the mastery slots. You can master two primary, two major and one minor skill, permanently. A build that needs three primary masteries does not fit.
7. Do not rely on Adrenaline Rush. It is a bonus below one sixth Health; a build that needs it is a build that is dying.

> [!warning] Build-agnostic means trade-offs
> No archetype is better in every fight. A fighter is easier to start, a caster controls range, and a stealth character chooses its fights. Pick the loop you enjoy repeating, then let gear and stars solve its weakness.

## Common mistakes

- Spreading damage across weapon families. The Firmament caps one channel, so a second family adds little until the first is full.
- Taking a custom-class disadvantage for the points and meeting it every fight. A forbidden material is not a difficulty setting; it is a loot filter.
- Dumping every point into one attribute. Attributes feed different formulas; check Attributes and skills before committing the pool.
- Ignoring the Health floor. Endurance raises the floor retroactively, so early Endurance is not wasted even if your Health roll was good.
- Planning past the online caps. The build stops at the channel caps, not at the last star in the tree.

## Next

- Build plans
- Choosing a playstyle

docs.title: Choices that are hard to undo
docs.summary: Separate decisions saved at creation from later systems that can change a limited part of your character.
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Review your name, face, attributes, skills and reflexes on the creation summary before entering the world; check race, class and biography on their own screens.
> - A custom class's skill tiers, health per level and restrictions shape how that character advances and equips gear.
> - A later, paid skill swap can change one class skill at a time, but nothing makes every creation decision freely editable.
> - If a choice is central to how you want to play, check the linked creation page before confirming.

## Review the saved character

The creation wizard takes you through race, gender, class, biography, name, face, attributes, skills and reflexes, then shows a summary before it finishes. The summary shows your name, face, attributes, skills and reflexes, and you can still adjust them there; the Enhanced review also names your race and class. Your biography answers are not shown on it, so check them as you answer.

Race determines morphology and racial effects; class supplies the character's career structure and class skills; biography answers can modify starting details. These are different inputs, so changing a later setting or interface skin should not be mistaken for changing the saved creation choice.

## Choices with lasting consequences

For a custom class, review the primary, major and minor tiers, health per level, attribute allocation, and every advantage and disadvantage. Those choices set its advancement difficulty and the constraints it carries into play. A forbidden weapon, armour type or material can rule out equipment you later find.

For any class, put the skills you expect to use into tiers that reflect your play. Your early skill choices affect starting values and advancement. Later, a paid skill swap can trade one class skill you have not mastered for a skill outside your class, in the same tier; it sits beside Masteries and specialisations.

The source identifies the wizard's final summary and later skill-swap system, but it does not establish a general undo button for race, biography, face or the rest of the original creation record. Treat those as decisions to verify before confirming rather than assuming they can be reset later.

## Before you confirm

1. Read the summary from top to bottom.
2. Check the class skill tiers against the way you expect to play.
3. Recheck any custom-class disadvantage that restricts equipment or spell use.
4. Confirm the name, attributes, face and reflex setting you intended, and that the race and class shown are the ones you chose.

## Common mistakes

- Treating all creation choices as a single “build” obscures which screen supplies each part of the character.
- Assuming a later skill swap can change race or the whole class overlooks its narrower scope.
- Taking a disadvantage for its difficulty points without accounting for its actual gameplay cost can create a restriction you notice often.

## Next

docs.title: Your first minutes in Privateer's Hold
docs.summary: Read the opening guidance, check your journal, and explore the cave toward its exit.
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Start in Privateer's Hold and follow the welcome guidance: take what you need, find the exit, and head toward town.
> - The short tutorial tour introduces movement, interacting, the bars and compass, and the menu.
> - Press L to open the journal on active quests or N to open its notebook.
> - Explore at your own pace; the source does not define the Hold's room layout or a fixed route through it.

## Begin in the Hold

Your new character starts inside Privateer's Hold. The welcome tutorial introduces the immediate task: look through your
pack, find the way out of the cave, and make for the nearest town. It is guidance for your first minutes, not a
room-by-room map.

The tutorial tour has five short subjects: Welcome, Moving Around, Using Things, The Bars and the Compass, and The Menu
and Saving. Tutorial pages can be reread from the menu. Their read state belongs to your device, so a second character
does not necessarily see pages you already read.

## Check your journal

Press L to open the journal to active quests. Press N to open the same window to your notebook. The journal's
other views include finished quests and messages. Both keys work underground.

## Take a measured first look

Use the controls to move, look around and ready your weapon. This guide does not
give a fixed room-by-room route or promise a particular item in a specific room.

## Common mistakes

- Leaving without checking the journal. It gives you a place to review active objectives and notes.
- Expecting to return to the public Hold later. Online, leaving closes the ordinary route back in. Finish what you
  want to do here before exiting.

## Next

- Moving through the Hold
- Loot and inventory

- Privateer's Hold walkthrough

docs.title: Privateer's Hold walkthrough
docs.summary: A textual route from the Hold's start to its exit and the road to Gothway Garden, with what to take.
headings: What the game fixes, and what it does not
What to take, and what to leave
Outside: the camp and the monument
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Your new character starts inside Privateer's Hold; the game's own welcome says to take what you need, find the way out and make for the nearest town.
> - The source does not define the Hold's room layout, its interior foes or its loot. This page is a procedure and a checklist, not a room-by-room map.
> - The way out is its exit door; activating it lands you outside on the entrance landing, facing out, beside the LeFay Monument.
> - Online, the Hold's public room is a one-way door: once you leave, it refuses re-entry. Finish what you want inside first.
> - Dying inside respawns you at the Hold's start marker, so a first death does not skip the dungeon.

## What the game fixes, and what it does not

The code fixes the start: a classic new game with Start In Dungeon on enters the Hold on the shipped start cell. It fixes two automatic quests, the five-page welcome tour, the exit-door behaviour, the respawn point and the one-way rule. It does not contain the Hold's interior layout, its foe placements, its traps or its loot; those come from the game's dungeon data, and no file in the source tree states them. Any page that draws you a fixed route is describing something the source does not hold.

So this walkthrough teaches the procedure the engine guarantees: how to leave, what the game expects you to do first, how to read the dungeon without a map, and what to check before stepping out.

## Before you move

1. Read the welcome. The tour's five pages are Welcome, Moving Around, Using Things, The Bars and the Compass, and The Menu and Saving. You can reread them from the menu.
2. Open the journal. L opens the LogBook on Active Quests; N opens the same window on Notebook. Both work underground.
3. Check the pack. You start with your class's starting gear and supplies. Equip the weapon and armour you intend to use; open the inventory with I/F5/F6 as your skin shows.
4. Set the controls you need. Ready/sheathe weapon (Z), swing (right mouse by default), and the Weapon Technique key (the mouse's back side button) if you have a technique line.
5. Read the bars. Health, fatigue and magicka are in the HUD; the compass shows direction. You do not need to memorise the dungeon to leave it.
6. Set the map key in mind. M opens the map at your current place; in a dungeon that is the automap, which fills in as you explore.

## The route, as a procedure

1. Start marker. You begin at the dungeon's start/enter marker. Online, this is also where a death inside the Hold returns you.
2. Sweep the first area. Check containers, take what is light and useful, and test your weapon on the first foe you can handle. You do not need to clear the dungeon.
3. Use the automap, not memory. Press M as you go. The dungeon automap draws the parts you have explored; a corridor you have not walked is not on it yet. Use walls, doors and junctions as breadcrumbs: at each junction, mark the way you came by the door or stair you used.
4. Every door is interactable. E interacts; a locked door can be picked in Steal mode (hold Left Alt, choose Steal, activate the door). No lockpick item is needed. The chance is your Lockpicking skill against the lock's value, clamped 5–95; a failed attempt is spent until your Lockpicking changes. A magically held lock (value 20 or more) cannot be picked.
5. Watch for action traps. Dungeon action objects can damage you, drain magicka, cast a spell or set a global flag when triggered. There is no universal “safe” rule beyond watching what you step on and opening what you must. The source does not place a specific trap set in the Hold.
6. Find the exit door. Activating the exit runs the transition to the exterior. If a small cart is in your pack and the Dungeon Exit Wagon Prompt setting is on, the door asks before leaving.
7. You step out facing outward. The landing puts you at the entrance door you came in by, on its outside face, facing away from the door. The LeFay Monument stands beside that way out.
8. Take the road to town. Gothway Garden is the first town a new character walks into out of the Hold; the road from the Hold enters at the town's north side. The source does not state the walking distance, so follow the road and the map rather than a step count.

## What to take, and what to leave

Take what your class can use, weight permitting: the weapon you are skilled with, the armour you are allowed to wear, any potions and cures you start with, and a light source if you have one. Leave heavy spare weapons you cannot use; a first character has no bank and no cart on the way out.

The source does not guarantee a particular item in a particular room, so do not wait for a specific drop before leaving. If you find loot you cannot identify, carry it out; Identify is available in town.

> [!warning] The one-way door
> Online, once you are outside, the Hold's public room refuses re-entry with its own message. An instanced copy of the Hold can be entered any time, but the first dungeon's story door is a one-time passage. Finish quest objectives and take what you want before you activate the exit.

## Death inside the Hold

Online, a death inside Privateer's Hold respawns you at the Hold's start marker, not outside and not in a town. The ordinary online death cost still applies: you rise with half your maximum health and lose a tenth of the gold you carry (banked gold and letters of credit are untouched). Dying does not end the run.

That is deliberate: the Hold is where you learn to fight, and a death there cannot skip the tutorial. Elsewhere, a death returns you to the nearest temple, town or graveyard, or just outside the dungeon's door.

## Outside: the camp and the monument

The Hold's exterior carries the World of Daggerfall camp online. It can place thieves, assassins and rogues, each standing only on a high roll of the source's 21–30 band, so the ground outside is not always empty. The LeFay Monument stands beside the exit landing; interacting with it offers the flowers and the inscription rows. From there, follow the road to Gothway Garden's north entrance, where the town's bounty boards stand.

## Common mistakes

- Waiting for a fixed route. The source has no interior layout; use the automap and the exit door.
- Trying to come back. The online public Hold refuses re-entry after you leave.
- Fighting everything. You only need the exit; a full clear is optional.
- Ignoring a failed lock. It is spent until your skill changes; train or move on.
- Leaving with an unfinished quest. Check the journal before the exit.

## Next

- Moving through the Hold
- Leaving the Hold

docs.title: Moving through the Hold
docs.summary: Walk, turn, look, jump, crouch, and run while watching the space around you.
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Use W/A/S/D to move and the left/right arrows to turn by default.
> - Space jumps; C crouches and sneaks; Left Shift runs.
> - Climbing and swimming spend fatigue. Online, sheathe a non-melee weapon before climbing.
> - Home centres your view if you have looked away from level.
> - Rebind any control in Settings → Controls → Key bindings.

## Move and look

The default keyboard controls let you move in four directions with W/A/S/D and turn with the left and right arrow keys.
Use Insert and Delete to look up and down. Press Home to centre the view.

## Change your pace

Press Left Shift while moving to run. Press C to crouch or sneak. Space jumps. Auto-run is bound to the
middle mouse button by default.

These are defaults, not requirements. Change them under Settings → Controls → Key bindings. The source has
separate primary and secondary bindings, so you can set a gamepad action alongside a keyboard or mouse one.

## Jump, climb and swim

Jump with Space. Climbing and swimming use fatigue, so leave some in reserve if you expect to climb or cross water.
Swimming fatigue depends on the Swimming roll.

Online, the Roleplay & Realism rule prevents you from climbing with a drawn weapon other than bare hands. Sheathe a
bow or other weapon before you mantle or clamber over an obstacle. A vault is a leap, so the rule does not block it.

## Explore carefully

Move through doorways and around obstacles with the view centred on where you intend to go. The Hold is a dungeon, so
keep enough room to turn toward sounds or threats before pressing the weapon swing control. For combat movement, see
Fighting.

docs.title: Fighting
docs.summary: Aim your swings, read enemy tells, and move out of marked attacks before they land.
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - A melee attack needs a foe within 2.5 m, in view, with a clear line of sight.
> - Swing direction trades accuracy for damage: an overhead strike hits harder but is less likely to connect.
> - When an enemy marks an attack on the ground, step outside the marked area before it lands.
> - Wear a shield in your off hand to give online combat a chance to block a blow.

## Make a melee attack

Ready your weapon with Z, then swing with right click. A blow can reach a foe whose centre is within 2.5 m of
your eye, provided it is in view and there is a clear line of sight.

### Swing direction

Direction changes the swing's hit and damage modifiers:

| Swing | Damage | To hit |
|---|---|---|
| Down | +4 | −10 |
| Down-left | +2 | −5 |
| Down-right | −2 | +5 |
| Left or right | 0 | 0 |
| Up | −4 | +10 |

How you choose the direction depends on your swing mode (Settings, Controls):

- Click or Hold (the default): a click swings, and holding the button keeps swinging. Each swing goes in a
  random direction from six (up-right, left, right, down-left, down, down-right). You don't choose.
- Click: a swing on each press, also in a random direction.
- Gesture: hold the attack button and drag the mouse; the direction you drag is the swing you get. Choose this if
  you want to pick Down for damage or Up for accuracy.

### Will it land?

Every swing rolls to hit. Online, the Physical Combat and Armor Overhaul works out the chance from your skill with
the weapon, your Agility, Speed and Luck against the target's, the target's armour where the blow falls, and half the
target's Dodging skill. The result is always between 3% and 97%. See
Attributes and skills.

## Read the enemy

Some stronger enemies telegraph attacks: a ground shape shows where the blow will land, and a glint marks the attacker
as it winds up. Move out of the shape before impact to avoid that telegraphed blow. A missed telegraphed attack leaves
the enemy Open for a short time; attacks against it deal 30% more damage during that window.

A perfect dodge keeps it open longer: stay inside the marked shape until the last quarter of a second, then be
outside it when the blow lands. The Open window is then one and a half times as long, and you hear a bright ring.

You can also interrupt a wind-up by striking the enemy. Hits fill its poise; a full poise meter staggers it. Heavy
weapons such as blunt arms contribute more poise than short blades. Keep moving while an enemy winds up, then use the
opening it leaves.

## Armour and shields

Against you, online armour reduces damage after an attack hits; it does not make the attacker miss. A held shield can also block: the
online combat core rolls a block on an incoming blow and, when the shield provides better protection than the armour
under it, applies the shield's reduction instead.

There is no separate active block action in the input list. The shield must be equipped and held. Press H to switch
which hand you use.

> [!online] Online rule
> The Physical Combat and Armor Overhaul runs online. Its armour reduction and shield block rules are the rules this
> page describes.

## Common mistakes

- Standing in a marked attack. Leaving the telegraphed shape before impact is what makes that attack miss.
- Treating a shield as an extra armour layer in every case. Its online block only counts when it protects better
  than the armour beneath it.
- Holding still to attack. Movement helps you leave a marked attack and maintain the distance and view needed for a
  melee hit.

## Next

- Weapon techniques
- Archery and magic

make-a-melee-attack.title: Make a melee attack
make-a-melee-attack.excerpt: Ready your weapon with Z, then swing with right click. A blow can reach a foe whose centre is within 2.5 m of your eye, provided it is in view and there is a clear line of sight.

swing-direction.title: Swing direction
swing-direction.excerpt: Direction changes the swing's hit and damage modifiers:

will-it-land.title: Will it land?
will-it-land.excerpt: Every swing rolls to hit. Online, the Physical Combat and Armor Overhaul works out the chance from your skill with the weapon, your Agility, Speed and Luck against the target's, the target's armour where the blow falls, and half the target's Dodging skill. The result is always between 3% and 97%. See Attributes and skills.

read-the-enemy.title: Read the enemy
read-the-enemy.excerpt: Some stronger enemies telegraph attacks: a ground shape shows where the blow will land, and a glint marks the attacker as it winds up. Move out of the shape before impact to avoid that telegraphed blow. A missed telegraphed attack leaves the enemy Open for a short time; attacks against it deal 30% more damage during that window.

armour-and-shields.title: Armour and shields
armour-and-shields.excerpt: Against you, online armour reduces damage after an attack hits; it does not make the attacker miss. A held shield can also block: the online combat core rolls a block on an incoming blow and, when the shield provides better protection than the armour under it, applies the shield's reduction instead.

docs.title: Combat maths
docs.summary: The online hit, damage and armour formulas behind one swing, with a checklist for why blows miss.
headings: Why am I missing: a 60-second checklist
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Online, the room forces PCAAO on, so the hit roll, damage, body parts and armour are PCAAO's, not the classic formulas.
> - A hit starts at ceil(weapon skill × 1.5); the attacker's Dodging target subtracts half its skill, and the roll is clamped to 3–97.
> - Armour does not make blows miss: it reduces the damage of a blow that lands, by a row chosen from the armour's material and the blow's kind.
> - The target's Dodging, your material and your Strength move the numbers; direction, Expertise and racial bonuses apply to player attackers only.
> - Telegraphed blows are positional: step out of the shape, then punish the Open foe for +30% damage.

## The maths that runs online

Read this first. ONLINEROOMMODKEYS forces PCAAO on for every player in the room, and PCAAO's pcaaoAttackDamage is registered over the classic calculateAttackDamage. Everything below is the online rule; where the classic formulas.js core still differs, the difference is named. Enhanced AI is a forced online preference, so telegraphed blows are always on.

## The hit roll

| Step | What it does |
|---|---|
| Base | ceil(weapon skill × 1.5) for every attacker, player or foe (classic used the skill alone). |
| Material | The weapon's material modifier × 2 + 2: +0 to +14 across the ladder, not the classic × 10. |
| Target Dodging | Subtract trunc(Dodging / 2) (classic subtracted / 4). |
| Stat difference | trunc((your Luck − target Luck)/10) + trunc((Agility difference)/4) + trunc((Speed difference)/8) − roundhalfeven((target Luck − 50)/10). |
| Adjustments | A player target subtracts its biography avoid-hit modifier; a monster target adds +50 and then every target takes −50 (a monster nets zero). |
| Clamp and roll | The total is clamped to 3–97, then a d100 is rolled under it. |

A player attacker adds four more terms; a foe gets none of them: the swing's direction modifier, Expertise, the racial weapon bonus, and the backstab chance. That is why a foe's skill is its whole accuracy while yours is not.

Two skills then bend the roll. Critical Strike: luck term floor((Luck − 50)/25); a d100 at or under trunc(Critical Strike / (4 − luck term)) adds trunc(Critical Strike / 4) to hit and multiplies the blow's damage by 1 + trunc(Critical Strike / 5) × 0.05. Adrenaline Rush (career ability): under trunc(max Health / 6), +8 to hit, or +12 with Improved Adrenaline Rush; a rushing target subtracts the same.

## Body part, armour and shields

A landed blow rolls a body part from PCAAO's 20-entry table: Head 1/20, Right Arm 3, Left Arm 3, Chest 4, Hands 3, Legs 4, Feet 2.

Armour's part in the hit roll is small. A player target reads 100 − enchant armour modifier − armour points on the struck part; a class-enemy target reads a flat 60; a monster keeps its own per-part armour value. Armour's real work happens after the hit:

damage taken = roundhalfeven(damage × (min(base × condition factor, cap) − natural resistance))

The [base, cap] row is chosen by the struck piece's material index (1–10) and the blow kind: unarmed, blunt or edged. Natural resistance is (Endurance − 50) × 0.002 + (Strength − 50) × 0.001 + (Willpower − 50) × 0.001. On a bare part it is the whole reduction: damage × (1 − natural resistance).

Condition matters. A weapon at 41–60% condition deals ×0.85 (blunt ×0.9); at 6–15% it deals ×0.45 (blunt ×0.65); at 5% or under ×0.25 (blunt ×0.5). Worn armour worsens its reduction factor on the same ladder (×1.1 to ×1.5).

Shields are a defender-side block roll on every blow that lands, not a button. Base chance by kind, with a strong spot (a covered part) and a weak spot: Buckler 30/20, Round 35/10, Kite 45/5, Tower 55/−5, anything else in the hand 40/0, plus stat terms. A block counts only if the shield's average reduction beats the armour under it; then the blow runs through the shield's own, stronger row. The Shield Widget only draws the shield.

## Damage

Online damage spans come from Roleplay & Realism's weaponBalance, not the classic tables: Longsword 2–15, Claymore 2–19, Dai-Katana 1–18, Warhammer 4–18, Shortsword 2–8. Archery keeps the classic spans: Short Bow 4–16, Long Bow 4–18. Bare hands stay skill-based: min floor(HandToHand / 10) + 1, max floor(HandToHand / 5) + 1.

On top of the span:

- Strength: floor((Strength − 50) / 10) added once, doubled for a two-handed weapon that is not a bow (classic used / 5).
- Material shortfall: a weapon under the metal a foe needs is multiplied by 1 − min(shortfall × 0.2, 0.9) — ×0.8, 0.6, 0.4, 0.2, then 0.1 — and the game says when a blow falls to 45% or less. The zero-damage refusal is the module-off path.
- Silver: doubles against the Skeletal Warrior and six careers (Werewolf, Ghost, Wraith, Vampire, Mummy, Wereboar); a non-edged weapon is halved against the Skeletal Warrior.
- Expertise and race add stat-based damage terms, for player attackers only.

Fatigue is part of the maths. A melee swing spends 8 fatigue when it reaches its hit frame, hit or miss. Running out while enemies are near costs 10% of your health and warns you; a Restore Fatigue potion is the in-fight answer.

## Swing pace

A melee strike is five frames and damage lands on frame two. The frame time is SWINGBASEFRAME × tempo × handling: base ≈0.199 s at Speed 50, tempo ×1.4 at Speed 0 and ×0.6 at Speed 100, handling 0.9 for daggers/bare hands, 1.0 long blades, up to 1.06 for a warhammer, ×1.06 for two-handed, ×0.9 for anything swinging with Short Blade.

Online, RRI's weaponBalance replaces the heft term for a held weapon: the Speed used is live Speed − min(live Speed, 98) × ((150 − Strength)% × base weight × 3.4) / 90, truncated. Heavier weapon, weaker arm, slower swing. Bare hands read live Speed plainly.

## Tells, Open and poise

Only tier foes telegraph: level 10 or higher, an elite, a champion or a revenant, and only kinds with shapes (class casters throw none). A missed shape leaves the foe Open: +30% damage taken for its shape's window (lunge 1.0 s, sweep 0.8, slam 1.2, ring 1.0, charge 1.4, leap 1.2), and a perfect dodge — inside the shape 0.25 s before landing, outside at the landing — lengthens that window 1.5×.

Hits during a wind-up fill poise instead of shoving. At full poise the wind-up breaks: the foe is helpless for 0.8–1.4 s by weight class and takes +25% damage, then cannot be staggered again for 3 s. Iron blows have no poise meter and cannot be broken.

## Why am I missing: a 60-second checklist

1. Range and line: is the foe's centre within 2.5 m of your eye, in view, with a clear line?
2. Material: is your weapon under the foe's required metal? Damage drops; against some foes it is the whole problem.
3. Dodging: a dodging target takes half its skill off your chance.
4. Body part: are your blows landing on a heavily armoured part?
5. Material to-hit: a low-metal weapon is missing accuracy as well as damage.
6. Fatigue: are you exhausted? The health loss and the miss look alike in a crowd.
7. Swing mode: is the attack bound, and is Click-or-Hold or Gesture the mode you think?
8. The foe: level 10+, elite or champion means tells and poise; if you are standing in the shape, you are choosing to be hit.

## Common mistakes

- Expecting armour to make you hard to hit. It reduces damage after the hit; Dodging moves the hit roll.
- Reading classic tables. Skill, material, Strength and Dodging all run on PCAAO's versions online.
- Ignoring condition. A worn weapon loses up to three quarters of its damage.
- Treating the shield as passive armour. It rolls a block; if it loses the comparison with your armour, it does nothing.
- Standing in the shape to trade. Step out, then hit the Open foe.

## Next

- Fighting
- Weapon techniques

docs.title: Weapon techniques
docs.summary: Some weapon and gauntlet lines grant a special attack that uses its own key, fatigue cost, cooldown, and damage multiplier.
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - A technique is a line that can appear on a weapon; a bare-handed technique uses your worn gauntlets.
> - Press the Weapon Technique key to use it. The default mouse binding is Mouse3, the back side button.
> - Techniques cost fatigue and have a cooldown.
> - Their damage modifies the normal attack formula; a technique can still miss.

## What a technique does

A weapon technique is a special attack attached to a technique line on eligible gear. The weapon in your hand provides
the technique; for bare-handed combat, worn gauntlets provide it. The line's printed value strengthens that technique's
own multiplier, which then modifies the normal weapon damage formula. It is not guaranteed damage: the attack still
uses its normal hit resolution.

Examples include Volley for bows, Whirlwind for long blades, and Haymaker for gauntlets. Other techniques
can lunge, leap, strike several nearby enemies or send a shot through a line of foes. Read the item's technique line
for the move it actually grants.

## Use the technique key

Press the Weapon Technique binding to activate the technique on the equipped weapon. Some techniques ask you to
aim before release; follow the targeting prompt on screen. The default keyboard/mouse action is bound to Mouse3,
the mouse's back side button; a touch layout provides a hold button labelled Tech.

Each technique has its own fatigue cost and cooldown. If you cannot use it, check that you have the required weapon or
gauntlets equipped, enough fatigue, and that its cooldown has ended.

## Find technique lines

Technique lines can be rolled on weapons and gauntlets by the loot system. Their chance and strength depend on the
item's rarity tier. You do not need to memorize every move now; compare a line's effect with how you prefer to fight.

## Next

- Archery and magic
- Loot and inventory

docs.title: Guns and paired weapons
docs.summary: Understand the Dwarven Pistolet, its ammunition, paired guns and the trade-off of carrying a blade beside one.
headings: Carry one gun or a pair
Pair a blade with a Pistolet
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - The Dwarven Pistolet is a one-handed weapon using Archery.
> - Its base damage is 4–15 and its template value is 260 gold.
> - Both guns consume Dwemer Pellets, not arrows.
> - You can pair two Pistolets or carry one beside a one-handed melee weapon.
> - Neither gun drops in the checked version; ammunition still drops and appears in shops.

## Recognize what you have found

You can encounter Dwemer Pellets before you own a gun. They are ammunition for the Dwarven Pistolet and the Dwarven Thunderlock. A pellet stack is not a broken weapon, a crafting requirement for assembling a pistol, or evidence that a gun must be nearby.

The Pistolet is the one-handed firearm. Its base damage span is 4–15, and its template value is 260 gold. That value is the item's underlying price field; it is not a promise that a shop or another player will sell one to you for that amount. Your actual combat results depend on the weapon and the wider combat rules, rather than the base span alone.

You use Archery when firing it. Equipping a gun does not turn its shots into melee attacks because the weapon fits in one hand. If you are learning ranged combat, read Archery and magic for the surrounding skill and resource concepts, while remembering that a gun fires by trigger rather than a bow's draw-and-release action.

## Carry one gun or a pair

You can equip a Pistolet in either hand. With a second Pistolet equipped, you have a gun pair. Each pistol has its own firing and reload state. When the next hand cannot fire because it is reloading, the attack can fall to the loaded pistol.

Use H to choose the lead hand. The pair still uses the ordinary attack control; you do not need a separate trigger button for each pistol. Keep enough ammunition for the shots you intend to make. Sharing an ammunition type means both guns draw on your pellets, rather than giving each hand an independent supply of free shots.

The Thunderlock is a different weapon. Do not treat every firearm as eligible for the Pistolet's pair rules: the code specifically admits Pistolets as the guns of a pair. Seeing a player carry two pistols does not mean you can equip two Thunderlocks in the same way.

## Pair a blade with a Pistolet

Equip an eligible one-handed melee weapon beside the Pistolet to make a mixed pair. Your hands take turns: a blade swing and a gunshot do not land as simultaneous actions from the same attack press. While the gun reloads, an attack that would use it falls to the blade. If you run out of pellets, the blade can still fight.

The cost is reload time. A lone Pistolet or a gun pair uses a 1.4-second reload. Beside a blade, the Pistolet reloads at twice that duration: 2.8 seconds. The source's MIXED.RELOAD = 2 is a multiplier, not a two-second timer. This gives you something to do during the reload, with a longer wait between available shots.

Your technique belongs to the lead weapon and does not automatically fall back to the blade. A technique attempted with a reloading lead gun can be refused. Check your lead hand before using Weapon techniques, and use Fighting for the underlying melee decisions.

## Understand current availability

The GUNS-UNFOUND change dated 23 October 2026 stops both guns from dropping. Existing owners retain their weapons and can still use them. Older descriptions of finding a gun describe an earlier version; they are not a route for a new character in this snapshot.

The former gun find now produces pellets alone. Weapon-selling shops also stock pellets, while their shelves do not sell the guns. You may therefore first meet this system through ammunition in loot, ammunition on a shop counter, or a firearm another player already owns. The checked sources do not set a new-player gun acquisition quest or a guaranteed replacement source.

## Common mistakes

- Farming a former gun drop: the current find produces ammunition without either weapon.
- Buying arrows for a firearm: both guns require Dwemer Pellets.
- Expecting a mixed pair to double your attacks: its hands take turns and the gun reloads more slowly.

## Next

- Weapon techniques
- Loot rarity

docs.title: Archery and magic
docs.summary: Draw a bow, lead your shots with movement, and manage spell points when casting.
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Bows use the Archery skill, and arrows travel as projectiles.
> - Draw time affects a bow shot: a quick release is less accurate and under-drawn shots deal less damage.
> - A normal spell cast costs at least 5 spell points; some effects can make a cast free.
> - A cast briefly occupies your hands, so leave room to move or choose a safe moment.

## Use a bow

Equip a bow and arrows, then draw and release to fire. A bow uses the Archery skill. Its arrow travels through the
space between you and the target, so moving out of an enemy archer's line can avoid a shot.

Give the shot time to draw. A release before 0.2 seconds takes a penalty to hit; a draw that is too short also
reduces damage. Holding the draw too long lowers damage rather than improving it. You can recover some arrows from
foes or from where a shot struck the environment.

## Cast a spell

Casting uses spell points. The cost depends on the spell's effects, target and your skill in its school, with a floor of
5 points. Some effects can make a cast free. If your spell points are low, use a less costly spell or rest when it is
safe.

Starting a cast occupies your hands briefly, and a short recovery period follows. Avoid beginning a cast when an enemy
is already in striking range; move or create space first.

## Next

- Loot and inventory
- Health, fatigue and rest

- Spellmaking maths

docs.title: Bestiary
docs.summary: The enemy families and tiers, what each resists or requires, how they fight, and what they pay.
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - A foe is minted from its row: a monster keeps its row's level and health, while a class enemy (bandit, knight, sorcerer) is built at your level.
> - Families matter: Animal, Undead, Daedra, Golem, Water, Daylight, Darkness, Human and None set innate damage reduction and behaviour.
> - Some monsters need a metal: silver for werewolves and many undead, dwarven for harpies, mithril for gargoyles, daedra and liches. Online a shortfall cuts damage rather than refusing it.
> - Online, Meaner Monsters and Enemy Expansion are both forced on; beside Enemy Expansion, MUDEX stands in for Meaner Monsters, so the shipped rows below are guides, not guaranteed online stat blocks.
> - Elite, champion and revenant promotions layer on top of the row: more health, better loot and, for revenants, a return.

## How a foe is built

The game's base table holds a row per classic monster id: a level, a health range, an armour value, up to three damage pairs, a minimum metal to hit, a soul point value, a loot table key and a behaviour/affinity pair. enemyLevelOf reads a monster's level from that row; a class enemy is handed the player's level instead, so a bandit or knight you meet is built for you while a rat is still a level-1 rat.

Online, the host owns the foe. The room forces Meaner Monsters and Daggerfall Enemy Expansion on and holds both whole at their defaults. With Enemy Expansion loaded, MUDEX — Meaner Monsters' author's form of it for a game with the Expansion — stands in for Meaner Monsters; Meaner Monsters' own rows and PCAAO's edit of them stand aside. Enemy Expansion also changes which types spawn. What you meet online is therefore the host's Enemy Expansion/MUDEX foe, not the base row below.

## Families and behaviour

| Affinity | Examples | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Animal | Rat, Giant Bat, Bear, Sabretooth, Spider, Giant Scorpion | Fight with natural attacks; usually no metal requirement. |
| Undead | Skeletal Warrior, Zombie, Ghost, Mummy, Wraith, Lich, Ancient Lich | Will not flee from morale in the ordinary sense; several need silver or better. |
| Daedra | Frost/Fire Daedra, Daedroth, Daedra Seducer, Daedra Lord | Strongest family tier; mithril requirement common. |
| Golem | Atronachs (fire, iron, flesh, ice) | Atronach rows share a template; resistances are kind-specific. |
| Water | Slaughterfish, Dreugh, Lamia | Aquatic behaviour; mostly met in water. |
| Daylight / Darkness | Spriggan, Centaur, Nymph, Orc, Vampire | The row's affinity, not a rule that they appear only then. |
| Human | Class enemies and the watch | Built at your level; may carry weapons and shields. |
| None | Horse | Not a normal enemy row. |

Behaviour drives movement: General, Flying, Aquatic, Spectral and Guard. Flying and spectral foes ignore some terrain paths that grounded ones must walk; aquatic foes only make sense in water.

## A tier sample

These are base-table rows, before Meaner Monsters/Enemy Expansion and before elite or champion promotion. Level and health are the clearest measure of a tier; damage is the row's first pair.

| Foe | Level | Health | Damage (first pair) | Metal needed |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Rat | 1 | 9–16 | 1–4 | — |
| Giant Bat | 3 | 12–26 | 2–12 | — |
| Grizzly Bear | 4 | 13–34 | 1–8 | — |
| Orc | 5 | 13–34 | 1–6 | — |
| Werewolf | 6 | 17–66 | 1–10 | Silver |
| Skeletal Warrior | 9 | 17–66 | 5–15 | — |
| Giant | 10 | 18–74 | 10–30 | — |
| Zombie | 10 | 52–66 | 15–50 | — |
| Ghost | 11 | 17–66 | 10–35 | Silver |
| Harpy | 8 | 16–85 | 5–15 | Dwarven |
| Giant Scorpion | 12 | 18–74 | 15–25 | — |
| Gargoyle | 14 | 19–82 | 10–15 | Mithril |
| Wraith | 15 | 30–90 | 20–45 | Silver |
| Dragonling | 16 | 14–42 | 5–15 | — |
| Orc Warlord | 16 | 20–90 | 5–50 | — |
| Frost Daedra | 17 | 25–130 | 50–100 | Mithril |
| Vampire | 19 | 28–154 | 20–50 | Silver |
| Daedra Lord | 20 | 35–210 | 15–50 | Mithril |
| Lich | 20 | 30–170 | 70–100 | Mithril |
| Ancient Lich | 21 | 30–170 | 70–100 | Mithril |

The table is a guide to order, not an online guarantee: a promoted elite or champion adds more, and the online room's rows are the mods'.

## What they resist

Metal requirements. The base row's minMetalToHit is a material index: silver (2) for the Werewolf, Wereboar, Nymph, Ghost, Mummy and Vampire; dwarven (4) for the Harpy; mithril (5) for the Gargoyle, the daedra, the liches and the Ancient Vampire. Online, "soft" material requirements multiply damage by 1 − min(shortfall × 0.2, 0.9) — a one-step shortfall is ×0.8, five or more ×0.1 — and the game tells you when a blow falls to 45% or less. The classic zero-damage refusal only runs with the module off.

Silver and edges. Silver doubles damage against the Skeletal Warrior and the six careers Werewolf, Ghost, Wraith, Vampire, Mummy and Wereboar. A non-edged weapon is halved against the Skeletal Warrior.

Innate reduction. A monster with nothing worn on the struck part reduces by its group's multiplier instead of natural resistance. Most are 1.0; exceptions include the Skeletal Warrior 0.8, Gargoyle blunt 1.21 and other 0.71, Spriggan blunt 0.66 and other 1.26, Ice Atronach blunt 1.4 and Iron Atronach blunt 0.6, and a few daedra careers at 0.84–1.04.

Poison and disease. The source routes poison through a monster's hit; the exact immunity set is per career and per spell, so check the effect's own saving throw rather than assuming a family is immune.

## How they fight

- Beasts telegraph a lunge. Brutes telegraph slam and sweep. Blades (humanoid weapon users) telegraph sweep and lunge. Class casters throw no telegraphed blow.
- An archer shoots from its ranged band on a 1/32 chance per classic tick; an aimed shot is faster and stronger.
- A caster's CastSpell action runs on a long cooldown; silence and magic resistance matter.
- An armed foe whose natural attack averages higher discards the weapon and strikes unarmed.
- A monster's unarmed attack can roll up to three damage spans, each gated by your Reflexes setting.
- Watchful revenants cannot be backstabbed and are never “unaware”.

## What they pay

The row's lootTableKey selects the loot table, and soulPts sets the soul value a trap captures. As a rough map from the sample: orcs use table A, giants F, ghosts and wraiths I, daedra J, vampires Q, daedra lords and liches S, the Skeletal Warrior H. Higher-tier tables carry better gear; promoted elites and champions improve the odds again. The same dungeon-kind grade that makes a place dangerous also sets its loot odds, so a high-tier foe in a high-tier place pays best.

Danger scales from the place as well as the foe. A town, a mine and a natural cave are the gentlest grades; a crypt, vampire haunt or dragon's den raises both foe strength and loot. See Danger and regions, The hero's threat and Elites and champions.

## Common mistakes

- Reading a base row as online fact. The room's Meaner Monsters/Enemy Expansion rows are the online foes.
- Bringing iron to a silver fight. Online it cuts damage; against the Skeletal Warrior the edge matters too.
- Assuming a family is immune to poison or magic. Immunity lives on the career/effect, not the label.
- Treating a class enemy as a fixed level. It is built at your level.
- Ignoring behaviour. Flying, aquatic and spectral foes path differently; a water foe will not come to you on land.

## Next

- Fighting
- Elites and champions

docs.title: Loot and inventory
docs.summary: Check what you carry and how heavy it is before taking more gear from the Hold.
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Your carry allowance is based on Strength: floor(Strength × 1.5) kilograms.
> - Online, carrying more than 75% of your allowance slows you and drains fatigue over time.
> - Item stacks add their weight together; loose gold also counts.
> - Some enchanted finds appear unidentified; the Identify spell or a Mages Guild service can reveal them.
> - Take what you can use, and check your carried weight before filling your pack.

## Check what you carry

Your inventory's carried weight is the sum of your items and loose gold. A stack counts as the item's weight multiplied
by the number in the stack. Your maximum encumbrance is based on live Strength, and an effect that increases carrying
allowance can raise it.

## Why weight matters online

Online, Roleplay & Realism's encumbrance effects run for everyone. Once your load passes 75% of your allowance, the
extra weight reduces your speed and drains fatigue. The effect grows with the load, up to the system's cap. Keeping
some room in your pack helps you move and fight without paying that cost.

> [!online] Online rule
> A base-game rule says exceeding the displayed allowance has no cost. That is not the effective online rule: the
> online lane forces Roleplay & Realism's encumbrance effects on.

## Choose what to take

Activate a container to inspect its contents, then take the items you want. Before you leave a room, compare what you
found with what you already carry. A heavier load can slow you and spend fatigue, so you do not need to take every
item. Keep track of your carried weight as you collect gear and gold.

## Unidentified finds

Some enchanted finds arrive unidentified. Their true name and bonus lines stay hidden until you identify them, though
the item's enchantment and rolled lines still work. Use the Identify spell or a Mages Guild service when one is
available. The service belongs to a later town guild visit; for now, check the item's visible
details and carry it if you want to keep it.

## Next

- Health, fatigue and rest
- Leaving the Hold

docs.title: Health, fatigue and rest
docs.summary: Watch your health and fatigue, and recover with rest when you have a safe place to stop.
headings: Survival: food, water, warmth and sleep
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Health, fatigue and spell points are separate pools; exertion spends fatigue.
> - Online, rest at a bed, lit fire or tent; a night advances your character's clock while a short rest does not, and rest restores spell points for every class.
> - Do not begin a rest with enemies nearby, while swimming or while airborne. Poison and disease are not cured by resting.
> - Climates & Calories adds hunger, thirst, warmth and sleep; its default Boons tier takes nothing from you and rewards needs met.
> - Horse care is a separate row: feeding a horse grows its bond, and every five bond points raise all four of its stats.

## Watch your pools

Health keeps you alive. Fatigue is spent through exertion such as walking, running, climbing, swimming and jumping.
Spell points are spent when you cast. You can check the pools on the interface while exploring.

## Rest to recover

Resting restores health, fatigue and spell points. Health recovery depends on Medical and your character's health.
Online, rest at a bed, lit fire or tent. When a night is due, resting advances your character's clock; a short rest
between nights does not. Online rest also restores spell points for every class.

Where you sleep changes what the sleep is worth. A bed (a rented room, your own house or your ship) and a camp within reach of a lit fire are the good sleep: they pay the full hourly recovery in every tier, and the survival sleep debt clears at 1.5 hours an hour. Bare ground is rough: on Hard it pays half recovery, brings more interruptions and leaves a stiff morning; Casual and Boons keep the full hour.

Danger can interrupt an online rest action.

If you are poisoned or diseased, the game warns that resting will not cure the condition and asks whether you want to
rest anyway. Choose a proper cure when one is available; do not treat sleep as a remedy.

> [!warning] Find a safe place first
> The game refuses to start a rest when enemies are nearby, while you are swimming or when you are not grounded. Hard
> survival also blocks rest in severe cold without shelter or fire, and in extreme heat even when sheltered.

## If fatigue runs out

When fatigue reaches zero with no nearby enemies and while you are not swimming, you collapse and lose an hour while
recovering. If you reach zero in water or with enemies nearby, the game damages your health instead. Watch fatigue
while moving and avoid unnecessary exertion when you are already worn down.

## Survival: food, water, warmth and sleep

Climates & Calories (Ralzar's mod, as a Features row) adds hunger, thirst, sleep, felt temperature and wetness. It has four tiers: Off, Boons (the default), Casual and Hard. Online each player chooses their own tier: the world's counters and food are shared, but only your body pays your tier's price. The temperature plate beside the compass is on by default.

The needs move in stages. Hunger counts since your last meal: Peckish at 4 hours, Hungry at 12 and Starving at 24. Thirst runs from Thirsty at 50 to Parched at 80 and Dehydrated at 100 on a 150 scale, with harm past 120. Sleep debt starts after 16 waking hours: four hours of debt makes you Tired, eight Drowsy and twelve Exhausted. Wetness runs from Damp to Drenched.

Food is the first answer. A meal's satiety holds the hunger clock, and better food lasts longer: rations about four hours, cooked fish far more than raw, meat more than raw meat. Food spoils through Fresh, Stale, Mouldy, Rotten and Putrid stages, and each stage feeds less. A waterskin holds drinks; one drink takes 40 off your thirst.

What each tier charges:

| Tier | What unmet needs cost |
|---|---|
| Boons (default) | Nothing. Needs never go red. Meeting them earns boons: Well fed (+5 Strength, +5 Endurance), Quenched (+5 Agility, +5 Speed), Well rested (+5 Intelligence, +5 Willpower, from a bed or fire only) and all three at once, Thriving (+5 Luck). A lit fire beside you while awake restores fatigue. |
| Casual | Unmet needs borrow stamina down to half the pool, and the loan is paid back when the need is met. No rest gate, no sickness, no stiff morning. |
| Hard | Unmet needs cost attributes and health; wet armour rusts; raw or spoiled food can make you sick; a rough night leaves you stiff for four hours; rest is refused in freezing cold without fire or shelter and in scorching heat. |

On Boons and Casual, raw or spoiled food cannot make you sick. On Hard it can. Exposure and dehydration can kill on Hard, but never in your sleep or in mid-jump.

## Feeding a horse

Horse care is its own Features row: Off, Boons (the default) or Hard, each player's own online. Each horse rolls its own Speed, Stamina, Endurance and Strength between 20 and 80. Feeding raises its bond with you: a day's food (a Sack of Oats) adds three bond points, and an apple is a smaller treat it loves a little more. Every five bond points are +1 to all four of its stats, so a fed horse is a better horse.

Hunger still shows as Fed, Hungry or Starving, but only Hard makes it cost anything: on Hard, Hungry takes ten off every stat and slows its breath, and after two days unfed it is Starving (twenty-five down, no gallop, and the bond fades). A horse never dies of hunger. A stabled horse is fed for you, a horse left waiting grazes, and one kept with you eats from your packs when game time passes.

## Common mistakes

- Sleeping on bare ground as a habit. On Hard, rough rest pays half and can leave you stiff; a bed or a fire is the better sleep.
- Resting when a need is at its worst and expecting a full recovery. On Casual and Hard, unmet needs still weigh on you; on Boons, meet the need first and take the boon.
- Ignoring the temperature plate. Felt cold and heat decide whether Hard will refuse your rest at all.
- Feeding a horse only when it is starving. Bond is the reward for feeding well, and on Hard starvation also fades it.
- Treating a potion as a cure for hunger or thirst. Survival needs are fed and watered, not cured.

## Next

- Dying online
- Leaving the Hold

docs.title: Lycanthropy and vampirism
docs.summary: Recognize infection, understand each curse's benefits and costs, and follow the available cure quests.
headings: Live as a werewolf or wereboar
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Treat an infection before it becomes a permanent curse if you want to avoid the change.
> - Lycanthropy's attribute and skill bonuses apply in beast form.
> - Vampirism changes with sunlight; a raised hood protects you without granting the night bonus.
> - Feeding and the werebeast's urge are different requirements.
> - Both curses have cure quests; ordinary disease treatment applies to the infection stage.

## Recognize an infection

Attacks from a werewolf or wereboar can infect you with that creature's strain of lycanthropy. A vampire or vampire ancient can infect you with vampirism. Infection is chance-based. The infection gate refuses characters below level 2.

At first, you carry a disease entry. A warning dream follows after the infection day. Once more than three game days have passed, and the warning dream has been dismissed, the infection can turn into a full curse. Vampirism also passes through a false-death sequence before the transformation completes. Do not confuse that presentation with ordinary combat death.

Use Cure Disease during the infection stage; the disease system includes these infections in its cure handling. Once the full racial curse takes over, you need its separate cure path. See Health, fatigue and rest for ordinary disease care. You cannot stack both completed curses: an existing racial override rejects another infection.

## Live as a werewolf or wereboar

Your curse grants a Lycanthropy spell that changes your form. Entering beast form unequips both hands and replaces weapon use with claws. While transformed, you cannot open your inventory or hold conversations. Prepare your supplies and finish town business before changing.

In beast form, you gain +40 Strength, Agility, Endurance and Speed, plus +30 Swimming, Running, Stealth, Critical Strike, Climbing, Hand-to-Hand and Jumping. In human form those bonuses disappear. The transformed body's minimum weapon material to be hit is Silver; you also have disease immunity. These benefits do not remove your form's restrictions.

Entering beast form normally has a once-per-game-day gate. Hircine's Ring bypasses that gate and prevents the forced full-moon change and rising urge. Transformation healing has its own daily gate: repeated changes do not provide repeated full heals. The ring frees the change, not the healing.

Online, a full moon forces the change while it is up at night. At dawn the lock ends, and you can use the power to change back. This differs from the offline full-calendar-day rule. You do not automatically become human merely because the forced period ends.

After a game month without killing an innocent, your maximum-health ceiling starts shrinking. The source counts dead civilians and city-watch guards for satiation; killing an ordinary monster is not a substitute. Online Renown health sits above the base-health limiter. The curse therefore carries a continuing cost even when you prefer to stay human.

## Live as a vampire

Your vampire bonuses apply without a separate beast transformation. Out of sunlight, you gain +20 to Strength, Willpower, Agility, Endurance, Personality, Speed and Luck. The Anthotis clan also applies the modifier to Intelligence. You gain +30 Jumping, Running, Stealth, Critical Strike, Climbing and Hand-to-Hand, along with vampire spells, disease immunity and paralysis immunity.

Direct daytime sunlight reverses the affected attribute bonus to −20. This port does not burn you for being a vampire in sunlight. Indoors and underground, the sunlight penalty does not apply. A raised cloak or robe hood gives a neutral attribute modifier in sunlight: it shields you without making daytime count as night. Holy-place damage remains a separate danger.

Feed by landing an attack. You do not need to kill an innocent as a werebeast does. If you have not fed within the last game day, you cannot begin resting. Bare-headed vampires also face a daytime fast-travel refusal; raising a suitable hood removes that racial travel block.

Becoming a vampire changes the active guild-membership book. Your mortal memberships are preserved for a cure, but you use the vampire book while cursed. The Thieves Guild and Dark Brotherhood carry across that swap. Your clan also has its own initiation and quests; do not assume your previous guild access remains identical.

## Remove a completed curse

The $CUREVAM quest leads through a vampire contact and the Keeper of the Bloodline to your bloodfather. Slaying the bloodfather lifts vampirism. The quest also allows an outcome where you remain loyal to the vampires and keep the curse.

The $CUREWER quest starts with a priest. Its bloodline route involves an alchemist's vial and passing your curse to the last descendant. Another branch searches for a book, then information about Glenmoril Coven and a kinder cure. Finding that information is not itself proof you are cured. Follow the quest's actual completion state.

Online, curse quests roll at shorter character-time intervals while the relevant quest arm is idle. This does not guarantee an immediate letter. The checked sources establish these quests; they do not set a universal shrine interaction or ordinary potion that instantly removes either completed curse.

## Common mistakes

- Treating Cure Disease as a completed-curse cure: use it before the infection turns.
- Expecting human-form werebeast bonuses or unlimited transformation heals: both have explicit limits.
- Raising a hood and expecting the night bonus: sunlight becomes neutral under it.

## Next

- Health, fatigue and rest
- Questions new players ask

docs.title: Dying online
docs.summary: Online death returns you to a safe point with half health and takes one tenth of the gold you carry.
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Death does not end your online character's run; you wake at a safe point.
> - In Privateer's Hold, you return to the dungeon's start marker.
> - You revive with half your maximum health, rounded down, with a minimum of 1.
> - The game takes one part in 10 of the gold you carry, rounded down. Banked gold is untouched.

## Getting back

If you die in Privateer's Hold online, you return to the Hold's start marker. If you die in another dungeon, you wake
just outside its entrance. Above ground, the game chooses a nearby temple, town or graveyard as your safe point.

A party member's Resurrect spell is a separate rescue path: they target your fallen body, and a successful rescue
raises you where you lie. It withdraws the ordinary respawn's stated gold loss. It is not the same as choosing respawn,
and special areas or death states can prevent resurrection.

If you are alive but stuck, /unstuck offers another route: indoors it leaves by the door you entered; outdoors it
takes you to the nearest town. See Keys and commands for the command and cancellation.

PvP death in the Open Zone has separate loss and return rules. Do not apply this page's
ordinary carried-gold penalty to it.

## What death costs

You return with half your maximum health, rounded down, and at least 1 health. The game removes one part in
10 of the gold you carry, rounded down. Gold in the bank and letters of credit are not part of
this carried-gold penalty.

The online death screen lets you respawn immediately with Enter or wait for the automatic respawn. The loss is
shown on the death screen before the game applies it.

> [!tip] Before you head out
> Keep only the gold you need to carry. The death penalty applies to your carried purse, not your bank balance.

## What you keep

The ordinary death penalty does not destroy your items, equipment or quest items. It subtracts from your carried
gold, and the revival restores the living character rather than replacing their inventory. Banked gold and letters
of credit are outside that carried-gold deduction.

There are separate exceptions to item safety: the world respawn also checks whether a revenant killer takes a piece,
and the Open Zone has its own death drops. Keeping your pack through an ordinary death does not protect it from those
systems or undo wear from the fight.

## Common mistakes

- Carrying all your gold into a dungeon: the ordinary penalty reaches your whole carried purse.
- Skipping the bank before a risky trip: gold left in the bank is outside the carried-gold penalty.
- Entering an Open Zone fight unprepared: PvP death there follows separate rules, including death drops.

## Next

- Leaving the Hold

docs.title: Stuck and recovery
docs.summary: A recovery ladder for a stuck character, a held quest or a missing NPC, and when to report a bug.
headings: /unstuck in detail, and what it will not do
Saves, deaths and what can be undone
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Decide first whether the game is holding you (a rule, a wait or a wall) or a step has bugged; the answer changes the ladder.
> - /unstuck leaves a dungeon or building by the door you came in, or outdoors takes you to the nearest town. It has a cooldown.
> - There is no developer console in the port, so console commands are not a recovery route.
> - Online, a death is not a reset: you respawn with half health and a tenth of carried gold gone, and you cannot rewind the character.
> - A black screen or a game that will not start belongs in Troubleshooting, not this ladder.

## Held or bugged?

Held means the game is doing what it says: a quest step waits for a place, a day, a letter or a level; a door is locked; an NPC is elsewhere. Bugged means the stated condition is met and the step still does not move, or an object or person the quest names is not there at all.

Read the journal before anything else. L opens the LogBook on Active Quests and the pause menu's Quests tab lists every questline with what it waits on (“Opens at level 10”, “Continues with a registered account”). A step that says it could not begin here and will be offered again is held, not broken.

## The recovery ladder

1. Read the journal and the questline list. Note the exact objective, region, place and any time stated. If the journal does not name the region, place or person together, write down what it does say.
2. Check the gate. Questline steps open at levels, Renown, registered-account or online gates, and festival windows. A letter arrives in a town, outdoors, by day; one new line begins at most once per character hour. If the list says it is waiting for an account, that is the answer.
3. Give a held step its condition. Be in a proper town when a step comes due, at the right building kind; leave and re-enter the region; let the character clock advance. A failed online step costs no faction standing and steps re-offer.
4. Use /unstuck for geometry, not for quests. Type it in chat. Inside a dungeon or building it takes you out by the door you entered. Outdoors it takes you to the nearest town. It is not a quest teleport and it will not move a quest object.
5. Handle the missing NPC or target. Re-read the objective; check whether the quest named a building or a dungeon and whether you are in the right instance. Quest dungeons can be entered as Your instance; a party member's quest does not complete yours. If the named person is genuinely absent after a reload of the area, treat it as a bug and keep the journal text.
6. Use death and loading only for position. Online death returns you to the nearest safe place (or the Hold's start, inside the Hold) with half health and the gold loss; leaving the page and returning saves the character. Loading an underground online save wakes you above ground at the nearest safe place. None of these rewinds progress.
7. Restart cleanly. Reload the page; the online character checkpoints are attempted during play, when the page hides and on exit. Do not clear browser storage before you know what it holds. Offline, F9 saves and F11 loads; loading is disabled during online play.
8. Report what you can reproduce. /bug opens the private developer report form; /report is for player conduct. The issue tracker and Discord are linked from Troubleshooting.

## /unstuck in detail, and what it will not do

/unstuck is a chat command, not a key. Its rules are specific:

- Indoors (dungeon or building) it leaves by the door you came in.
- Outdoors it takes you to the nearest city, never into the Open Zone, and past the Eltheric Veil to the nearest freeport rather than back across the sea.
- Cooldown: 30 minutes normally, 60 minutes in the Open Zone. In the Open Zone it also runs a five-minute wait that you can cancel with /unstuck cancel, and it fails if another player is within 600 m; you cannot use it with another player that close.
- Some made levels refuse it or give their own way home (a court refuses it; an Elite Breach's Redoubt is the way home), so the command is not a universal exit.
- /unstuck now is refused; the only argument it takes is cancel.

There is no console. The port hides ToggleConsole because it has no console, so no console command can rescue a character, spawn an item or complete a quest. Anything that promises that is not DFO.

## Missing NPCs and quest objects

A named NPC can be in another building, another region, or inside a quest instance you have not entered. The journal may name a place without naming the person, and the quest may point at a building you have already passed. Work from the journal, use the map for the region and place, and check the Quests tab for the step's status. If the quest is sharing with a party, remember that each character keeps its own copy and progress; a party kill does not advance your objective unless the quest is yours and the objective is shared.

A quest object is not vendor loot: selling it can make the quest unrecoverable. If an item is gone, say so in the report rather than continuing to guess.

## Saves, deaths and what can be undone

Online, the character belongs to the account service, not to your browser. Checkpoints are attempted during play, on page hiding and on exit; a crash can lose recent progress. Loading an offline save cannot rewind an online character, and an online death is not a reload. Offline, F9/F11 are the classic save/load pair and an offline Project Legacy rise can respawn you at the gold cost.

What can be undone: dying (respawn), a bad position (/unstuck), a logged-off span (checkpoint), a stuck UI (reload). What cannot: a sold quest item, a completed permanent choice (mastery, specialisation path, a third craft above 50), or an online character's lost progress before the last checkpoint.

## Black screen or no start

If the game does not render or the page will not load, stop here and use Troubleshooting. Check the game data picker (ARENA2, not its parent folder), WebGL2, and the browser console message. The source does not promise a universal blank-canvas fix, and clearing site data can erase saves and imported game data. Record the visible message and where loading stops before changing anything.

## Common mistakes

- Using /unstuck for a held quest. It moves your body, never a quest state.
- Expecting a console. The port has none.
- Clearing site data as a first fix. It can delete saves and an imported data store.
- Assuming a party shares quest progress. Each character keeps its own copy.
- Reporting without the journal text. The exact objective, region and step wording is what a report needs.

docs.title: Leaving the Hold
docs.summary: Find the dungeon's exit door to emerge outside Privateer's Hold, then follow the road toward Gothway Garden.
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Leave through the dungeon's exit door; the transition places you outside the entrance you used.
> - A monument to Julian LeFay stands beside the Hold's exit landing.
> - Gothway Garden is the first town a new character reaches from the Hold.
> - Online, the public Hold is one way: after you leave, you cannot return to its public room.

## Find the exit

Follow the cave toward its exit door. Activating that door takes you outside and places you on the landing by the
dungeon entrance, facing outward. The source does not define the Hold's internal layout, so use the game's compass and
your own exploration to find the door.

## Continue toward town

The monument to Julian LeFay stands beside the exit landing. From there, follow the road toward Gothway Garden, the
nearest town and the first one a new character walks into after leaving the Hold.

> [!warning] The Hold is one way online
> The public online room refuses re-entry after you have left Privateer's Hold. Complete anything you want to do here
> before taking the exit.

Your own private instance of the Hold is different: you can enter it again at any time. It is a separate copy
for you and your party, not a way back into the public room.

## Next

- Your first town
- Moving through the Hold

docs.title: Reading a town
docs.summary: Use the town map and building signs to find services, then account for opening hours and the online rules at night.
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Open the town map to see discovered buildings and their doors; the map groups them into quarters.
> - Read the building name and type before entering. Shops, banks, guild halls, temples and taverns offer different services.
> - Online, shops, banks, libraries, palaces and guild halls stay available around the clock. City gates also stay open.
> - Houses, temples and taverns keep their own entry rules; “online” does not mean every door is open.

## Find a building

Original handbook symbols for eight town services

Use the town map to orient yourself, then follow the marked doors in the street. A building's name identifies its kind of service: an Armorer repairs and sells armor (shops and prices), a Weapon Smith handles weapons, and a General Store carries general goods. A Bank or guild hall is a distinct service building, not a shop counter.

If you do not know where a service is, ask a towns-person with Where is. People may point you in a direction or mark a known building on your map. See talking to people.

## Hours and entry

In the classic schedule, shops and public buildings have different hours. DFO Online relieves shops, guild halls, banks, libraries and palaces of their classic closing hours. You can use those services at night without waiting for morning. Temples and taverns are open at all hours under their own schedule; houses are not public services, and faction houses may require membership.

Online city gates do not close at night. This removes the old need to wait outside a walled city until morning, but curfew laws can still matter in places where an edict is active. See the law.

> [!tip] Locked door?
> Check whether it is a private house or a faction building before assuming the town is closed. Membership, ownership, a quest, or a lock can govern entry independently of the hour.

## Common mistakes

- Waiting outside a city gate for morning. Online city gates stay open, so a night spent waiting costs a game day of events, couriers and quest timers; walk in and use the relieved services.
- Assuming every door follows the relieved hours. Houses, faction houses and some temples keep their own entry rules; forcing the wrong door can bring the watch rather than a service (the law). Cost: time, or a crime.
- Searching a large town by eye. A towns-person's Where is answer can mark the building on your map (talking to people); walking every quarter first can take the whole session.

## Next

- Shops and prices
- Talking to people
