docs.title: Shops and prices
docs.summary: Match a shop to the goods it stocks, compare its offer with your needs, and use haggling with condition and town prices in mind.
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Use the right counter: each shop type stocks and buys particular groups of goods.
> - The price shown before you confirm is the price that matters; haggling depends on both Mercantile and Personality.
> - Online, worn weapons and armor are worth less, and a shop limits what it pays for items you sell.
> - A town's Prosperity affects asking and selling prices. Compare counters before spending or selling.

## Choose a counter

The nine shop types are Alchemist, Armorer, Bookseller, Clothing Store, Furniture Store, Gem Store, General Store, Pawn Shop and Weapon Smith. Their stock is rolled for each shop and can change when the game day changes. A shop buys only the item groups its counter accepts. The Pawn Shop takes a broad range; specialist counters are narrower. Only Armorers, General Stores and Weapon Smiths repair equipment.

Some goods are handled through their own systems rather than ordinary shop shelves. For example, the game excludes endless-stock supplies, trade goods and boat parts from ordinary buyback. Read the counter's available actions before hauling something across town to sell.

## Read the price

The regional price index sets a shared baseline, and shop quality moves the counter's asking price around that baseline. Haggling uses the merchant's skill against yours. Mercantile carries more weight in the calculation than Personality, but both matter (attributes and skills). Your offered sale price is worse than the counter's buying price, and online limits the maximum a counter pays.

Online, Roleplay & Realism: Items prices weapons and armor by condition. New or well-kept goods are worth more than badly worn pieces. Town Prosperity adds another local factor to what counters ask and pay; the score is shown on the town's card (reading a town). A thriving town can therefore feel different from a struggling one even where the regional index is the same.

> [!tip] Before you sell
> Check condition, compare the counter's displayed offer, and keep in mind that an item bought from a counter cannot later be sold back to that counter for more than it originally charged.

## Common mistakes

- Selling to the first counter you pass. Offers vary with the counter's quality, the item's condition and the town's Prosperity; compare a second counter before selling a full haul. Cost: the difference on every item.
- Repairing a found item to raise its sale price. A found item keeps its found condition mark when sold, and a paid repair adds no resale credit (salvage and repair). Cost: the repair fee.
- Carrying a day's takings into the next dungeon. The online death penalty takes one tenth of the gold you carry; deposit the proceeds at a bank first. Cost: gold on every death.

## Next

- Banks
- Taverns and rooms

docs.title: Banks
docs.summary: Deposit gold, move money with a letter of credit, and understand the shared online account before borrowing.
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Online, every branch accesses one Bank of the Empire account.
> - Deposit spare gold before travel; carried coins add weight and are exposed to the risks of adventuring.
> - A letter of credit costs a 1% commission and is lighter than carrying its value in coins.
> - An online loan is limited to 1,000 gold per character level, and default or an existing loan blocks new borrowing empire-wide.

## Your account

Use any bank branch to deposit or withdraw. Offline, accounts are regional. Online, all branches use one Empire account, and gold already held in regional accounts folds into it when you join. Loan records and due dates stay tied to the region where they were taken. A default there blocks new borrowing at every branch; the Empire can collect what is owed from the shared account and other regional deposits.

Deposits draw from your purse first, then from a wagon if needed. A withdrawal can be refused if you lack the balance or cannot carry the coins. Gold has weight, so a large withdrawal can burden you even when the account can cover it.

## Letters of credit

A letter of credit carries a stated face value without coin weight. The bank charges 1% above that value when issuing it, and the minimum is 100 gold. You can use eligible letters to pay for purchases, fines and market transactions. Deposit a letter to turn its full face value back into account gold; the bank deposits all letters you carry together.

## Loans

Online loans use the Empire's shared cap: up to 1,000 gold per character level. You can hold only one active loan across the Empire, and a default or an existing loan standing prevents another. Interest of 10% is added when the loan is made, so early repayment does not remove it. The term is one game year. If a loan becomes overdue, the bank takes what it can from the account before the remainder defaults.

> [!warning] Borrow with a repayment plan
> The game charges the interest up front and checks repayment against the game calendar. Missing the due date can affect your account and legal standing.

## Common mistakes

- Withdrawing your whole balance before a trip. Carried coins have weight and face the online death penalty; a death costs one tenth of the gold you carry, while bank gold and letters of credit are untouched. Withdraw only what you will spend.
- Borrowing up to the full 1,000 gold per character level without a repayment plan. The 10% interest is added when the loan is made, so early repayment does not remove it, and a default blocks new borrowing empire-wide.

## Next

- Taverns and rooms

- Safe storage

docs.title: Taverns and rooms
docs.summary: Rent a room to rest in town, or buy food and drink while keeping the online price and rest rules in mind.
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Taverns stay open around the clock. Their rooms and menu are separate services.
> - A room is rented by the day; you can rent no more than 350 days in total.
> - Online, positive room, food and drink prices are halved and rounded up, with a minimum of 1 gold; a free room stays free.
> - A Knightly Order member can rent a room free. You can eat or drink once every four game hours.

## Rent a room

Choose the room service at a tavern and set the number of days. The base room price is 7 gold per day before haggling; online, the essential-price rule halves it. The total rental limit counts days you already have, so a free room does not bypass the 350-day ceiling. Members of a Knightly Order receive free rooms.

The game advances time as you rest. You can rest in a town tavern without using the outdoor camp action, which is important because camping in town can count as vagrancy. See the law.

## Food and drink

The tavern menu has food and drink at listed prices. Online, their essential prices are halved, rounded up, and never fall below 1 gold. Eating or drinking restores health based on the menu price, not the online discount. You can consume another item after four game hours.

Food can help when you need a small amount of healing or want to avoid spending a potion. It does not replace managing fatigue, health and safe rest during a dangerous trip (health, fatigue and rest).

> [!tip] Check the clock
> A room stay moves game time forward. Shops may be open when you wake even if the hour changed, because online shop hours are relieved; your quests and other timers can still advance.

## Common mistakes

- Camping in town instead of renting a room. Camping in town can count as vagrancy while a rented room does not (the law). Cost: a fine or a legal-standing loss.
- Renting for several days when you need one night. A room is rented by the day and advances game time as you rest; a long stay burns gold and can move quest timers forward.
- Treating tavern food as your only healing on a dangerous trip. One item every four game hours is a small heal; it does not replace potions or a safe rest (health, fatigue and rest). Cost: dying with food still in your pack.

## Next

- Talking to people
- Time and weather

docs.title: Talking to people
docs.summary: Ask about places, people and news with a tone suited to the person, and use the town's reputation to understand their response.
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Use Tell me about for information and Where is to ask about places, people, things or work.
> - Polite and Blunt draw on Etiquette and Streetwise respectively; Normal avoids either tone's social-group modifier.
> - A person's willingness to talk reflects the local People faction's view of you and your social standing.
> - A helpful direction may point toward a place or mark it on your map, but not every person knows every answer.

## Choose what to ask

Start a conversation with a towns-person, then choose Tell me about or Where is. The first offers general topics and named organizations (the NPC guilds). The second sorts questions into Location, People, Things and Work. Ask about a service when you need directions; the map reveal, when it happens, marks the building so you can find it after the conversation.

People do not share one universal opinion. Townsfolk stand with their region's People faction, and the greeting reflects that faction's reputation toward you together with your biography and standing with their social group. If someone refuses to speak, another person may react differently.

## Tone and skill

The three tones are Polite, Normal and Blunt. Polite uses Etiquette; Blunt uses Streetwise (the skills). Each question rolls an answer tier using your Personality, the question type, your tone and the relevant skill. Polite and Blunt can suit different social groups, so there is no single tone that improves every exchange.

Questions are not guaranteed to produce a useful answer. The person may not know the place, and a low answer tier can give only a brush-off. When you are looking for a building, ask several people or use the town map.

## Common mistakes

- Using Blunt on a polite crowd. Blunt rolls Streetwise and Polite rolls Etiquette, and the wrong tone for the social group lowers the answer tier; a brush-off leaves you without directions. Cost: a wasted search.
- Giving up after one refusal. Townsfolk answer from their own faction's view of you, so another person may help where the first would not; ask several or use the town map. Cost: a building you never find.
- Expecting every answer to be true or useful. A low answer tier can return only a brush-off, and not every person knows every place; a wrong direction can send you across town. Cost: travel time.

## Next

- The NPC guilds
- Notice boards

- Standing and reputation

docs.title: The NPC guilds
docs.summary: Join a guild, temple or knightly order through its own requirements, then earn rank to unlock services and training.
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Most guilds let you apply at their hall when your faction reputation and relevant skills meet the entry requirements.
> - Rank depends on both standing and permanent skill values; temporary skill boosts do not count.
> - Online, earned promotions are granted immediately when you open the guild services. Other rank reviews still follow their review rules.
> - Guilds and temples train skills only up to 50. Members pay 100 × character level a session; temples also train non-members at 400 × level; knightly orders train nothing.
> - A session takes three game hours and raises one skill, and your character can train again after 12 game hours.

## Joining

Ask at the hall of a Fighters Guild, Mages Guild, temple or knightly order to check whether you qualify. The ordinary application requires non-negative standing with the faction, one guild skill of at least 22 and a second guild skill of at least 4. Each temple shares a membership slot with the other temples, and all knightly orders share another; joining a different one replaces that membership.

The Thieves Guild and Dark Brotherhood are different. You cannot apply at their halls. Their membership begins with an invitation quest that follows the relevant crime tally, and you join only after completing that quest successfully. The online letter wait is shorter than the classic three-day delay.

## Rank and services

Ranks run from 0 to 9 under the guild's rank table. Higher rank needs higher faction reputation and skill values, and the required skills are read at their permanent values. In ordinary online play your own guild rank stops at 7; ranks 8 and 9 are chapter seats. Online, when you have earned a promotion, opening the services applies it at once; the usual 28-day review delay is not used for earned promotions. Demotion and probation still use review timing.

Services vary by organization. A temple can offer healing, a library or other services at its own rank thresholds. The Mages Guild adds services such as magic items, summoning and teleport at higher ranks. Its rank-8 teleport requires a chapter seat online. Check the hall's service list to see what your membership currently unlocks.

## Training

Guilds and temples train skills, but only to a cap of 50. A trainer refuses a skill whose permanent value is already above 50; a skill sitting exactly on 50 is still offered. Each session trains one skill, takes three game hours, and costs fatigue, so a session is a real commitment of your character's day.

The base price is the same formula everywhere: 100 × your character level as a member, or 400 × your character level as a non-member. At level 10 that is 1,000 gold a session as a member and 4,000 as a stranger, before any Refined Training reduction. Guild halls train members only; temples are the places that also train non-members. A character can train once every 12 game hours, whichever skill and whichever trainer the session uses.

| Organization | Skills offered for training |
|---|---|
| Fighters Guild | Archery, Axe, Blunt Weapon, Critical Strike, Giantish, Hand-to-Hand, Jumping, Long Blade, Orcish, Running, Short Blade, Swimming |
| Mages Guild | Alteration, Daedric, Destruction, Dragonish, Harpy, Illusion, Impish, Mysticism, Orcish, Restoration, Spriggan, Thaumaturgy |
| Thieves Guild | Backstabbing, Blunt Weapon, Climbing, Dodging, Jumping, Lockpicking, Pickpocket, Short Blade, Stealth, Streetwise, Swimming |
| Dark Brotherhood | Archery, Backstabbing, Climbing, Critical Strike, Daedric, Destruction, Dodging, Running, Short Blade, Stealth, Streetwise, Swimming |
| Temples | Each divine trains its own list; for example Akatosh's includes Alteration, Archery, Destruction and Long Blade, and Arkay's includes Axe, Restoration and Medical |
| Knightly orders | None; an order offers no training at all |

Roleplay & Realism's Refined Training service is in force online. It lowers a session's price most at low skill: the reduction is half the base price times the skill's remaining share of 50. A raw skill therefore trains for about half price, and a skill near 50 pays almost the full base. The variant also offers a five-day intensive course that costs (session price + level × 8 + 72) × 5 and adds four permanent skill points after four days. It is offered only below skill 46 and is forced off online, because the shared world clock will not spend the four days it asks for.

## Services at a glance

| Organization | Main services |
|---|---|
| Fighters Guild | Training, repair, quests, identify, donations and cure disease |
| Mages Guild | Training, quests, identify, spells (buying is public), spellmaking, magic items, soul gems, Daedra summoning and teleport at rank 8 |
| Thieves Guild | Training, quests, selling magic items at rank 2 and the spymaster at rank 4 |
| Dark Brotherhood | Training, quests, potions at rank 1, potion making at rank 3, soul gems at rank 5 and the spymaster at rank 7 |
| Temples | Training open to anyone, quests, donations and cure disease, plus potions, spells, magic items, summoning and soul gems at the divine's own ranks |
| Knightly orders | Quests, an armour gift by personal rank and a house at rank 9 |

The Mages Guild's ranks, spell shelf and summoning rules are detailed on Mages Guild services.

> [!tip] Rank is not a single skill
> A high value in one skill is not enough by itself. Keep the standing requirement and the second qualifying guild skill in view as you work toward the next rank.

## Common mistakes

- Expecting a knightly order to train you. Orders offer no training; their gifts come from rank instead.
- Paying for a session above 50. A skill already past 50 is refused outright.
- Training twice in a day. The 12-game-hour cooldown applies per character across all trainers and skills.
- Assuming a guild hall will serve a stranger. Guild services need membership; temples are the exception for training.

## Next

- The law
- Mages Guild teleport

docs.title: The Fighters Guild
docs.summary: Join a Fighters Guild hall for training, repair, identify and cure services, and the guild's own quest work.
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Join at a Fighters Guild hall with non-negative standing, one guild skill at 22 and a second at 4.
> - The hall trains members only; it is the place for weapons, movement and combat skills.
> - Its non-training services are repair, identify, donations, cure disease and guild quests.
> - The guild does not sell spells or potions; those are Mages Guild or temple services.

## Joining and rank

The ordinary guild application needs non-negative faction standing, one Fighters Guild skill of at least 22 and a second
guild skill of at least 4. Ranks run from 0 to 9; promotion reads faction reputation and the permanent values of the
guild's skills, not temporary boosts.

Online, personal rank stops at 7. Ranks 8 and 9 are chapter seats. When you earn a promotion, opening the hall's services
applies it immediately; the old review delay is not used for earned promotions. The NPC guilds explains
the shared rules.

## What the hall offers

| Service | What it does | Access |
|---|---|---|
| Training | Raise one guild skill by one point | Member; 100 × character level a session |
| Repair | Repair worn equipment | Member; quoted gold |
| Identify | Identify an item | Open to anyone |
| Quests | Take guild work | Open; see the Fighters Guild quests |
| Donate | Give gold to the guild | Open; affects standing |
| Cure disease | Treat a disease | Open; quoted gold |

A training session takes three game hours, costs fatigue, and can be taken once every 12 game hours. The guild trains
Archery, Axe, Blunt Weapon, Critical Strike, Giantish, Hand-to-Hand, Jumping, Long Blade, Orcish, Running, Short Blade
and Swimming, up to skill 50. The price formula and Refined Training reduction are in The NPC guilds.

The hall does not offer the Mages Guild's spell, magic-item, soul-gem, summoning or teleport services, and it does not
sell potions. Use Mages Guild services, Temples or
The Thieves Guild for those.

## Common mistakes

- Applying with only one qualifying skill.
- Expecting a promotion to arrive on a timer after you have already earned it.
- Paying for training above skill 50; the trainer refuses it.
- Looking for potions or spells at a Fighters Guild hall.

docs.title: Thievery
docs.summary: Stealth, backstabs, locks, pockets, stolen goods, and how the Thieves Guild and Dark Brotherhood find you.
headings: How the crime guilds find you
In town, for a new character
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Crouch with C to sneak; a foe's stealth check comes once a game minute, and slow movement skips checks.
> - A backstab needs the foe facing away; a success triples the blow.
> - Pickpocketing and lockpicking use the Steal interaction mode; a failed pickpocket is a crime and calls the watch.
> - Stolen goods carry a mark: merchants buy them but never reshelve them, and a conviction takes them.
> - The Thieves Guild and Dark Brotherhood cannot be joined by asking; tallies of 10 thefts or 15 murders invite you.

## Stealth

Hold C to crouch and sneak; the separate held Sneak action ships unbound. A foe within about 25 metres makes a stealth check once a game minute, reading your Stealth against the distance. Moving at less than half speed skips every other minute's check, while a fast mover that has already been encountered is detected outright.

## Backstabs

A backstab is a separate check. The foe must be facing away when your swing resolves, and the game rolls your Backstabbing skill; a success deals triple damage. Every back-facing swing trains the skill, even when the triple roll fails, and a Watchful revenant cannot be backstabbed. Fighting covers the swing itself.

## Locks

Hold Left Alt, choose Steal, and activate a locked door to pick it; any other mode tries the door normally, and its lock refuses. No lockpick item is needed. An interior door's chance is Lockpicking + 5 × (your level − the lock's value); an outside building door is Lockpicking − 5 × the lock's value. Both clamp between 5 and 95. A magically held lock (value 20 or more) cannot be picked.

A failed attempt records the skill you tried with; the same lock does nothing until your skill changes.

## Pockets and shops

In Steal mode within about 3.2 metres, activate a person to pick their pocket; you get one attempt per person. Against a townsperson it is your Pickpocket skill (5–95); against an enemy, each level you have over it adds five. Two successes in three pinch 1–6 gold; one in three finds nothing, and only the gold arm counts for the guild. Against a townsperson, a failure sets the Pickpocketing crime and calls the watch; against an enemy it alerts the room instead.

An open shop's stock trains Pickpocket, then a being-seen roll reads that skill, the shop's quality and your load; getting away takes the goods and counts for the guild, being seen is Theft and calls the guards. A shut shop's shelf has no roll and no guards but still counts as theft for the guild. A private container tallies the guild first, then rolls, with Theft and guards on a failure.

## Stolen goods and the fence

A stolen piece carries a mark through stacks, splits and trades. Merchants buy a marked piece but never reshelve it, and a guilty verdict takes every stolen piece you carry. The Thieves Guild's fence service sells magic items from rank 2; its spymaster opens at rank 4. The Dark Brotherhood sells potions at rank 1, makes them at 3, soul gems at 5, and keeps a spymaster at 7.

## What the law does

A crime is charged where it happens and lowers that region's standing. A first pickpocketing, trespass, vagrancy or attempted breaking-and-entering may be warned instead of arrested, but the charge still lands; getting away ends the chase, not the loss. A Curfew town doubles crimes' standing cost at night. The law covers court and recovery.

## How the crime guilds find you

The Thieves Guild invites at 10 thefts; the Dark Brotherhood invites at 15 murders, counting a murdered townsperson as 5 and a guard as 1. Crossing the tally stamps a letter: three game days classically, or 24 character minutes online, about two real minutes. The initiation starts only while you are outside, the tally freezes while a letter is pending, and it never fires twice. Joining reveals the guild's hall on your town map. The NPC guilds covers ranks and services.

## In town, for a new character

- Do not test pickpocketing with a low skill: a failure is a crime.
- Do not force a lock you cannot pick; the attempt is spent until your skill moves.
- Do not carry stolen goods into a court date; a conviction takes them.
- Do not grind murders for the Dark Brotherhood. Murder leaves a lasting mark that a sentence does not fully clear.

## Common mistakes

- Expecting stealth to guarantee a backstab. The foe must face away, and the roll is your skill.
- Expecting every pickpocket success to pay. One success in three finds nothing.
- Trying the same lock twice in a row. The attempt is spent until the skill changes.
- Applying to the Thieves Guild. The tally invites you.

## Next

- The law
- The NPC guilds

docs.title: Temples
docs.summary: Join a temple, train with its clergy, and check which potions, spells, magic items, summoning and soul gems its divine offers.
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Temples share one membership slot; joining a different temple replaces the old membership.
> - Temples train anyone, members at 100 × level and strangers at 400 × level, up to skill 50.
> - Every temple offers quests, donations and cure disease; the divine's rank table decides its other services.
> - Potions, spells and magic items at a temple are the temple's service, not a Mages Guild service.

## Joining and rank

Apply at a temple with non-negative standing, one temple skill at 22 and a second at 4. Membership is shared across the
temples, so joining another divine replaces the previous temple membership. Ranks run from 0 to 9; promotion reads
reputation and permanent skill values. Online personal rank stops at 7; 8 and 9 are chapter seats. Earned promotions are
applied immediately when you open the services.

## Services

Training, quests, donations and cure disease are available at every temple. The rest depend on the divine and your rank
in that temple; the source's temple table is the authority for the exact threshold.

| Service | What it does | Typical temple access |
|---|---|---|
| Training | Raise one of the divine's skills | Anyone; member price or non-member price |
| Quests | Temple work and quest sites | Open |
| Donate | Give gold to the temple | Open; affects standing |
| Cure disease | Treat a disease | Open; quoted gold |
| Buy Potions | Buy stocked potions | Arkay/Dibella/Zenithar 1; Mara/Stendarr 2; Akatosh 4 |
| Make Potions | Mix carried ingredients | Arkay 4; Akatosh/Dibella/Mara/Stendarr 5; Zenithar 6 |
| Buy Spells | Add a ready-made spell | Kynareth 3 |
| Make Spells | Design a spell | Kynareth 6 |
| Buy Magic Items | Buy enchanted stock | Julianos 3 |
| Make Magic Items | Enchant a carried item | Julianos 5 |
| Daedra Summoning | Attempt contact and a quest offer | Other temples 7; Zenithar 8 (Julianos 6) |
| Buy Soulgems | Buy empty or filled traps | Arkay 4 |

The Mages Guild has its own versions of the spell, magic-item, summoning, soul-gem and teleport services; use
Mages Guild services for those. The Mages Guild teleport is not a temple service.

## Training

Each divine trains its own list; Akatosh's includes Alteration, Archery, Destruction and Long Blade, while Arkay's
includes Axe, Restoration and Medical. A session takes three game hours, costs fatigue, raises one skill and can be taken
once every 12 game hours. The cap is 50. See The NPC guilds for the shared price formula and Refined
Training reduction.

## Common mistakes

- Joining two temples and expecting both memberships to persist.
- Treating a temple's spell shelf as the Mages Guild's.
- Expecting every divine to sell the same potion or summoning service at the same rank.
- Paying the member price as a non-member; temples train strangers, but at 400 × level.

## Next

- The NPC guilds
- Mages Guild services
- Temple quests

docs.title: Knightly orders
docs.summary: Join an order for quests, an armour gift by personal rank and a house at rank 9; orders do not train.
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Knightly orders share one membership slot; joining a different order replaces the old one.
> - Orders train nothing. Their rewards are quest work, an armour gift and a house.
> - The armour gift follows personal rank; the house arrives at personal rank 9.
> - Online chapter seats do not grant the house, and rank 8/9 are seats rather than ordinary promotions.

## Joining and rank

Apply at an order with non-negative standing, one order skill at 22 and a second at 4. All knightly orders share one
membership slot, so joining another order replaces the previous membership. Ranks run from 0 to 9 and follow the same
reputation-and-skill promotion law as the other guilds.

Online, personal rank stops at 7; ranks 8 and 9 are chapter seats. Earned promotions are applied immediately when you
open the order's services. A chapter seat does not count as personal rank for the permanent gifts.

## What the order offers

| Service | What it does | Access |
|---|---|---|
| Quests | Order work, including hunts and rescues | Open |
| Receive Armor | Choose the order's armour gift | Knightly member; one claim per personal rank |
| Receive House | Claim the order's house | Personal rank 9; once per order |
| Training | None | The order offers no training |

The armour gift is a choice from the order's set. The house is a one-time claim at personal rank 9; online, chapter
seats grant no house. For quest work, see Knightly order quests.

Orders do not sell potions, spells, magic items, soul gems or summoning, and they do not offer the Mages Guild teleport.
Those are temple or Mages Guild services. See Temples and Mages Guild services.

## Common mistakes

- Expecting a knightly order to train a skill.
- Counting a chapter seat as personal rank 9 for the house.
- Joining two orders and expecting both memberships.
- Looking for spell or potion services at an order hall.

## Next

- The NPC guilds

docs.title: Mages Guild services
docs.summary: Find spells, magic items, soul gems and summoners, and check which membership opens each service.
headings: Services that are not Mages Guild
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Most guild services need membership and sufficient rank; buying Mages Guild spells is an exception.
> - Makers turn gold, an item or ingredients into capability. Check the finished cost before confirming.
> - Potions, fencing, spymaster work and knightly gifts belong to other organizations; this page keeps to Mages Guild services and links to them.
> - Online guild and temple summoners let you choose a prince on any day.

## Finding the guild

Visit a Mages Guild hall and speak to its service NPCs. Temples, Thieves Guild halls, Brotherhood sanctuaries and knightly orders offer different services.

Admission needs non-negative reputation and magic-school skills at 22 and 4. See The NPC guilds.

Its rank ladder is Apprentice (0), Journeyman (1), Evoker (2), Conjurer (3), Magician (4), Enchanter (5), Warlock (6), Wizard (7), Master Wizard (8), Archmage (9). Advancement checks reputation and permanent skills. Online, personal advancement stops at 7; the higher ranks are chapter seats. Opening services applies an earned promotion immediately.

## Services and access

Ranks below are Mages Guild ranks. Where another organization offers the same service, the row says so and links to that faction page. Trade windows quote purchase and sale prices.

| Service | What it does | Rank needed | Cost/what it consumes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Training | Practise an offered skill | Guild member; temples train strangers too | Quoted gold, time and fatigue |
| Quests | Take Mages Guild work | Open | None beyond the quest |
| Identify | Identify an item | Open | No guild fee |
| Buy Spells | Add a ready-made spell | Public | Quoted gold |
| Make Spells | Design a spell | Guild member | Gold; carry a spellbook |
| Buy Magic Items | Buy enchanted stock | Rank 3; Julianos 3 at a temple | Gold |
| Make Magic Items | Enchant a carried item | Rank 5; Julianos 5 at a temple | Gold, eligible item; a filled gem if binding a soul |
| Teleportation | Choose a destination on the teleport map | Rank 8; paid option admits any member | Free at 8+; paid travel below it |
| Daedra Summoning | Attempt contact and a quest offer | Rank 6; Julianos 6, other temples 7 except Zenithar 8 | Summoning fee; failure still costs gold |
| Buy Soulgems | Buy empty or filled traps | Rank 4; Arkay 4 at a temple | Quoted gold |

Paid teleportation depends on your Travel Options setting, off by default. Below rank 8 its fee is (8 - rank)  200 gold. See Mages Guild teleport for world-boundary restrictions.

## Services that are not Mages Guild

Those services are listed here only because a player may have seen them in a guild or temple window. They belong to
another faction:

- Potions, temple spells, Julianos magic items, temple summoning and Arkay soul gems: Temples.
- Selling magic items and the spymaster: The Thieves Guild.
- Brotherhood potions, potion making, soul gems and spymaster: The Dark Brotherhood.
- Armour and house gifts: Knightly orders.
- Fighters Guild training, repair, identify, donations and cure disease: The Fighters Guild.

## Daedra summoning

Online guild and temple summoners list princes by name. Offline, they match the recorded day of year. The source describes fifteen of sixteen princes as annual summons, although its calendar lookup also includes Hircine's dated entry.

Glenmoril witches always select Hircine. Other covens draw a prince other than Hircine and remember the selection for the day; online that reroll uses the event clock, rather than the sky calendar.

The fee is 200000 - reputation  1000, using your standing with the summoner. Example: reputation 0 means 200,000 gold. Success uses the prince's separate reputation and weather bonus. Sheogorath can replace your selection. Failed attempts and repeat greetings cost gold; if no quest can be created in the region, you keep your money.

## Soul gems and Azura's Star

Buy Soulgems stocks empty and filled traps. Bought stock stays gone for the day. Filled traps supply Soul Bound; empty ones need captured souls.

Azura's Star is reusable: filling prefers an empty Star, while binding consumes an ordinary matching gem first. If only the Star supplies that soul, it empties and survives. See Enchanting, spellmaking and potions.

## Common mistakes

- Joining for one service without checking its rank or another temple's offer.
- Treating rank prestige as spendable gold: service access uses standing and rank, while the bill consumes its listed resources.
- Expecting the offline calendar to govern online guild summoners, or every coven to offer every prince.

## Next

- The NPC guilds
- Temples, The Thieves Guild, The Dark Brotherhood and Knightly orders for their own services
- Enchanting, spellmaking and potions
- Mages Guild teleport

docs.title: The Thieves Guild
docs.summary: How the guild invites you, what its hall trains, and which fence and spymaster services open at rank.
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - You cannot apply. The guild invites you after 10 thefts.
> - The invitation letter is stamped outside; online it arrives faster than the classic three-day wait.
> - The hall trains stealth skills and opens the fence at rank 2 and the spymaster at rank 4.
> - Joining reveals the guild hall on the town map.

## How you get in

The Thieves Guild has no application desk. Its tally counts thefts; at 10, it stamps an invitation letter. The initiation
starts only while you are outside, and the tally freezes while a letter is pending. It never fires twice. Joining
reveals the guild's hall on the town map.

The letter is a crime-guild invitation, not a courier questline letter. Online the wait is shorter than the classic
three-day delay. Thievery covers the theft tallies, stolen goods and the law.

## Rank and services

and 9 are chapter seats. Earned promotions apply when you open the hall's services.

| Service | What it does | Access |
|---|---|---|
| Training | Raise one guild skill | Member; 100 × character level a session |
| Quests | Guild work | Open |
| Sell Magic Items (fence) | Sell enchanted equipment | Rank 2 |
| Spymaster | Open an information conversation | Rank 4 |
| Buy/Make Potions, spells, magic items, soul gems, summoning | Not offered | Use a temple or the Mages Guild |

The hall trains Backstabbing, Blunt Weapon, Climbing, Dodging, Jumping, Lockpicking, Pickpocket, Short Blade, Stealth,
Streetwise and Swimming, up to skill 50. A session takes three game hours and is limited by the shared 12-game-hour
cooldown. The NPC guilds covers the price formula.

- Trying to apply at the hall instead of waiting for the tally.
- Carrying stolen goods into a court date; a conviction takes them.
- Expecting the fence or spymaster at rank 0.
- Looking for spellmaking or teleport at a guild hall; those are Mages Guild services.

docs.title: The law
docs.summary: Crimes affect the region where they happen; understand how the watch responds, what court can impose, and how standing recovers.
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Legal standing is tracked separately by region, and a crime is charged where it happens.
> - The watch responds when a crime is witnessed or otherwise detected; leaving the area does not erase its standing loss.
> - If a guard catches you, surrender takes you to court. A guilty plea reduces a fine or prison term; a not-guilty plea uses Debate or Lie.
> - A temple can help repair standing. Banishment restricts entry to the region until its term ends or a pardon is obtained.

## What counts as a crime

The law tracks offenses such as theft, breaking and entering, assault, murder, trespassing and vagrancy. The action and its detection rules vary: taking from a private container can be noticed when you close it, while attempting to force a locked door can attract attention. Some actions create a crime only if someone sees them. The game records legal standing for each region, so trouble in one region does not automatically become a charge everywhere.

## The watch

When a crime is witnessed, nearby townspeople or guards can raise the alarm. The watch pursues you in the town. A first minor offense may receive a warning in a region, but the crime still affects your standing. A known criminal can also be stopped by a wandering guard in the street and asked to answer the law.

If a guard lands a blow while you have an active crime, you can surrender or refuse. Refusing continues the chase. Surrender sets your health to 1 before court begins, so it is a way to end the pursuit, not a way to avoid the sentence.

## Court and recovery

At court, a guilty plea halves the fine and prison days for a fine-or-prison sentence. If you plead not guilty, choose Debate with Etiquette or Lie with Streetwise. The court makes a skill-based decision; an unsuccessful defense leaves the sentence in place. Banishment applies to particular serious crimes and bars you from that region for a period.

Paying or serving a sentence repairs much of the legal standing lost for the offense. Assault, Murder and treasonous offenses retain part of their mark. A temple's penance can restore standing, and negative standing also recovers over time. A regional temple can sell a pardon that lifts banishment early (the NPC guilds).

> [!warning] Curfew
> A town seat's Curfew edict doubles the legal-standing cost of crimes and strengthens the night watch. Keep the edict in mind after dark; the edict belongs to a town's seat (city control).

## Common mistakes

- Running or dying to end a chase. Getting away or dying ends the pursuit but does not repay the standing loss; answer the watch or court to repair it. Cost: a lasting legal mark in that region.
- Pleading guilty without checking what sticks. A guilty plea halves a fine or prison term, but Assault, Murder and treasonous offenses still keep part of their mark. Cost: standing you cannot get back cheaply.
- Ignoring an active Curfew. Under a Curfew edict crimes cost double legal standing and the night watch is stronger (city control). Cost: double the standing loss for a mistake after dark.

## Next

- Notice boards
- Time and weather

- Standing and reputation

what-counts-as-a-crime.title: What counts as a crime
what-counts-as-a-crime.excerpt: The law tracks offenses such as theft, breaking and entering, assault, murder, trespassing and vagrancy. The action and its detection rules vary: taking from a private container can be noticed when you close it, while attempting to force a locked door can attract attention. Some actions create a crime only if someone sees them. The game records legal standing for each region, so trouble in one region does not automatically become a charge everywhere.

the-watch.title: The watch
the-watch.excerpt: When a crime is witnessed, nearby townspeople or guards can raise the alarm. The watch pursues you in the town. A first minor offense may receive a warning in a region, but the crime still affects your standing. A known criminal can also be stopped by a wandering guard in the street and asked to answer the law.

court-and-recovery.title: Court and recovery
court-and-recovery.excerpt: At court, a guilty plea halves the fine and prison days for a fine-or-prison sentence. If you plead not guilty, choose Debate with Etiquette or Lie with Streetwise. The court makes a skill-based decision; an unsuccessful defense leaves the sentence in place. Banishment applies to particular serious crimes and bars you from that region for a period.

docs.title: Standing and reputation
docs.summary: The three standing tracks — People, regional law and guild faction — and how each moves, recovers and gates.
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - DFO keeps three separate tracks: People reputation (a region's townsfolk), legal standing (per region) and faction standing (guilds, temples, orders).
> - Faction and legal standing both run from −100 to 100; guild rank n needs faction standing 10 × n.
> - A quest pays its faction +5 for success and −2 for failure; a crime costs legal standing and half as much People standing.
> - Negative standing recovers one point every seven game days, and a temple penance buys five points back for 200 gold the first time.
> - A change to one faction can propagate: its allies move half the amount the same way, its enemies half the other way.

## Three kinds of standing

Players say "reputation" for three systems. They are stored separately, and improving one does not improve the others.

| Track | What it is | What reads it | What it gates |
|---|---|---|---|
| People | The regional population faction's view of you | Town talk: greetings and the chance of a useful answer | Directions, topics and how much a stranger will engage |
| Legal standing | Your record with the law, tracked per region | The watch, the court, banishment | Whether guards stop you, what a court does, entry to a region while banished |
| Faction standing | Your standing with a guild, temple, knightly order or other faction | Joining and promotion, services, rank tests | Guild membership, rank, some services and training |

The People track is not a shop-discount stat: shop offers come from the counter's own price law and your Mercantile and Personality. The People track is about conversation. See Talking to people and Shops and prices.

## What moves each track

### Quests

A quest's end pays the faction it was given for. The quest law's values are +5 for success and −2 for failure (questRepute.js QUESTSUCCESSREP, QUESTFAILUREREP). Individual quest scripts can also carry their own reputation actions (ChangeReputeWith). The handbook's design records state that failing a quest costs no faction standing online, so treat the −2 as the offline/default hook rather than a reliable penalty online.

### Crimes

A crime is charged to the region where it happens. Each crime has a fixed legal loss, and the region's People faction takes half of it, truncating down:

| Crime | Legal loss | People loss (half) |
|---|---:|---:|
| Vagrancy | 1 | 0 |
| Trespassing, Smuggling, Piracy, Pickpocketing, Criminal conspiracy | 2 | 1 |
| Theft, Assault, Attempted breaking and entering, Breaking and entering, Tax evasion, Loan default | 8–10 | 4–5 |
| Murder | 20 | 10 |
| Treason | 36 | 18 |
| High treason | 75 | 37 |

A town Curfew doubles the legal loss only; the People's half stays as it is. See The law and City control.

### Faction service and propagation

A successful guild or temple service can move its faction: a temple donation has a chance to add one point of reputation, where the chance is 2 × the gift ÷ max(|current standing|, 1) + 1 percent (guildServiceActions.js). A faction reputation change can also propagate: allies take half the change the same direction, enemies half the opposite direction, and the walk climbs a faction's hierarchy. Helping one temple can therefore cool its enemies toward you without your doing anything to them.

### Bounty contracts

Finishing a bounty contract for a region's board improves that region's legal standing by two points (standing.js CONTRACTLEGALGAIN). It is one of the few voluntary ways to repair a legal record.

## How standing recovers

- Time. Negative legal and faction standing each recover one point every seven game days (court.js RECOVERYINTERVALMINUTES). This runs on the character's clock and continues across an absence — online time model's recovery-only walk. Positive standing instead drifts one point down toward zero every 112 game days of lived play (NORMALIZEINTERVALMINUTES); an absence does not wear a positive standing down.
- A sentence. Serving or paying a court sentence returns about half the crime's legal loss, minus one (court.js sentence refund). A fine-plus-prison sentence can refund twice, a classic quirk the port keeps.
- A temple penance. A temple sells penance that moves five points of the region's legal standing back toward zero, never past it. The first costs 200 gold in a region and the n-th costs n times that (standing.js PENANCEPOINTS, PENANCEBASEPRICE).
- A pardon. Murder and treason can bring banishment. A temple sells a pardon that lifts it early; the first costs 2,500 gold and the n-th n times as much (PARDONBASEPRICE). The banishment itself is timed: thirty days on the calendar you see online (BANISHMENTMINUTES).

## What each track gates

- Guild joining needs non-negative standing with the faction and two qualifying guild skills (guilds.js isEligibleToJoin). See The NPC guilds.
- Guild rank needs faction standing 0, 10, 20 … 90 for ranks 0–9 (RANKREQREPUTATION), plus the rank's skill bars. Online, an earned promotion applies immediately when you open the services.
- Legal standing decides how the watch treats you, what the court imposes and whether you may enter a banished region.
- People standing decides how much a townsperson is willing to tell you. It does not change shop prices.

## Practical standing habits

1. Take the court, do not run. Leaving or dying ends the chase but not the record; a plea or a served sentence repairs part of it.
2. Use the board for a region you need. A finished bounty contract is +2 legal standing in that region.
3. Bank a penance before a big purchase. Five points for 200 gold is cheaper than the standing you lose by being refused a guild hall.
4. Watch your allies. A temple favour can lower a rival temple's standing with you; check the faction before donating heavily.
5. Do not expect a positive score to last. Lived play wears positive standing down toward zero; only negative standing drifts back.

## Common mistakes

- Treating the three tracks as one number. A guild that likes you does not make the town watch forgive a crime.
- Running from the watch. The pursuit ends; the legal mark stays until a sentence or time repairs it.
- Donating without reading the chance. The donation's chance falls as your standing rises, so large gifts to a faction that already likes you are poor value.
- Ignoring propagation. A change to one faction can move its allies and enemies; a favour for one temple is a statement about another.
- Assuming a high positive score is permanent. It drifts down every 112 game days of play.

## Next

- The NPC guilds
- The law

docs.title: Notice boards
docs.summary: Read town notices and bounty listings, or use the Work board to find and post player commissions.
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - The Notice board shows town news, a pointer to the separate Bounty Board where one is available, server notices and player notes.
> - The Work tab shows Court and regional guild writs, plus crafting commissions; its forms are separate from reading notes.
> - Player notes can stay up for one, three or seven days, and one account may keep three live notes across boards.
> - Read the terms on a listing before accepting work; the board is a meeting point, not a guarantee of a particular reward.

## Read the board

Use the physical notice board to browse town news, server notices and player notes. Where the town has a separate Bounty Board, its notice points you there to read the hunts (how money is earned). A town's notice boards share the same set of player notes, so a note posted at one board is visible from its other notice boards. The window marks items that are new to you.

Player notes have a subject and body, a chosen lifespan of one, three or seven days, and may carry one response button. The available buttons can ask to join the author's party or guild (meeting other players), challenge them to a duel, or open a commission form. The request still goes through the normal party, guild, duel or crafting rules.

## Work and commissions

Open the Work tab to browse Court and regional guild writs, as well as crafting commissions. A commission names a crafter, a piece, its minimum quality and the pay. You can fill or decline commissions addressed to you, and post one yourself. A player note's Commission a piece button opens the form with that note's author named. Review the terms before you post or fill a commission.

You can keep up to three of your own notes live across all boards. Choose a duration that fits the message, and take down an old note when it no longer applies. A note can also be reported; the system hides a note from everyone after enough eligible reports while it waits for moderation.

> [!tip] Finding work
> The Bounty Board and the Work tab serve different purposes. Read the listing type and its terms before you set out or deliver an item.

## Common mistakes

- Posting the same announcement at several boards. One account may keep only three live notes across all boards, so duplicate posts use the slots your other notices need. Cost: a notice expires before anyone acts on it.
- Accepting a Work listing without reading its terms. Court and guild writs, bounties and crafting commissions take different deliveries and pay from different boards; a trip begun for the wrong listing costs the journey.
- Letting a note reach the report threshold. A reported note is hidden from everyone while it waits for moderation (meeting other players); a recruitment or commission note can vanish before it is answered. Cost: the deal falls through.

## Next

- Courier letters
- Talking to people

docs.title: Meeting other players
docs.summary: Chat channels, finding a group, parties, shared kills and mentor mode.
headings: Find a group and travel together
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Use Local for nearby players, Region for your region, or World to reach everyone online.
> - Join Trade or LFG when you want those opt-in channels.
> - Invite people into a party for shared play; party members keep individual quest progress.
> - Use /block to hide a player's chat and requests, and /report to report conduct.

## Choose a channel

DFO chat separates messages by audience. /world or /g reaches everyone online; /region or /r reaches your region; /local, /l, /say or /s reaches nearby players. /party and /guild stay with those groups. Trade and LFG are opt-in: use /join trade or /join lfg to listen and speak there, and /leave trade or /leave lfg to leave one. The chat panel shows the channels available to you.

## Find a group and travel together

Post in LFG to look for companions, then invite players from the Social panel. A party can hold 8 accounts including you. Invitations expire after two minutes. Each member retains their own quest state when a shareable quest is copied to them; questline steps cannot be shared.

When several party members fight the same foe, recent attackers count toward the shared encounter's scaling. Renown from a kill is not divided among the party. For a journey to the leader, see Party travel.

## Keep control of contact

/block, /unblock and /blocked manage who can reach you through chat, requests and invitations. A block hides that player's lines and requests from you; the other player is not told. Use /report  or a chat line's Report action for player conduct. /bug opens a private developer report form.

> [!note] Shared containers
> Some dungeon containers have a shared base list. Taking an item from that list can change what remains for other players; personal bonus loot is separate.

## Next

- Party travel
- Tavern games

- Play with a friend

docs.title: Play with a friend
docs.summary: Add a friend, form a party, share kills and quests, and leave the group safely.
headings: Mentor mode: the safety net for mixed levels
Step 4: what is shared and what is not
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Friends and parties live in the Social interface beside the chat panel.
> - A party holds up to 8 accounts. An invitation expires after 2 minutes.
> - Every party member in the room earns the whole kill; Renown gains +10% per extra member.
> - Mentor mode switches on automatically for a much higher-level member, so you can play together without trivialising the content.
> - Questline steps cannot be shared. Shareable quests give each member their own copy and their own progress.

## Before you start

You both need to be online and in the shared world. DFO is one world rather than a set of lobbies: there is no "server select" step, and the game keeps friends and parties as account relationships (server/src/index.js is the social hub; src/net/social.js is the client's picture). Guest accounts can play; whether a guest can hold friends and join parties is not stated in the source, so treat registration as the reliable route for social play (see Your account).

You will also want a place to meet that is easy to describe: a town's gate, a tavern or a guild hall. The world is large, and the travel tools are faster once you are in a party.

## Step 1: add a friend

Open the Social panel, the button beside the chat panel, and use the friends area.

1. Send a friend request by account or name.
2. The other player accepts or declines from the same panel.
3. Once accepted, the friend's row shows whether they are online or when they were last online.

The source's limits are one home for the whole list: 64 friends and 32 pending requests each way (src/net/wire.js: FRIENDSMAX, PENDINGMAX). A blocked account's friend request, party invitation and notes never land, and are taken back if they were already waiting when you blocked them (src/net/social.js: the block behaviour; /block, /unblock, /blocked).

## Step 2: form the party

1. From the friends row, choose Invite to send a party invitation. Any party member may invite, not only the leader (src/net/social.js: actionsFor, "any member may invite - the hub's law").
2. The other player accepts from the Party tab or from the invitation toast.
3. A party holds at most 8 accounts, including you (src/net/wire.js: PARTYMAX).
4. An invitation is good for 2 minutes (INVITETTLMS); after that it lapses and must be sent again.

The Party tab is also where the group lives: it shows the members, their poses (health, fatigue and spell points), who is online, and the leader controls. The leader can kick a member or make another member leader; any member can leave the party (src/ui/socialPanel.js: the party rows and their buttons). Party members' names are drawn green over the world (src/net/social.js: PARTYGREEN).

## Step 3: meet and travel together

The fastest way to gather is party travel:

- /leader offers to take you to your party leader. You pay your own fare and arrive beside them, or at the door if they are inside (src/systems/party/partyTravel.js).
- The leader can call a party journey with /travel. Followers have 30 seconds to join. If you miss the window, fall back to /leader.
- Party travel arrives at the world's present and does not advance world time, and it cannot cross into or out of the Open Zone or across the Veil (src/systems/party/partyTravelLaw.js: TRIPFOLLOWMS, fare and boundary rules).

For ordinary walking, the middle mouse button drops a party ping: a mark for your party for 5 seconds, and a route for 12 (reference/keys-and-commands.md). Waypoints you place can be shared with your party (src/ui/waypointMenu.js: "Your party sees it").

### Mentor mode: the safety net for mixed levels

If one of you is much higher level, the game becomes the mentor automatically. A party is measured by a reference level that leans toward its lowest member; when that reference is at least 3 levels below yours, you fight as the reference level and your real progress is kept (src/systems/mentorMode.js: MENTORMINGAP, mentorTargetLevel, mentorProfile). You do not need to switch anything on, and /mentor prints whether you are mentoring.

This is what makes "play with a friend who is new" practical: the high-level character does not delete the content, and the low-level character does not get carried by numbers alone.

## Step 4: what is shared and what is not

| Thing | How it works |
|---|---|
| Kills | Every party member in the room earns the whole kill rather than a split. Renown gains +10% per extra member (src/net/renown.js: RENOWNPARTYBONUSPCT, renownPartyXp; docs/23-playing-online.md, "Group up with the strong players"). |
| Quest progress | A shareable quest is copied to each member; each member keeps their own quest state. Questline steps cannot be shared (src/systems/quest/questShare.js; town/meeting-players.md). |
| Quest dungeons | A quest's dungeon can be opened as your instance, a copy for you and your party, at full size (docs/23-playing-online.md, "Dungeons without the crowds"; src/scenes/instanceDoor.js). |
| Loot | Some containers have a shared base list: taking from it can change what remains for the others. Personal bonus loot is separate (src/scenes/roomLootHost.js). Loose loot in a public dungeon is first come (docs/23-playing-online.md). |
| Party rest | /ready explains the party rest state online; resting together is a party action rather than a solo one (reference/keys-and-commands.md). |

The party does not share a bank, a purse or a quest log. Loot etiquette — who takes what — is a player agreement, not a rule the game enforces. If a shared container matters, say what you are taking.

## Step 5: leave safely

1. Finish in a safe place. Party travel follows the leader; if you leave the party deep in a dungeon, you will walk out yourself. Leave at a town, a port or a cleared entrance.
2. Use Leave party. The button is in the Party tab. A leader who leaves should hand leadership over first if the group is continuing; the Party tab has the Make leader button (src/ui/socialPanel.js: party rows, Make leader, Leave party).
3. Say goodbye. There is no need to drop the group to log off. Your character checkpoints as you go; the party simply sees you offline.
4. If someone is harassing you. Block them (/block) and report them (/report); blocked accounts cannot send you requests, invitations or notes. Use /bug for a private report to the developers, or the project's issue tracker and Discord for a fault (see Troubleshooting for the reporting routes).

## Unverified or unstated

- The source does not state a dedicated key for the Social panel; the panel is described as a button beside the chat UI.
- The source does not state whether a guest account can hold friends or join a party; registration is the safe assumption for social play.
- The source does not state that party kills share character XP; the documented full-kill and +10% rule is the Renown reward.
- Party composition rules at the level of classes or roles are not stated; any mix is allowed by the party law.

## Common mistakes

- Inviting a player who is offline. The request needs a tab in the world; offline friends cannot accept.
- Letting the invitation expire. Two minutes pass while you are still in a dungeon.
- Assuming the leader pays for party travel. Each travelling member pays their own fare.
- Expecting a shared questline step. Questline steps are personal; only shareable quests copy.
- Leaving the party at the bottom of a dungeon. You lose the easy way back to the group.

## Next

- Meeting other players
- Party travel

docs.title: Courier letters
docs.summary: Questline letters arrive on a paced schedule and only reach you outdoors in a town during the day.
headings: What to do when you are waiting
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - A questline's next step waits one character hour after the previous step ends.
> - New lines are paced too: the runner will not start one while another line's letter is still on its way.
> - A courier can deliver only when you are outdoors in a town by day.
> - If a letter cannot find you, it stays pending; the questline window tells you what it is waiting for.

## When letters arrive

Questlines use letters to introduce their next step. After a step ends, its line waits one hour of character time before the next step can begin. Opening several lines does not make their first letters arrive together: the runner spaces new lines and letters by an hour and waits for a pending first letter to reach you.

Delivery has a place and time requirement. Be outdoors in a town during the day. A courier that reaches you somewhere else does not complete delivery, and the letter remains on its way until the conditions are met.

## What to do when you are waiting

Open the Quests view to see a line's steps and its current wait. You can keep playing while a letter is pending; return to a town street during daylight when you want to receive it. A letter wait is different from a quest deadline. Online, quest delays marked for the shared clock are shortened; deadlines keep their full length and run only while you play. See the later questline ladder for the broader system.

## Next

- Time and weather
- The NPC guilds

docs.title: Time and weather
docs.summary: Read the game clock for daylight and service hours, and use the weather and season as context for travel and outdoor conditions.
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - The game day has daylight from 6:00 to 18:00; darkness begins before 6:00 and from 18:00 onward.
> - Online, the shared world clock advances while you play. Waiting, resting and journeys can move your character's time forward.
> - Weather includes clear, overcast, fog, rain, thunder and snow; the enhanced lane can also produce desert sandstorms.
> - Weather and season affect the sky and light. Use the travel forecast before choosing a long outdoor route.

## Day and night

The day-night cycle controls daylight, street lighting and the classic building schedule. Online, service hours are relieved for shops, banks, libraries, palaces and guild halls, and city gates remain open at night. Other rules still use time: couriers need daylight for delivery, and travel, rest and quest clocks can move forward.

The shared online clock advances in the world while you are playing (world events and their clock). A fast carriage trip advances your character's clock by the trip length; a party trip to its leader arrives at the world's present. Check the travel method before assuming all trips spend the same time.

## Weather and seasons

Weather changes the sky and outdoor light. Rain and thunder darken daylight, snow and overcast skies reduce it, and fog affects visibility. A sandstorm is a desert weather condition in the enhanced lane. The calendar season also affects the sky and can change the weather conditions a region can produce.

Weather is not a travel timer or a promise that a road is safe. Check the route view's forecast and pace controls, then decide whether to travel now or use a different route. See overworld travel.

## Common mistakes

- Planning around a still clock. A carriage trip advances your character's clock by the journey even though you arrive instantly, so an errand timed for daylight can arrive after dark; party travel does not spend world time (world events and their clock). Cost: a missed courier window or event.
- Treating a forecast as a safety guarantee. Weather changes light and visibility, not the danger of the place or the length of the journey; a storm-darkened road still holds the same foes. Cost: a fight you did not prepare for.
- Travelling at night when a questline letter is due. Couriers hand letters over in a town, outdoors, by day (courier letters); a night in the wilds or in a dungeon holds that line back. Cost: a day of questline delay.

## Next

- Courier letters
- Overworld travel

Online, service hours are relieved for shops, banks, libraries, palaces and guild halls, and city gates remain open at night. Other rules still use time: couriers need daylight for delivery, and travel, rest and quest clocks can move forward.

A sandstorm is a desert weather condition in the enhanced lane. The calendar season also affects the sky and can change the weather conditions a region can produce.

docs.title: Overworld travel
docs.summary: Plot a walked route across the Iliac Bay, adjust its pace, and account for road, terrain and encounter settings.
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Use the Overworld Travel View to plot a route over roads, tracks and open ground.
> - The route planner favors roads, then tracks, then open ground; a direct cross-country line may take longer.
> - Set a travel pace and a slower near-enemy pace. The default pace dial is ×60 and the default near-enemy pace is ×5; ground and Open Zone caps can lower the active pace.
> - Cautious travel is slower but can avoid an encounter; reckless travel uses the normal journey-time calculation.

## Plan a route

Road, track, open-ground and carriage routes with pace caps

Choose your destination in the Overworld Travel View (the map and danger). The route planner weighs roads most cheaply, tracks more heavily and open ground most heavily. A longer road route can therefore be faster in the travel calculation than a short cross-country cut. Towns are crossed through their streets and gates rather than treated as open ground.

Walking costs no fare; the hired carriages page covers the paid shortcut. Your displayed pace is separate from the classic travel-time calculation: the pace controls how quickly the character moves through the active route, while the route and transport determine how much game time the trip represents. A horse changes your physical pace, not the route.

## Set your pace

The pace dial offers ×5, ×10, ×20, ×30, ×40, ×60 and ×100. Outside the Open Zone, roads and tracks allow ×100 and open ground caps the active pace at ×60. In the Open Zone, the caps are ×40 on roads or tracks and ×20 on open ground. Leaving a road or track caps the running pace without erasing your chosen dial, which returns when you reach one. The near-enemy dial controls your slowest pace when a threat is close.

In Travel Options, Speed Penalty defaults to 20%, and Max Chance to Avoid Encounter defaults to 95%. Cautious travel's avoidance roll uses Luck and Stealth up to that cap. Reckless travel does not reduce the calculated trip time or provide Cautious travel's encounter avoidance. Review the pace and caution choices before setting out.

The wilderness between towns is also where spawned dungeons appear, so a walked route can be an exploration trip rather than only a way to arrive.

> [!tip] Leaving town
> City gates stay open online. A walked route through town therefore does not stop at a night gate.

## Common mistakes

- Taking the straight line because it looks shorter. The planner prices roads cheapest, tracks next and open ground most, so a longer road route can be faster. Cost: travel time on every trip.
- Leaving the pace dial at its fastest through bad ground. Leaving a road or track caps the active pace (×60 outside the Open Zone) without changing your setting. Cost: a fast trip runs slower than you planned.
- Using Cautious travel for every leg. Cautious is slower and only adds its encounter-avoidance roll; using it on safe roads spends session time. Cost: fewer activities per hour.

## Next

- The map and danger
- Hired carriages

docs.title: Danger and regions
docs.summary: How a place's kind sets its danger, the Bay's regions compared, and how to open and read both maps.
headings: Danger comes from the place, not the distance
The regions and what they offer
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Danger comes from the kind of place, not the distance you have travelled.
> - Towns, mines and natural caves are gentlest; a crypt, vampire haunt or dragon's den is several grades up.
> - Online the sky runs a day every real hour, so the wilds are safer by day than at night.
> - The Wrothgarian Mountains are the Open Zone: PvP, ×4 foes, and a death that can strip your pack.

## Danger comes from the place, not the distance

Distance does not make foes stronger; the kind of place does. Every dungeon kind has a fixed grade, and the grade drives the foes and the loot: a crypt near home is as dangerous as one across the Bay. Online, Loot Rarity is forced on and the grade comes from that ladder; The map and danger covers routes.

## The danger grades

| Grade | Places | Foe health | Foe damage |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| 4 (base) | Towns, mines, natural caves | ×1 | ×1 |
| 5 | Prisons, spider and scorpion nests, the wilds by day | ×1.07 | ×1.02 |
| 7 | Harpy nests, the wilds at night | ×1.21 | ×1.05 |
| 9 | Crypts, orc strongholds | ×1.36 | ×1.09 |
| 11 | Barbarian strongholds | ×1.50 | ×1.13 |
| 14 | Vampire haunts | ×1.71 | ×1.18 |
| 15 | Desecrated temples | ×1.79 | ×1.20 |
| 18 | Dragon's dens, volcanic caves | ×2.00 | ×1.25 |

Other kinds sit between: cemetery 3, human stronghold or ruined castle 6, giant stronghold 8, laboratory 10, coven 13; a town's ground is base grade. The place multiplies a foe that is already a threat — a rat in a vampire haunt stays a rat, while a class foe built at your level takes the full step — and from level 10 and Renown 15 a second layer answers you too (The hero's threat). The same grade also sets rare loot odds.

## Day and night

Online the sky runs a day every real hour, midnight on the hour. The wilds read grade 5 by day and 7 at night.

## The Open Zone

The Wrothgarian Mountains are the one region with open player-versus-player combat. Every foe there stands at ×4 health and blows; the inner rings multiply that and the loot, ×1.25 in The Foothills to ×2 in The Heart, so ×5–×8. A death there drops eligible bag and cart pieces and half your carried gold, and a player who kills you may take one worn piece; consumables and the wallet stay. See The Open Zone.

## The regions and what they offer

Region names are geographic, not a difficulty switch; the danger follows the places you enter.

| Area | What it offers | Early caution |
|---|---|---|
| Daggerfall, Wayrest and the crown cities | Town services, guilds, banks; the Arena; the LeFay Monument | Safest ground; the routes out begin the wilds |
| High Rock interior and forests (Dwynnen, Northmoor, Menevia, Ravennian, Malekna) | Settled country, roads, dungeons, woodland logging and herbs | Stay on the roads and travel by day |
| Hammerfell crown, Alik'r Desert, Dragontail Mountains, Dak'fron | Sentinel, a port and early destination; ore and herbs | Long land distances; desert pixels have no trees |
| The Marches: Betony, Anticlere, Lainlyn | Every gathering node pays +25% | Contested: the bonus comes with danger |
| Jungle of Bantha (Lainlyn, Satakalaam, Mournoth) | The southern logging destination | A far southern trip; prepare first |
| Wrothgarian Mountains, Orsinium Area, Devilrock | Mountain country and Orichalcum; the Open Zone | Stay out of the Open Zone while you are new |

## Where to go first

- Renown and gear: towns, your quests' private instances and a town-raid party (Spawned and Elite dungeons); then the Arena, town defence and the later group content.
- Materials and money: nearby confirmed pixels (timber and herbs in woodland, ore in mountains and deserts), sold where town prices are good, then banked.

## Open and read the map

One map window has three sheets: automap, town and world; which a place offers follows where you stand.

| Key | Default action | What you get |
|---|---|---|
| M | AutoMap | The map where you stand: explored dungeon or building plan, town map, or world sheet in the wilds |
| V | TravelMap | The same window opened with the world sheet chosen, where it is available |

Inside a dungeon or building only the automap; in a town the town and world sheets; in the wilderness only the world, with tabs that do not apply dimmed. V picks a destination; the Overworld Travel View is a separate route plotter, unbound by default (Overworld travel).

The world map lists only discovered places, so an unvisited dungeon is not on it; spawned dungeons are found by leaving the road. The entry plaque names the place and, online, its room tier (Regular Dungeon, Elite Dungeon or Abyss Dungeon) — not the base kind: a Regular Dungeon can be a crypt.

## Common mistakes

- Avoiding a far mine while entering the crypt next door. The crypt is harder.
- Reading the online tier as the base kind. Elite and Abyss are room tiers.
- Expecting the map to mark every dungeon. It shows discovered places only.

## Next

- The map and danger
- Overworld travel

docs.title: The map and danger
docs.summary: Use the world map to choose a destination and route, then treat terrain, location type and nearby threats as separate parts of risk.
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - The world map organizes the Iliac Bay into regions and map locations; use the place names and route overlay to orient yourself.
> - Road, track and open-ground routes have different travel costs, so the shortest line is not always the quickest trip.
> - A town, wilderness encounter and dungeon entrance are different kinds of risk; check what your destination is before entering.
> - The Overworld View draws nearby pursuit and encounters around your route. A chase is not the same as a destination marker.

## Read the map

Choose a named place on the world map to set a destination. The route overlay shows how the journey crosses roads, tracks and open ground. Region boundaries, climate and location types help you understand where you are headed (danger and regions); they do not by themselves tell you the strength of every opponent inside a location.

The map also distinguishes settlements from other destinations. A road journey can pass through a town, while a dungeon or other location begins a separate visit. Some places appear only after they are discovered or made available by the game's world systems.

## Think about danger

Treat travel risk in layers. The route exposes you to travel encounters and possible pursuit (overworld travel); the destination determines the location you enter; and the enemies within it follow that place's own rules. Slow down near a chase, use Cautious travel if you want its encounter-avoidance roll, and check the destination before committing to a trip.

This page does not assign one fixed danger rating to every map pixel. Spawned sites and dungeon tiers can depend on world state and system rules. See the later Spawned and Elite dungeons guide for those destinations.

## Common mistakes

- Choosing a dungeon by distance rather than type. Danger comes from what kind of place you enter, not how far from town it is; a nearby crypt can be far worse than a distant mine (danger and regions). Cost: a death and one tenth of the carried purse.
- Walking into the Wrothgarian Mountains as ordinary wilderness. The Open Zone adds open PvP and much stronger foes; the map does not mark every risk at its edge (the Open Zone). Cost: carried items and cart contents.
- Following a chase marker as if it were a destination. The Overworld draws pursuit and encounters around your route; chasing one can pull you off the path into harder ground. Cost: time and a fight you chose by accident.

## Next

- Hired carriages
- Horses

docs.title: Hired carriages
docs.summary: The carriage driver outside a walled city's gate sells instant land travel for a small daily fare.
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Carriages stand just outside the gate of walled cities. Hamlets and villages never have one.
> - Talk to the driver and choose Fast Travel, then pick a destination on the driver's map.
> - The default fare is 1 gold per travel day, plus 1 gold. The fare screen shows the exact price before you pay.
> - You arrive at once, but your character's clock moves forward by the length of the trip.

## Where to find a carriage

A carriage driver waits with a carriage and horses outside the gate of a walled city. Only four kinds of city-gate
block hold a driver (the gate blocks WALLAA08 to WALLAA11), so only some cities have one. Every place with one is a
city; no hamlet or village does.

You board at the gate, not at the town's Stable or Wagon Yard: those sell horses and wagons you drive yourself.

> [!tip] Finding the nearest one
> Large walled cities are the place to look. The handbook's map can filter places by service, including carriages.

## Taking a trip

1. Walk out through the city gate and find the driver beside the carriage.
2. Talk to the driver and choose Fast Travel.
3. Pick a destination on the map. Online, the shipped settings allow cities, hamlets and villages, not only other
   carriage cities.
4. Read the fare and confirm. The game then performs a Daggerfall-style fast trip.

If you chose inn stops in the travel options, the fare includes inn charges. A long journey that crosses water can
include a ship fare when ship travel is selected and enabled.

## What it costs

The fare has a daily part and an optional inn part:

- a daily carriage fee for each whole day of land travel, plus one more daily fee;
- inn charges, if you chose to stop at inns.

The daily fee is a setting that defaults to 1 gold. With inns off and default settings, a trip costs 1 gold plus 1
gold for each complete travel day.

> [!example] Example
> A trip the game calculates at 3 whole travel days, with inns off and the default fee, costs 1 + 3 = 4 gold.

## Time passes

The trip is instant for you, but the world's clock for your character moves on by the trip's length. Shops may have
closed and the day may have turned by the time you arrive. A walked overworld route spends that time as you travel instead.

## Limits

- Online, regional carriage restrictions are off by default, so a valid destination is not limited to the current
  region. The shipped destination types still apply.
- Fast travel can't enter or leave the Wrothgarian Mountains Open Zone (a later area).

## Common mistakes

- Waiting for a carriage in a village or hamlet. Only walled cities with the right gate blocks have a driver; every place with one is a city. Cost: a long walk or a missed trip.
- Expecting the Stable or Wagon Yard to sell the carriage trip. Those sell horses and wagons you drive yourself; the carriage is a separate driver outside the gate (horses, wagons and hauling). Cost: gold spent on the wrong purchase.
- Forgetting that the fare moves your clock. You arrive at once, but the trip advances your character's time by its length, so an errand timed for daylight can arrive after dark. Cost: a missed courier window or event.

## Next

- Horses
- Ships and passage
