docs.title: Mods, saves and wipes
docs.summary: No mods and no save import, where progress lives, and what is known about wipes and seasons.
headings: Mods: no, and why the answer is firm
Wipes and seasons: what is actually known
If you lose access or a save
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - DFO Online does not support mods. You cannot install DFU or Nexus mods, and the game fixes its own ruleset for online play.
> - You cannot import a classic Daggerfall or Daggerfall Unity save yet. DFO characters are made in DFO.
> - Progress lives in one of three places: browser save slots, desktop-app save files, or your online character on the account service.
> - Cloud backup is a manual action, not an automatic sync.
> - The source and the official site set no wipe schedule. Character deletion is manual and permanent.

## Mods: no, and why the answer is firm

The official site says it plainly: there is no mod support (https://daggerfalljs.dev/, "Not finished"; index.html). There is no mod folder, no load order, no Nexus integration and no DFU mod compatibility. A player arriving from Daggerfall Unity should not copy a modlist across, because the client will not load it.

The Features rows are not mods. They are the game's own built-in systems and settings, registered in one place (src/systems/features.js) and drawn as tiles on the Features page. Some are the port's own work, some are built-in versions of familiar mods, and some are cosmetic. Online, their scope is decided for everyone:

- Shared and balance systems are forced on at shipped values: the world mods, PCAAO, Meaner Monsters, Enemy Expansion, Unleveled Loot, Roleplay & Realism and its Items (src/systems/online/onlineLane.js: ONLINEROOMMODKEYS, ONLINEWHOLEMODS).
- Personal switches — looks, sound, survival tier, horse care, wagon upkeep and a few similar settings — remain the player's (ONLINEPLAYERSOWNMODS; the Features registry's online: 'player' declarations).
- Offline, the same Features rows follow your own choices, because an offline game is yours.

Which rules apply online is the index to which is which. The practical answer for a mod question is always the same: if the feature is in DFO, it is a Feature row; if it is a downloaded mod, it does not exist here.

## Save import: not yet

The official site's exact words are that you cannot import classic or Daggerfall Unity saves yet (index.html). There is no converter and no character transfer from another Daggerfall install. A DFO character is created in DFO, in either an offline slot or an online account slot.

Two doors do exist between DFO's own modes: an offline DFO character can be brought online once, and an online character can be copied to offline as a new local character (src/ui/enhanced/enhancedMenu.js: "Bring an offline character in (once)", copyToOffline). Neither door imports a save from another game.

## Where your progress lives

There are three stores, and they do not merge by themselves:

| Store | What lives there | What it follows |
|---|---|---|
| Browser save slots | Offline characters made in that browser | That browser's storage only |
| Desktop-app save files | Offline characters made in the app | The files you keep and back up |
| Online character checkpoint | Your online character, its quest state and account records | The account service and your account |

The browser/desktop distinction is on the official site: browser saves are in the browser's storage, while the desktop app keeps real files you can back up (https://daggerfalljs.dev/, "Saves" and "The desktop app"). The local slots themselves are filed under the first free slot number (src/systems/save/saveSlots.js), which is why two devices can hold the same character under different numbers.

An online character is different in kind. It is checkpointed by the account service as you play and on exit, and it is chosen from the Online menu's character list (src/scenes/world.js: online checkpoints, exit autosave; src/ui/enhanced/enhancedMenu.js: the Online pane). Local browser slots and the online character are separate records; opening an offline save is not a way to rewind an online session.

For the full save behaviour, including what closing the tab does, see Saving and returning.

## Cloud backup is manual

There is a third destination, the cloud save, and it is deliberately not automatic. The cloud save is an explicit backup action, not a live sync: a slot is identified by the character and the save name (not the local slot number), it is skipped rather than duplicated when the store already holds it, and nothing here resolves conflicts by picking a winner (src/systems/cloudSaves.js: the header states the design and the reasons). Two devices that saved in a different order can hold the same QuickSave under different local numbers; what travels is the character identity.

The consequence is simple: if you want a backup, take it. The game will not quietly take one for you.

## Cross-device play

- Online characters follow the account. Sign in on another device and your online character is there (src/ui/enhanced/enhancedMenu.js: the Online pane reads the service's characters).
- Browser offline characters do not follow you. Another browser or the desktop app has its own store.
- Desktop-app offline characters are files; copy them if you want them elsewhere.
- Cloud backups are the supported way to move an offline slot; because the operation is manual, the copy is the one you asked for.

## Wipes and seasons: what is actually known

The source and the official site do not state a wipe policy. I found no automated character wipe, no launch-reset schedule and no seasonal character reset in the code or on the site. The official page says the game is not finished and points to the project ledger for what remains (https://daggerfalljs.dev/, "Not finished"); that is a statement about completeness, not a wipe plan. If a wipe policy is ever set, it must come from an announcement, not from this page.

What does exist is seasonal standing, not seasonal characters:

- Arena seasons last eight weeks from a configured UTC epoch, with a rating ladder; a new season changes standings, not characters (src/net/arena/arenaLaw.js; Arena seasons).
- City-control seasons last eight weeks; at the end Standing moves halfway back to 50, Legacy clears and each fortification drops a tier, but Charters remain (src/net/townSeatLaw.js: SEASONWEEKS; City control).
- Starfall is a festival event with its own calendar and rewards, not a reset of characters (src/net/festivalLaw.js, src/net/starfall/starfallLaw.js).

Character deletion is the one permanent, player-triggered reset, and the game warns before it: deleting an online character is permanent, and its Renown, professions, Stores, homes it bought and guild place are lost; homes belong to the account, so your other characters lose them too, while any offline copy you made stays (src/ui/enhanced/enhancedMenu.js: the delete-character warning). Treat deletion as final.

## If you lose access or a save

- Registered account: use a saved recovery code to get back in. Recovery codes are credentials, not character backups; they restore access, not a deleted character (server-account/src/accounts.js: recovery set).
- Guest account: the guest lives with the browser session, so clearing site data can remove the way back (begin/your-account.md).
- Offline slot: check the other store first — the browser or the app may be the one holding it — then the cloud backup if you made one.
- Bug or crash: reload first, then the project's issue tracker or Discord (https://daggerfalljs.dev/, "If it breaks").

## Common mistakes

- Installing a mod. DFO does not load external mods; a copied DFU modlist changes nothing.
- Expecting a DFU save import. Import is not available yet.
- Assuming the cloud is syncing. It is an explicit backup; take it or do not have one.
- Playing a browser offline character on another device. It is in that browser's store, not on your account.
- Believing a season will reset your character. Seasons reset standings, not characters; no wipe schedule is stated.
- Deleting a character to "start fresh online". The warning is permanent; an offline copy is the only thing that survives.

mods-no-and-why-the-answer-is-firm.title: Mods: no, and why the answer is firm
mods-no-and-why-the-answer-is-firm.excerpt: The official site says it plainly: there is no mod support (https://daggerfalljs.dev/, "Not finished"; index.html). There is no mod folder, no load order, no Nexus integration and no DFU mod compatibility. A player arriving from Daggerfall Unity should not copy a modlist across, because the client will not load it.

save-import-not-yet.title: Save import: not yet
save-import-not-yet.excerpt: The official site's exact words are that you cannot import classic or Daggerfall Unity saves yet (index.html). There is no converter and no character transfer from another Daggerfall install. A DFO character is created in DFO, in either an offline slot or an online account slot.

where-your-progress-lives.title: Where your progress lives
where-your-progress-lives.excerpt: There are three stores, and they do not merge by themselves:

cloud-backup-is-manual.title: Cloud backup is manual
cloud-backup-is-manual.excerpt: There is a third destination, the cloud save, and it is deliberately not automatic. The cloud save is an explicit backup action, not a live sync: a slot is identified by the character and the save name (not the local slot number), it is skipped rather than duplicated when the store already holds it, and nothing here resolves conflicts by picking a winner (src/systems/cloudSaves.js: the header states the design and the reasons). Two devices that saved in a different order can hold the same QuickSave under different local numbers; what travels is the character identity.

wipes-and-seasons-what-is-actually-known.title: Wipes and seasons: what is actually known
wipes-and-seasons-what-is-actually-known.excerpt: The source and the official site do not state a wipe policy. I found no automated character wipe, no launch-reset schedule and no seasonal character reset in the code or on the site. The official page says the game is not finished and points to the project ledger for what remains (https://daggerfalljs.dev/, "Not finished"); that is a statement about completeness, not a wipe plan. If a wipe policy is ever set, it must come from an announcement, not from this page.

docs.title: The questline ladder
docs.summary: Every questline, its gate, giver, and the system or story it introduces.
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Questlines group related quests in the journal and show what each line is waiting for.
> - The ladder below lists all 14 lines in the source registry.
> - Some steps wait on a feature, a Renown threshold or a seasonal event even after the line itself opens.
> - Introduction lines point to the handbook page for the system they introduce.
> - The quest guide has every questline step's objectives, outcomes and recovery advice.

## Questlines

| Questline | Gate | Giver | What it teaches or covers | Stage page |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| The Burning Doors | Character level 10; online; registered account | Ysolde Marnhel, Master Conjurer of the Mages Guild of Wayrest | Dagon's Breaches and the investigation behind them | Dagon's Breach |
| The Covens' Hoard | After The Burning Doors; online; registered account | Ysolde Marnhel, Master Conjurer of the Mages Guild of Wayrest | Elite dungeon champions and the Weir Key | Spawned and elite dungeons |
| The Weir Road | After The Covens' Hoard; online; registered account | Corvane Tull, Battlemage of the Spire's last class | The Elite Breach and the road through its Redoubts | Elite Gates |
| The Hour That Was Not | Character level 12; online; registered account | Prior Anselm Vey of the Order of the Hour | Abyss Dungeons and the Brass Remnant | Abyss dungeons |
| The Old Coil | Character level 8; online; registered account | Hamid al-Rasheen, a packet captain of Sentinel | The Sea Serpent | Sea serpent |
| The Thirteenth of Frostfall | Character level 6; online; registered account; Witches' Festival (Starfall) staged | Morwen, a Wyrd Sister of Glenmoril | The seasonal Starfall and fallen stars; star-dependent steps wait for the Festival | Festivals and Starfall |
| The Court Crafter | Character level 2; online; registered account | A court crafter | Gathering, professions, crafting and Stores | Crafting |
| The Smith's Secrets | Character level 4; Loot Rarity on for its steps | An armorer | Rarity gear, sockets and the Reforge | Loot rarity |
| The Harbormaster's Word | Character level 5; Naval Combat on for its steps | A harbormaster | Ships, cargo and naval combat | Owning a ship |
| The Merchant's Road | Character level 3 | A stable master | Wagons, hauling and delivery work | Wagons and hauling |
| A Seat at the Table | Character level 2; The King's Gambit on for its second step | A tavern regular | Tavern games, including The King's Gambit when enabled | Tavern games |
| The Herald's Call | Character level 6; online | The Arena's Herald | The Arena and its first bouts | The Arena |
| The Bay's Troubles | Character level 6; online; second step waits until Renown 10 | A captain of the watch | Town raids, then the revenants called the Kneeling Dead | Town raids |
| Written in the Stars | Character level 3; online | An astrologer | Renown Stars and the Firmament | The Firmament |

“Registered account” means a guest account cannot open the line: the service records no guest's receipts, so its witnessed steps could not be done. The level and sequence gates come
from the line registry. Where a feature or event is named, it can hold a step even after the line is listed; the journal
shows the current wait. The source does not provide a fixed per-step building list for these lines.

## Finding your place

The Quests tab shows each line's completed, current and upcoming steps, along with what a line is waiting for. A seasonal line you have not begun is shown only while its event runs. The
introduction lines are short invitations to their related systems; the longer story lines are available later in the
ladder. A questline step that is held by a feature or seasonal gate waits rather than starting and failing.

## Common mistakes

- Reading the character-level gate as the only condition. Account registration, online play, feature switches,
  earlier lines and event timing can also matter.
- Assuming every giver is in a fixed building. The registry names the giver role or person, but the source does not
  define a fixed building for each step.
- Confusing a line's introduction with its whole system. Use the linked stage page for the system's full rules.

docs.title: Quest rewards
docs.summary: Compare quest payments, reward choices and questline gates before you decide what to pursue.
headings: Read the payment before you leave
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Read the quest's outcome and reward card before choosing a branch.
> - A gear reward normally offers three cards; you keep one item.
> - Register before pursuing account-backed questline deeds and titles.
> - Claim waiting gear regularly: the reward queue has limited space.

## Read the payment before you leave

Open Quests and inspect your objectives, branches and expected reward. Gold, gear, faction standing, Renown and a questline deed are separate benefits. 

Gold starts with the quest script. Some scripts specify a range; the ordinary generated purse also considers your character level or guild rank, guild power and regional prices. There is no universal gold payment for a quest tier. A letter is quest mail, not payment.

An outcome can change that purse. Standard outcomes keep the script's amount; a lesser payment uses three quarters, while a greater payment uses one and a quarter times the amount and raises the gear reward's tier by one, within the tier limit. A betrayal can pay the other side's coin without awarding the betrayed guild's extra gear. A quest with its own special reward can retain that reward instead of adding a choice card.

## Choose one piece of gear

When an eligible outcome pays gear, you receive a choice normally containing a weapon, an armour piece and a jewel. You keep one, rather than collecting the whole display. The pieces are identified and checked against your class's equipment restrictions. If a category cannot produce a suitable piece, another armour piece or jewel can fill its place.

The weapon choice uses your two highest live skills among Short Blade, Long Blade, Axe, Blunt Weapon and Archery. Hand-to-Hand is not a weapon-card category. A fist-focused character should therefore compare the armour and jewellery rather than expect a fist weapon to appear. Fitting does not guarantee an upgrade over what you wear.

The rolled cards stay with the waiting offer, so reloading does not refresh them. A named questline reward uses its named base only when you can equip that base; otherwise that card can be an unnamed suitable item. Compare statistics before choosing.

## Understand tiers

A quest's tier is set when it starts. An explicit quest-sheet tier takes priority. Otherwise guild-rank requirements, reputation requirements or character-level bands determine it.

| Tier | Guild rank requirement | Reputation requirement band | Character-level band | Ordinary gear floor |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 0â€“1 | Below 20 | 1â€“6 | Magic |
| 2 | 2â€“3 | 20â€“39 | 7â€“13 | Magic; each card has a 25% chance of Rare |
| 3 | 4â€“5 | 40â€“59 | 14â€“20 | Rare |
| 4 | 6 or higher | 60 or higher | 21 or higher | Rare |

These columns are alternative ways of assigning a tier, not requirements you must satisfy together. Social quests use your level band rather than interpreting their low requirement as guild rank. Higher tiers do not make ordinary choice rewards Legendary. A greater outcome can improve the effective tier, but it still stops at tier 4.

## Separate standing, Renown and deeds

Faction standing affects the guild or faction concerned. Renown is your separate online progression: a successful quest can earn Renown XP once through the online tracker. Its amount depends on the character-level formula and Renown ceiling, and the account's hourly cap still applies. A larger gold purse does not itself promise more Renown.

Questline deeds use another record. The account service must witness the relevant event after the line opens and in its required order. Closing a Breach before starting its line does not automatically satisfy a later witnessed step. The service checks receipts for deeds such as Breach closures, Redoubts, the Brass Remnant, the Sea Serpent and fallen stars. Titles and the Covens' Hoard's once-per-account Weir Key have their own checks; keeping the key is a branch choice. The Starwarden title can also pay Soul Cakes while the festival is open; this is a separate account reward.

## Failure, retries and private rooms

Failing an unfinished quest costs no faction standing online. That protection does not erase a deliberate branch's standing consequences or a crime's legal consequences. An unsuccessful quest also does not receive the success-only gear choice or successful-quest Renown payment.

A failed questline step is offered again after one day on your character's clock. Successful steps normally wait one character hour before the next step starts. These are character-clock delays, not a promise that every failed ordinary quest returns automatically. Read the journal's current state before travelling again.

A dungeon named by your active quest can offer a private instance for you and your party. Shared quest foes can be fought together, but each character keeps their own quest copy and progress. A private room helps you pursue your objective without public-room competition; it does not bypass reward gates or replace an account-service witness.

## Which questline first

Choose the system you want to learn next. These are opening gates; individual steps can wait for additional requirements.

| Your immediate goal | Line | Opening gate and later restriction |
|---|---|---|
| Craft or play tavern games | The Court Crafter / A Seat at the Table | Level 2; crafts require online registration, King's Gambit must be enabled for its step |
| Plan growth or haul goods | Written in the Stars / The Merchant's Road | Level 3; Stars requires online play |
| Improve equipment | The Smith's Secrets | Level 4; Loot rarity needed for its steps |
| Learn ships | The Harbormaster's Word | Level 5; Naval Combat needed for its steps |
| Try Arena or shared threats | The Herald's Call / The Bay's Troubles | Level 6 online; the revenant step waits for Renown 10 |
| Follow Starfall | The Thirteenth of Frostfall | Level 6, registered online, event open |
| Pursue the serpent | The Old Coil | Level 8, registered online |
| Begin the Breach chain | The Burning Doors | Level 10, registered online; then Covens' Hoard and Weir Road |
| Learn Abyss Dungeons | The Hour That Was Not | Level 12, registered online |

## Common mistakes

- Leaving cards unclaimed indefinitely: only twelve offers wait, and overflow can discard an offer.
- Expecting an event completed before the line opens to count as its witnessed deed.
- Confusing a character-clock retry with a real-world daily reset.

## Next

- Caps, timers and resets

docs.title: The main story
docs.summary: How the main quest begins, the chapter records the journal tracks, and how to recover when a chapter goes quiet.
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - The main story starts with a letter from Lady Brisienna after the opening dungeon.
> - It is a set of chapter records, not one linear quest; the journal names the current chapter and the next lead.
> - Several chapters wait on an earlier one, a meeting, or a ruler's summons, so check the journal before travelling.
> - The story is optional in DFO; it is the long answer to what happened to Lysandus and the Emperor's letter.
> - The pinned pack also contains background controllers; they are not chapters you play.

## Before you start

The main story begins with Lady Brisienna, the Emperor's agent, after you leave Privateer's
Hold. Everything after that is a chain of chapter records: a royal court asks for something, a place must be searched,
or a message must be delivered. The journal is the route; this page is the map of the chapter names.

> [!warning] The main story has permanent refusals
> Refusing a ruler's request can close the branch that request opens. Read the offer before you decline. This guide does
> not promise a second chance in DFO.

## The chapters

The chapter order below is the order of the records in the pinned pack. It is not a promise that every character
sees every chapter in exactly this order: the classic main story branches, and the journal is the authority for your
character.

| # | Chapter | What it asks | Guide |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 1 | Lady Brisienna | Meet the Emperor's agent at the tavern named in her letter | Full guide |
| 2 | Missing Prince | Find proof of what became of Prince Lhotun's brother | Quest entry |
| 3 | Prince Helseth's Blackmail | Carry Prince Helseth's letter and bring back the reply | Quest entry |
| 4 | Freeing Medora | Find the horn of the Great Unicorn and bring it to Medora | Quest entry |
| 5 | Morgiah's Wedding | Carry Princess Morgiah's letter to Scourg Barrow and return with the answer | Quest entry |
| 6 | Concern for Nulfaga | Find Nulfaga in Shedungent and speak with her | Quest entry |
| 7 | Elysana's Robe | Bring Princess Elysana's robe to Lord Castellian | Quest entry |
| 8 | The Werebeast | End the werewolf of Tristore Laboratory | Quest entry |
| 9 | Who Gets the Totem | Meet Lady Brisienna and decide where the Totem goes | Quest entry |
| 10 | Elysana's Betrayal | Answer Princess Elysana's summons at Castle Wayrest | Quest entry |
| 11 | Stronghold of the Blades | Meet the Underking's agent in Sentinel | Quest entry |
| 12 | Barenziah's Book | Answer Queen Barenziah's letter, then recover the lost chapter | Quest entry |
| 13 | The Emperor's Courier | Find the Emperor's messenger and learn what happened to the letter | Quest entry |
| 14 | Mynisera's Letters | Answer Queen Aubk-i's letter at Castle Daggerfall | Quest entry |
| 15 | Lysandus' Revenge | Bring down Lord Woodborne, by death or disgrace | Quest entry |
| 16 | Journey to Aetherius | Find the Mantella in the Mantellan Crux and touch it | Quest entry |
| 17 | Wayrest Painting | Answer Queen Akorithi's summons at Castle Sentinel | Quest entry |
| 18 | Dust of Restful Death | Ask Gortwog where the Dust can be found | Quest entry |
| 19 | Orcish Treaty | Find who holds the Emperor's letter and return to Mynisera | Quest entry |
| 20 | Lich's Soul | Answer the King of Worms' summons at Scourg Barrow | Quest entry |
| 21 | Lysandus' Revelation | Return to Medora in Direnni Tower when the month has passed | Quest entry |

The pack also has optional side chapters (Lord K'avar and the Former Student parts), background records that run
Daggerfall's curse and the Totem claimants' moves, and the Mantella/backbone controllers. They are not separate chapter
pages here; the browser lists them under Main quest.

## How to read the journal

- The Quests tab lists the active chapter, its latest entry and its time remaining. The newest entry is the current
  instruction; older entries are context.
- The journal names the place, person or ruler to visit. A generated site is your site; a guide cannot give a fixed
  map pin.
- If an entry says to wait, the chapter is not broken. Several chapters wait for a month, a summons or another
  chapter's outcome.
- If you have more than one active main-story entry, finish the one the journal calls current before chasing the other.

## If it goes quiet

1. Re-read the newest journal entry. It names the next person or place.
2. Check the Quests tab. A chapter waiting on a ruler's summons or a month is waiting, not stalled.
3. Visit the court or tavern the entry names. Main-story meetings happen at fixed castles and generated taverns.
4. If a ruler refused you, the branch may be closed. This guide does not promise another opening; reload a save if you
   have one, or continue with the chapters that remain.
5. If the journal and the world disagree, note the chapter, the source file and what you saw, and report it through
   How this guide is checked.

## Rewards and what it unlocks

The main story is not a gold-per-chapter ladder. It pays story access, titles and the ending, with the ordinary quest
rewards on the side. For the payment rules that do apply, see Quest rewards. The story is
optional in DFO; the late game explains what else competes for that time.

## Next

- Browse the complete quest guide
- The questline ladder — the online lines that run alongside the main story.
- Lady Brisienna — the first chapter in full.

docs.title: Lady Brisienna
docs.summary: The Emperor's first letter, the tavern meeting that starts the main story, and what happens if you never arrive.
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - The main story begins with a letter from Lady Brisienna, the Emperor's agent in Daggerfall.
> - The letter names a tavern; go there and speak to her. The meeting is the quest.
> - The source starts a 14-day failure clock and an earlier invitation window, so read the letter's own date.
> - If you miss her, she reports you as a traitor and this main-story branch fails. There is no reward beyond the story.

## The quest facts

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | Main story, first chapter |
| Given by | Lady Brisienna, the Emperor's agent; she is in the tavern the letter names |
| Opens when | After you leave Privateer's Hold; the quest arrives by letter |
| How it reaches you | A letter, with the meeting place named in it |
| Time limit | The source starts a 14-day failure clock and a 7–14 day invitation clock; the letter's date is the one to follow |
| Can it fail? | Yes. Missing the meeting fails the approach to the main story and she reports you |
| Rewards | No gold or gear; it opens the next main-story chapter |
| Permanent choices | Missing the meeting is the failure; there is no alternate route from this chapter |
| Instance / party | A town tavern; no private dungeon |

## How you get it

The quest starts by letter after the opening dungeon. Read the letter before you sell anything or leave town: it names
the tavern where Lady Brisienna waits, and the date matters. The meeting is in a generated tavern, so the name in your
letter is the only reliable location.

> [!online] Online
> The letter is a quest letter, not a courier questline invitation. It can arrive in the same session as the opening;
> the journal is the authority on the place and date.

## What you do

1. Finish or leave Privateer's Hold.
2. Read the letter from Lady Brisienna and note the tavern and the date.
3. Travel to that tavern. Taverns keep normal opening hours; if the door is locked at night, wait or come back.
4. Find Lady Brisienna inside and speak to her. The journal updates when she has told you where to start.
5. Follow the next main-story lead: the royal families of Daggerfall, Wayrest and Sentinel.

## Choices that matter

There is no branch to choose here; the choice is whether you attend.

| Choice | Immediate effect | Later effect | Reversible? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Meet Lady Brisienna | The journal advances to the next chapter | The main story continues | No — it is the chapter's success |
| Miss the meeting | She reports you to the Emperor as a traitor | This approach to the main story fails | No |

## If it goes wrong

- No letter yet. The quest starts by letter after the opening. Check the Quests tab and the journal; if it has not
  appeared, keep playing the opening and check again in town.
- Can't find the tavern. Read the letter's place line again. It is a generated tavern, so a guide cannot give a fixed
  address. Ask directions in town or use the town map.
- The door is locked. Taverns have hours; wait until they open.
- She is not there. Check the date in the letter. The failure clock is real; reload a save only if you have one, and
  do not assume the quest can be restarted.
- The journal says you failed. This chapter's approach is over. The main story has alternate starts in classic
  Daggerfall, but this guide does not promise one in DFO; report what you saw if the journal contradicts the letter.

## Rewards and what it unlocks

There is no purse, gear choice or reputation payment in the source. The value is the next main-story chapter: the
journal sends you to the royal families of Daggerfall, Wayrest and Sentinel.

## Known notes

- The source's own clocks are 7–14 days for the invitation and 14 days for the failure. The letter is generated with a
  date; the journal's entry is more specific than this page.
- The quest file uses three letter items internally. Do not treat them as loot; they are the letter and its reminders.

## Next

- Browse the complete quest guide — the main-story list starts here.
- Missing Prince — the next main-story step.
- How this guide is checked — what Draft means and how to report a mistake.

docs.title: The Court Crafter
docs.summary: Gather materials, make a station-crafted piece, and report to the court's crafters through three introductory quests.
headings: Rewards and what the line unlocks
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Play online with a registered account at character level 2 or higher.
> - Receive the first note outdoors in a town by day; choose a town with a General Store and a smith.
> - Gather while the relevant step is active. Buying materials does not perform the required actions.
> - For the final step, make a piece at a crafting station; cooking and brewing do not count.
> - Read each new journal entry: the next crafter can have a different name and workplace.

Checked against e4f093166.

## Line facts

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Giver | A court crafter; each step creates its own local smith |
| Opens when | Character level 2, online, registered account |
| Steps | Three: QLIP01–QLIP03 |
| Tier | 1 throughout; an early crafting introduction |
| Where it starts | A courier note; the crafter works at a General Store in the town where the step starts |
| Online/account/feature needs | Online registration for the profession actions; a local General Store and smith for quest setup |
| What it unlocks | The next lesson, then completion of the crafting introduction; no separate profession-access unlock is specified |

## How the line starts

The runner sends a note rather than adding a normal quest offer to a smith's dialogue. Once eligible, stay outdoors in a town during daylight for delivery. New lines are paced, so another pending first letter can delay yours. Check Quests before moving on.

Use a substantial town when a step comes due. If its required building or person cannot be generated, the runner waits before trying again. Later steps enter the journal directly; do not wait for another physical note each time.

## Step table

| Step | Quest | Objective | What the outcome changes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Of Rod and Root | Catch three fish, gather three plants, then report | Payment and the next gathering lesson |
| 2 | Ore and Timber | Mine ore or stone three times, chop wood three times, then report | Payment and the making lesson |
| 3 | Made by Hand | Craft a station-made piece, then report | Final payment and line completion |

## Walkthrough

### 1. Of Rod and Root

Read the note for the crafter's name, General Store and town. Catch three fish and gather three plants while this step runs, then speak to that crafter. The tasks track fishing and gathering actions, rather than a purchase or a pile of stock already in your bag. The script does not take your gathered materials when you report.

If you see the crafter asking for more work, check both objectives before leaving again. Finishing the fish requirement does not finish the plant requirement. Use the journal's return location rather than assuming any smith can accept the report. Once both tasks are complete, speaking to the named crafter pays you and advances the line. There is no choice between different employers or rewards in this step.

### 2. Ore and Timber

Check the new journal entry after the line advances. This assignment creates another crafter in the town where it starts; the name and General Store can differ from the first step. Mine ore or stone three times and chop wood three times. The game counts the relevant gathering actions, so bringing purchased ore and timber is not a substitute.

If you see only one objective complete, continue the other kind of gathering rather than repeating the finished one. Once both are done, return to the smith named in this step's journal and speak to them. Nothing is taken from your stock by the report task. An early conversation only reminds you of the unfinished work; it does not replace it or choose a different outcome. Successful reporting pays you and opens the final lesson after the normal step delay.

### 3. Made by Hand

Make a piece at a crafting station, then visit the crafter named in the current journal. The script points to stations such as a forge, loom or mason's bench. Choose work you can make with your available materials and profession access; this quest does not specify one mandatory recipe or quality.

If you see no crafting progress after cooking food or brewing potions, make a station-crafted piece instead. Those activities do not emit the action this objective listens for. If the piece objective is complete but the quest remains active, speak to this step's crafter at its named General Store. The report finishes the line and pays the final reward. The script does not consume your piece in that conversation, and there is no branch asking you to commit to a permanent profession choice here.

## Choices and outcomes

The line has no branch. Each successful report advances the sequence; timing out produces an unpaid failure, followed by the runner's retry schedule.

## Rewards and what the line unlocks

All three sheets specify tier 1 and standard payment. The scripts pay gold; the final sheet adds The Crafter's Thanks, a named Ring option. Named bases remain subject to equipment fitting, and a gear offer lets you keep one item.

Successful quests can also earn online Renown XP under the general tracker and account cap. These sheets specify no faction-standing change or fixed Renown amount. Completing the line teaches gathering and crafting; it does not grant exclusive access to those systems. See quest rewards for tiers and claim rules.

## If it goes wrong

1. Journal: reread the current crafter, store, town and unfinished actions; each step has a deadline.
2. Quests tab: check whether the line is active, waiting or retrying.
3. Held step: confirm online play and registration before attempting profession actions.
4. Letter/building: receive mail outdoors in town by day; be in a town with a General Store and smith when setup retries.
5. Private instance: no dungeon is required here. A private dungeon cannot replace gathering or station work.
6. Retry timing: successful steps normally wait one character hour; failure or failed setup waits one character day. Online deadlines charge played time; a delivery delay is separate.
7. Report: if the state contradicts your actions, record the step ID, objective, giver and town through How this guide is checked. Reload or abandon is not a guaranteed repair.

docs.title: Written in the Stars
docs.summary: Allocate new Firmament stars and visit the astrologers who introduce your online growth choices.
headings: Rewards and what the line unlocks
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Reach character level 3 online, then receive the astrologer's chart outdoors in town by day.
> - Use a registered account for the Firmament service, even though the line's opening gate only says online.
> - Allocate one new star for the first step and three more for the second.
> - Confirm changes in Growth, then return to the temple named in the current journal.
> - Do not refund and rebuy the same star for progress: each star counts once.

Checked against e4f093166.

## Line facts

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Giver | An astrologer; each step creates its own local spellcaster |
| Opens when | Character level 3, online |
| Steps | Two: QLIF01–QLIF02 |
| Tier | 1 in both sheets |
| Where it starts | A courier chart naming an astrologer at a local temple |
| Online/account/feature needs | Online line; a registered account for Firmament allocation; a town with a temple and suitable person for setup |
| What it unlocks | A second reading, then completion of the Firmament introduction; no separate tree-access reward is specified |

## How the line starts

The runner sends a chart once the level and online gate opens. You do not request this quest from an ordinary temple questor. Wait outdoors in town during daylight for delivery. Another line's pending first letter can hold yours back.

If nothing arrives, inspect Quests for the current wait and choose a substantial town with a temple when setup is due. The follow-up starts through the journal rather than another chart delivery. Its astrologer and temple can change.

## Step table

| Step | Quest | Objective | What the outcome changes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | The First Star | Allocate a new Firmament star, then visit the named astrologer | Standard payment and access to the second lesson |
| 2 | A Constellation of Your Own | Allocate three additional new stars, then visit the current astrologer | Standard payment, named reward option and line completion |

## Walkthrough

### 1. The First Star

Read the chart for the astrologer, temple and town. Open the pause menu's Growth tab and its Firmament section, choose a connected star you want, and press Accept to keep the allocation. Renown supplies Stars; the quest asks you to spend through the Firmament rather than merely gain character levels or open the window. Return to the named astrologer once the objective completes.

If you see the service refusing access on a guest account, register before trying to allocate. If you see no points available, continue earning Renown and check your budget again. Allocations made before the quest runs are not retroactive quest actions. A successful reading pays you and advances the line. The choice of star affects your character, but the sheet has no alternate reward branch for different stars or signs.

### 2. A Constellation of Your Own

Read the fresh journal entry before travelling: this step sends you to another generated astrologer, potentially in a different temple or town. Allocate three further stars while this step is active, then visit that astrologer for the final reading. Plan connected purchases around the bonuses you actually want; the quest does not require a particular combat path or constellation shape.

If you see no progress after refunding and buying back a star, choose a star your character has not held before. The Firmament remembers previously held stars, so repeated purchases of the same node do not supply repeated quest credit. If the objective is complete but payment is missing, return to the current reading location and speak to its astrologer. That conversation finishes the introduction. No choice locks you to the astrologer's suggested role or changes the quest's standard payment.

## Choices and outcomes

The line has no branch. Your Firmament allocation remains a character-building decision, but both sheets have one successful reading outcome and one unpaid failure outcome. Do not confuse the freedom to choose stars with a quest reward choice.

## Rewards and what the line unlocks

Both steps specify tier 1 and standard payment, including script gold. The final sheet names The Astrologer's Star, an Amulet option. Equipment fitting can substitute a suitable base, and you keep one item from a gear offer.

The introduction teaches the Firmament; it does not award a free stock of allocation points. Renown supplies Stars at 2 per Renown level after the first. Successful quests can separately earn Renown XP under the general online tracker and account cap. Neither sheet sets a fixed Renown payment or faction-standing adjustment. See quest rewards for those distinctions.

> [!note] Opening gate and usable service
> The line registry requires online play at character level 3. The Firmament service also requires registration to store your allocation; reaching the line's level gate alone does not make a guest's allocation work.

## If it goes wrong

1. Journal: confirm the active star count, current astrologer, temple and deadline.
2. Quests tab: distinguish a running lesson from a waiting next step.
3. Held step: confirm online access and registration; check your available points and accepted allocation.
4. Letter/building: stand outdoors in town by day for the first chart; use a town with a temple when setup retries.
5. Private instance: neither lesson needs a dungeon. A private room does not award Stars or bypass the account service.
6. Retry timing: a successful step normally waits one character hour; failed steps or failed setup wait one character day. Quest deadlines run while you play online, separately from courier delays.
7. Report: record QLIF01 or QLIF02, the objective and allocation state through How this guide is checked. Reloading or abandoning is not a promised fix.

docs.title: The Bay's Troubles
docs.summary: Defend a shared-world town raid, then bring one of your revenants to its knees for the watch.
headings: Rewards and what the line unlocks
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Begin online at character level 6; receive the watch's order outdoors in town by day.
> - Fight raiders and stay in the attacked town until the raid is repelled, then report to the named tavern.
> - Expect the second step to wait until Renown 10.
> - Bring one of your own revenants to its knees; another player can help with the fight.
> - After the kneeling objective, receive the watch's thanks outdoors in town by day instead of returning to a captain.

Checked against e4f093166.

## Line facts

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Giver | A captain of the watch, associated with the region's ruling faction |
| Opens when | Character level 6, online |
| Steps | Two: QLIW01–QLIW02 |
| Tier | 2 in both sheets |
| Where it starts | A courier order; the first captain waits at a local tavern named in the journal |
| Online/account/feature needs | Online; no registered-account condition in the line definition; step 2 needs Renown 10 |
| What it unlocks | The revenant lesson after the raid lesson, then line completion; no exclusive access to raids or revenants is awarded |

## How the line starts

The runner sends the captain's order when you qualify. Stay outdoors in a town by day for the courier, and check Quests if another first letter is pending. The first step needs a local tavern and a suitable captain when it starts; a small settlement can fail that setup.

After the raid report, the second assignment appears in the journal once its Renown requirement is met. It comes from another captain. Its eventual reward arrives by courier, so the first tavern is not a permanent headquarters for the line.

## Step table

| Step | Quest | Objective | What the outcome changes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Raiders at the Gate | Help repel a town raid, then report to the named captain | Standard payment; next lesson waits for its Renown gate |
| 2 | The Kneeling Dead | Have one of your revenants kneel, then receive the watch's letter in town | Standard payment, named weapon option and line completion |

## Walkthrough

### 1. Raiders at the Gate

Read the order for your captain's name, tavern and town. The raid itself can be in any town: follow the shared event information to the attacked settlement, fight its raiders, and remain there until the defence resolves. The quest's action requires a raid you fought in and your presence in its town when the raiders are driven off. Visiting an attacked town without contributing is not enough.

If you see the raid end without objective credit, check whether you struck a raider and stayed for the cleanse. Join a later raid if the requirement is still unfinished. Once the journal records success, return to the named captain at the named tavern. That report pays you and advances the line. The shared raid's event rewards are separate from this conversation's quest reward.

### 2. The Kneeling Dead

Wait for the Quests view to release this step at Renown 10. The objective concerns one of your own revenants: it must yield and kneel to you. Another player may strike the blows that force it down. The quest does not require you to deliver the final blow yourself, and a revenant belonging to someone else is not a substitute.

If you see a waiting Renown requirement, continue your ordinary progression rather than searching for a missing tavern giver. If the kneeling objective is complete but the quest remains active, go outdoors in a town by day and allow the watch's courier to deliver its thanks. The script waits for that letter before paying and ending. You may kill or spare the kneeling revenant under that system's rules; neither choice changes this quest's successful payment outcome.

## Choices and outcomes

The line has no quest branch. Killing or sparing a kneeling revenant belongs to the revenant system; QLIW02 checks the kneeling event and courier delivery, with the same success outcome afterward.

## Rewards and what the line unlocks

Both sheets specify tier 2 and standard payment, with script gold. The final sheet names The Watch's Thanks, a Mace option. Gear offers award one chosen item, and named bases remain subject to your equipment restrictions.

Neither quest sheet specifies a faction-standing adjustment or fixed Renown amount. The raid system has its own participation benefits, and successful quests can earn Renown XP through the general online tracker and account cap. Keep those rewards separate when checking what arrived. The line introduces shared threats; completing it is not the switch that enables town raids. See quest rewards for the tier and payment rules.

> [!online] Shared town defence
> Town raids happen in the shared world. A private quest dungeon cannot stand in for the attacked town or satisfy the raid objective.

## If it goes wrong

1. Journal: check which action is unfinished and note the return tavern or courier instruction and deadline.
2. Quests tab: distinguish the raid assignment from the later revenant assignment.
3. Held step: QLIW02 waits for Renown 10; character level 6 alone is insufficient.
4. Letter/building: receive the order and final thanks outdoors in town by day. First-step setup needs a town with a tavern and captain.
5. Private instance: raids remain shared town events; private dungeon progress does not replace them. Each party member keeps their own quest progress.
6. Retry timing: success normally waits one character hour before the next eligible step; failure or failed setup waits one character day. Online quest deadlines charge played time, separately from delivery delays.
7. Report: record QLIW01 or QLIW02, objective state, event and town through How this guide is checked. Do not rely on reload or abandon to restore progress.

docs.title: The Burning Doors
docs.summary: Investigate Dagon's covens, close a Breach, and decide the embers' fate.
headings: Rewards and what the line unlocks
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Reach character level 10 online with a registered account.
> - Receive Ysolde's letter outdoors in town by day; follow its generated meeting place.
> - Keep the rite-book sealed for Guild standing, or read it for greater pay and a standing cost.
> - Break the rite and close a Breach after their respective steps open.
> - Compare the final ember choices before answering.

Checked against e4f093166. Spoilers follow.

## Line facts

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Giver | Ysolde Marnhel, Wayrest Mages Guild Master Conjurer |
| Opens when | Character level 10, online, registered account |
| Steps | Five: QLBD01–QLBD05 |
| Tier | 3 in all five sheets |
| Where it starts | Courier; generated magery |
| Online/account/feature needs | Registration; ordered rite/Breach witnesses |
| What it unlocks | Doorwarden at witnessed closure; The Covens' Hoard after completion |

## How the line starts

Receive the runner's invitation outdoors in town by day. If absent, check Quests for gates or pending letters. Follow the current journal's generated hall and town.

## Step table

| Step | Quest | Objective | What the outcome changes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | A Letter from Wayrest | Meet Ysolde | Payment; coven lead |
| 2 | The Faithful | Kill coven Summoner; deliver book | Pay/standing branch |
| 3 | Breaking the Rite | Kill omen's Summoner before opening; report | Rite witness; payment |
| 4 | Through the Burning Door | Defeat Breach Warden; report | Closure witness; payment; Doorwarden |
| 5 | The Caged Broker | Choose embers' destination | Standing; named option; completion |

## Walkthrough

### 1. A Letter from Wayrest

Read Ysolde's letter and travel to its named hall and town. She occupies a generated magery site; her Wayrest title does not identify a fixed address. Speak to her for the introduction and payment. This meeting explains the covens behind the Breaches and leads to the next assignment.

If you see no letter, check eligibility and courier conditions before travelling. If the meeting objective appears but you cannot find her, compare the current journal's place with your destination. You need a conversation here, rather than a boss kill. There is no branch. Missing the waiting window produces an unpaid failure, with a later retry.

### 2. The Faithful

Read the new letter for the coven dungeon, target Summoner and return hall. Defeat that Summoner and recover the rite-book from the body. Other coven kills do not replace the named target. Keep the book for delivery.

If you see the read-or-seal prompt, compare the choices below. Reading pays more but costs Guild standing; preserving the seal gives standard payment and gains standing. Both routes require delivery to Ysolde. If the kill is complete but the book objective is missing, inspect the Summoner's remains. If hand-in stalls, check that you carry the book at this step's hall. Both successful routes continue the line.

### 3. Breaking the Rite

With this step active, find the faithful's ritual at a Dagon's Breach omen. Defeat its Summoner before the door opens. This world-event deed differs from the previous dungeon kill. Breaking the rite weakens the door; the Breach still opens.

If you see the gate already open, seek another qualifying omen. A later Warden kill is a different objective. Once the rite action registers, Ysolde sends a letter naming your next meeting place. Receive it outdoors in town by day, then visit her for payment. A meeting deadline replaces the deed deadline, so the ritual alone does not finish the quest. Account witness checks remain separate from journal progress.

### 4. Through the Burning Door

With this step running, follow the active Breach's instructions to confront its Warden, Valkynaz Ruhn. Defeat him to close the door. A broken rite alone cannot complete this assignment: it requires closure and an account receipt. Follow current event information for the location and phase.

If you see Ysolde saying the door remains open, inspect the closure objective and receipt. A closure before this step opened does not automatically satisfy its witnessed sequence. Once it registers, return to the journal's hall before the meeting deadline. The report pays you. At this witnessed closure step, the service also awards Doorwarden, subject to its claim checks.

### 5. The Caged Broker

Receive Ysolde's letter and visit its named hall. This meeting asks you to choose the embers' destination: the Mages Guild, the Order of the Hour or the Sigil Broker. There is no separate collection quota or delivery trip to each recipient.

If you see the destination prompt, compare the table before selecting. Guild and Order routes give standard payment and their respective faction's standing. The Broker pays more but lowers Guild standing. Each supplies a different named gear option, subject to equipment fitting. Answering completes the line; no reconsideration task follows. Missing the meeting's waiting window instead produces an unpaid failure and a later retry.

## Choices and outcomes

| Step / choice | Payment | Standing change | Named option / consequence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Faithful: read the book | Greater | Mages Guild −3 | Deliver it afterward; line continues |
| Faithful: preserve the seal | Standard | Mages Guild +5 | Deliver it afterward; line continues |
| Broker: Mages Guild | Standard | Mages Guild +5 | Ysolde's Ember-Rod, Staff |
| Broker: Order of the Hour | Standard | Order of the Hour +5 | Seal of the Hour, Ring |
| Broker: Sigil Broker | Greater | Mages Guild −2 | Broker's Dusk-Wing Mantle, Left Pauldron |

No reversal task is scripted.

## Rewards and what the line unlocks

Tier 3 outcomes pay gold and eligible gear; greater payment improves effective tier. Keep one item per offer, subject to class fitting. Successful quests can earn general online Renown XP; the sheets set no amount. See quest rewards.

Completion opens The Covens' Hoard, followed by The Weir Road; see the ladder.

> [!warning] Failure protection has limits
> Online failure costs no faction standing. Branch penalties still apply.

## If it goes wrong

1. Journal: check step, generated places, target, book and deadline.
2. Quests tab: inspect the next task and unwitnessed deeds.
3. Held step: confirm online registration and required event order.
4. Letter/building: receive mail outdoors in town by day; retry setup in a substantial town.
5. Private instance: use the coven's offered quest instance. Breaches remain shared; party quest progress stays separate.
6. Retry timing: success normally waits one character hour; failure/setup failure waits one character day. Online deadlines charge played time; delivery and meeting clocks differ.
7. Report: send step, objective and receipt state through How this guide is checked. Reload/abandon repairs are unverified.

| What it unlocks | The Weir Road; account-checked Covenbane and optional Weir Key |

## How the line starts

Receive Ysolde's letter outdoors in town by day. New lines begin at most once per character hour, with no other first letter in flight. Check Quests for the prior-line gate or a held step. If setup cannot find a required site, let it retry from a suitable town. Follow the generated hall in the current journal; Wayrest is Ysolde's affiliation, not a fixed meeting address.

## Step table

| Step | Quest | Objective | Outcome effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Gold-Lit | Kill three Elite Dungeon champions; report | Standard pay; lieutenant lead |
| 2 | The Lieutenant | Kill named lieutenant; recover and deliver key | Standard pay; key decision |
| 3 | What the Key Opens | Meet Ysolde; keep or seal | Branch rewards; line completion |

## Walkthrough

### 1. Gold-Lit

Read the letter for Ysolde's hall and town, then hunt three of the covens' gold-lit champions in Elite Dungeons. Their gold light identifies the relevant enemies; ordinary dungeon kills do not replace the required action. Follow current exploration information rather than a fixed dungeon pin. Count kills during this step, rather than assuming earlier victories satisfy it.

When the third champion falls, the journal changes to a report objective. Return to the hall it names and speak to Ysolde for standard payment. Visiting early only produces a reminder; it does not finish the assignment. The kill window gives way to a separate meeting deadline, so check the updated time remaining before another expedition. There is no branch here. Party help does not remove the need to check your own objective progress.

### 2. The Lieutenant

Read the new journal entry as soon as the step begins. It names a generated dungeon, a particular coven lieutenant and Ysolde's return hall. Travel to that dungeon and defeat the named lieutenant. Another gold-lit champion is no substitute for this target. Inspect the body and take the wrapped quest key before leaving; a completed kill objective alone is not the hand-in.

Carry the key to Ysolde and speak to her at this step's hall. The script checks possession for delivery and pays the standard outcome. If the hand-in stalls, compare your inventory and journal destination before repeating the fight. Use Your instance when the quest dungeon offers it; party members retain separate quest progress. This recovered quest item is not yet the usable account-backed Weir Key awarded by the final choice.

### 3. What the Key Opens

Receive Ysolde's next letter and visit its named hall. She asks whether you will keep the key or give it to the Order of the Hour for sealing. Both choices pay the Guild's fee and complete the line. Keeping requests a usable Weir Key from the account service; sealing trades that grant for greater payment, Order standing and a named ring option.

Before choosing keep, check whether another character on your account has already received this line's key. The grant cannot be repeated by running another character through the story. The service also requires the Burning Doors witness condition; local completion alone is not proof of entitlement. If the key does not arrive, inspect the account claim state. No reversal is scripted. Answer before the meeting deadline rather than leaving the decision unresolved.

## Choices and outcomes

| Final choice | Payment | Other effect |
|---|---|---|
| Keep | Standard | Once-per-account Weir Key, subject to service checks |
| Seal | Greater | Order of the Hour standing gain; Hourkeeper's Linen Signet, Ring option |

## Rewards and what it unlocks

The sheets specify tier 3. Covenbane is awarded at the final step under the service's prior-line check. Completion opens The Weir Road with either choice; sealing does not provide its key. See Elite Gates for other key sources. Named gear remains subject to equipment fitting and a one-item claim; successful quests can earn general online Renown. See quest rewards.

## If it goes wrong

1. Journal: check target, key possession, generated hall and deadline.
2. Quests tab: distinguish active objectives from pending account claims.
3. Held step: confirm registration, prior-line completion and site setup; retry from a suitable town.
4. Instance/party: use the offered quest instance; check each player's progress separately.
5. Retry timing: success normally waits one character hour; failure/setup failure waits one character day. Online deadlines charge played time. Failure costs no faction standing.
6. Report: record step ID, objective and claim state through How this guide is checked. Reload/abandon recovery is unverified.

## Next

- Elite Gates · Dagon's Breach

docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Complete The Covens' Hoard online with a registered account.
> - Prepare for the shared Elite Breach; check your Weir Key access.
> - Do each Redoubt assignment while its own step runs.
> - Return to Corvane Tull after each combat objective; compare the final truth/mercy choice.

Checked against e4f093166; spoilers follow.

## Line facts

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Giver | Corvane Tull, surviving Battlemage |
| Opens when | After The Covens' Hoard; online; registered account |
| Steps | Four: QLWR01–QLWR04 |
| Tier | 4 throughout |
| Where it starts | Letter; generated tavern |
| Feature/event needs | Shared Elite Breach and ordered Redoubt receipts; no extra step needs |
| What it unlocks | Weirwalker at the witnessed warrior-duke step; final story resolution |

## How the line starts

Receive the invitation outdoors in town by day, with at most one new line per character hour and no other first letter travelling. Check Quests for holds or building setup; retry from a suitable town. Sealing the previous key still opens this line; see Elite Gates for entry.

## Step table

| Step | Quest | Objective | Outcome effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | The Weir Gate | Take a first Court; meet Corvane | Standard pay; next assignment |
| 2 | The Torn Halls | Take three Redoubts; report | Standard pay; duke assignment |
| 3 | A Warrior Duke | Take a Valkynaz's Redoubt; report | Standard pay; witnessed title |
| 4 | The Battlemage's Account | Advise Corvane | Truth/mercy rewards; completion |

## Walkthrough

### 1. The Weir Gate

Read Corvane's letter for the current tavern and town. The assignment introduces turning a Weir Key, raising an Elite Breach and taking its first Court. Follow the shared event's entry instructions rather than looking for a generated quest dungeon. If you lack a key after sealing the previous line's gift, check the linked system guide before planning entry.

The quest tracks a Redoubt taken, while the account service checks its receipt. Opening a gate without completing the combat objective is insufficient. Once the Court objective registers, visit Corvane at the letter's tavern for standard payment. His early response only reminds you to fight. A separate meeting deadline starts after the deed. Party participation does not automatically settle every member's journal or account claim, so check your own state before leaving.

### 2. The Torn Halls

Read the journal when this step opens; it begins directly, without another first-letter wait. Take three Redoubts of an Elite Breach while the assignment runs. The Court from your introduction does not replace these new actions. Use the current Breach's progression and party information to find the next fights, rather than travelling to a fixed tavern address from an older step.

After the third qualifying action, return to the tavern named in this journal and speak to Corvane. That report pays the standard outcome and advances the line. An early conversation only gives a reminder. Check both the local objective and the account's ordered receipts if they disagree. Shared combat can help you finish the fights, but a party member's completion is not proof of your own witness. The report has its own deadline after combat finishes.

### 3. A Warrior Duke

Receive Corvane's letter and pursue a Valkynaz's Redoubt in the torn halls. The sheet identifies these as every fifth Court. Follow the Breach's current progression to reach that fight; killing an unrelated daedra or taking an ordinary Redoubt does not satisfy the warrior-duke objective. Start this assignment before pursuing the qualifying deed so the local action can register.

Once the Valkynaz falls, read the updated journal and return to Corvane at its tavern. Reporting pays the standard outcome. This is also the line's title-bearing witnessed step, before the final conversation. Check the account claim if the journal advances without Weirwalker appearing. Earlier Redoubt witnesses must satisfy the required order. A shared Breach does not become a private quest dungeon because you have this assignment. Return before the separate meeting timer expires.

### 4. The Battlemage's Account

Receive the final letter and visit Corvane at its generated tavern. Hear his account of the Spire's fall, then advise him what to tell the Empire about the Secretary who surrendered the keys. This is a conversation step, with no additional Redoubt quota. The earlier combat does not finish the line until you give your answer.

Choose truth to preserve the full account and gain Knights of the Dragon standing, or mercy to support the Secretary's requested version and receive greater payment. Each route has its own named equipment option. Compare the table before answering; no reversal task follows. If Corvane is missing, check this letter's town and tavern rather than returning automatically to an earlier meeting place. The waiting window still applies, and missing it produces an unpaid failure rather than either branch reward.

## Choices and outcomes

| Final answer | Payment | Other effect |
|---|---|---|
| Truth | Standard | Knights of the Dragon standing gain; Oathkeeper's Dragon Helm, Helm option |
| Mercy | Greater | Corvane's Spire-Blade, Longsword option |

## Rewards and what it unlocks

Tier 4 pays gold/gear with fitting and one-item claims. Renown and Weirwalker are separate. No next line is specified; see quest rewards.

## If it goes wrong

1. Journal: check Redoubt type/count, current tavern and deadline.
2. Quests tab: inspect pending witnesses separately from completed objectives.
3. Held step: confirm prior line, registration, shared event access and building setup.
4. Instance/party: this Breach is shared; private quest instances cannot replace its receipts.
5. Retry timing: success normally waits one character hour; failure/setup failure waits one character day. Online deadlines charge played time; failure costs no standing.
6. Report: send step and receipt state through How this guide is checked. Reload/abandon recovery is unverified.

docs.title: What changed
docs.summary: Player-facing changes in the latest sync, plus the archived notes from the previous one.
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Current sync: 0df2d87eb (21 October 2026) → e4f093166 (24 October 2026).
> - The sea past Veilhaven's peace became an online open-PvP zone, with ship prizes, bounties, seasons, vaults and events.
> - Guns, a spell hand, account-owned homes, a 75-member guild cap, crafting writs, Collections, the event board and several dungeon changes arrived.
> - No new level or registration gate was set for these systems; the only registered number that changed was the guild cap (50 → 75).
> - Older entries remain below as an archive; they describe changes already present in the guide before this sync.

## Sync: 0df2d87eb to e4f093166 (21–24 October 2026)

### Sea and ships

- The Eltheric Ocean past Veilhaven's peace is an online open-PvP zone (ETHER-WILD). The same wild-zone law as the Wrothgarian Mountains applies: relay-refereed fights, death's drop and remains, four-times-stronger foes, and loot that rises through four depth bands (+25%, +50%, +75%, +100%). A death at sea rises at the nearest freeport's town, and the peace around Veilhaven and the Veil is safe. See The Eltheric Ocean.
- Ship-vs-ship prizes (SHIP-PVP): a wrecked and boarded ship is not a death — its captain keeps the hull's hold — but the boarder takes about one third of the hold's worth, at most eight pieces, held by the account service for collection. See Owning a ship.
- New sea activity: freeport bounties funded by players' gold, a realm season board, daily deep-sea elite vaults, the Aether Storm and treasure-fleet shared events, and the Eltheric Tidemail Aetheric set.

### Weapons and hands

- The Dwarven Pistolet is in the game: one-handed, Archery, uses Dwemer Pellets, deals 4–15 damage. Two pistols can be paired, and a pistol can be paired with a blade; the mixed pair's gun reloads in 2.8 s instead of 1.4 s (PISTOLET, MIXED-PAIR). Since GUNS-UNFOUND (23 October) neither gun drops, but pellets still drop and are still sold.
- A readied spell can share the hand with a one-handed weapon when the other hand is empty (SPELL-HAND); a two-hander or two occupied hands still use the classic cast.

### Homes, guilds and the interface

- Homes are the account's, bought by one character (ACCOUNT-HOMES). charid is the buyer whose three-home cap counts it, and deleting that character releases its homes. See Owning a home.
- A guild holds 75 members, not 50 (GUILD-CAP); the guild hall can be sold at its door by its guildmaster (GUILD-HALL-SALE), and the Guild tab is now a window of its own (GUILD-WINDOW).
- Collections (COLLECTIONS-II): titles, auras, profile icons and glyphs, where each comes from and whether it can be had now.
- The HUD event board and a grouped Timers window announce shared events (EVENTS1, TIMERS2), and the pause menu's season book shows the season's boards (SEASON-BOOK).
- NPC marks (NPC-MARKS): a bobbing gold ! over a quest person, a gold coin over a merchant and a blue gem over a guild servant, on Morrowind bodies.
- Middle mouse is the party ping (PARTY-PING), and auto-run moved to F3.

### Professions and economy

- Crafting writs (CRAFT-WRITS): up to three per account per UTC day, drawn within the character's best crafter's ranks, filled with goods the service saw made, and paid in Marks, craft XP, Renown and guild standing.
- Potion drops were cut to under half; a Novice's brew now makes two potions at 25 gold, and cooked food is lighter (CRAFT-PAYS, POT-THIN).

### Dungeons and world timing

- The Abyss Dungeon's Way Through portal stands beside everyone in the dungeon after the first person crosses the Rift, and beside each later arrival (SD-THROUGH).
- Unpicked boss/floor loot is mailed to the mailbox (LOST-SPOILS), so a missed floor is not always a loss.
- Wilderness spawned dungeons are 25% rarer (SPAWN-THIN): the 30% normal and 10% elite bands are kept on three quarters of the pixels that rolled them.
- Daily books turn up to ten minutes after 00:00 UTC (DAY-TURN): each book (professions, nodes, dungeon state, town state) turns its own UTC day within that spread.
- Several quest, chat and rendering fixes: keyboard focus in chat, quest giver/location names, travel-view stalls, snow on steep faces, horse posing and boat state.

### What did not change

The reviewed changes set no new character-level or registration gate for these systems. The stock-class revision belongs to the previous sync. The fact registry re-read 34 values at e4f093166: only guild.membersMax changed (50 → 75); the online-ruleset table gained the Event board and Morrowind People Marks rows.

## Previous sync: 4bba28c6c to 0df2d87eb (archive)

These changes were already in the guide before the current sync and are kept for returning readers. The source interval is 4bba28c6c..0df2d87eb (20–21 October 2026).

- Starfall can populate denser waves (up to 24 foes) under a dedicated spawn grant; the account claim record still counts at most nine stars per account per UTC day.
- Open Zone and professions: death gold drops show correctly when partly taken, and Enemy Expansion animals can be skinned for profession hides.
- Items and trading: loose-pack Essence can be spent on the Reforge; Enemy Expansion souls in Soul Gems no longer freeze trading.
- Chat and quest clarity: Tab/Space no longer hijack chat focus; quest responses identify the questor and the temple or guild hall.
- Travel and rendering: travel-view stalls reduced, horses posed on entry, held boats tracked, grass updates spread, snow on steep faces.
- Character and desktop: the eighteen stock classes have revised skill lists (movement skills keep a high tier only where they are the class's own; languages no longer take a tier slot); the Burglar is forbidden chain and plate; the desktop shell recovers from renderer loss.
- Shared-world timing: the online world carries an owner's clock through streets, buildings and dungeon foes without catch-up progress; shared foe updates are prioritized and bounded.

## Next

- Caps, timers and resets
- Questions new players ask

docs.title: Fighters Guild hunts
docs.summary: Read generated hunt offers, distinguish house and dungeon targets, and recognise protection or capture jobs.
docs.body:
Checked against e4f093166. This page describes DFO Online.

> [!tip] At a glance
> - Record the site, target and deadline before accepting.
> - Choose Your instance when the quest destination offers it.
> - Finish a hunt's required kills, then return to the hall.
> - Read protection and capture instructions before attacking.

## What every version shares

| Field | Shared shape and variations |
|---|---|
| Giver/guild | Fighters Guild questor at a hall |
| Typical gate | Membership and guild rank; some local hunts admit non-members |
| Where it sends you | Generated house, remote site or dungeon; protection adds people and destinations |
| Time limit | Offer-specific deadline; online deadlines charge played time — read the journal's Time remains |
| Reward shape | Script payment, often gold; eligible success can add gear and Renown |
| Instance | Private destination for you and your party when offered; quest dungeons are full-size |

## How to read the offer

Record region, site, creature, kill count, deadline and return contact; the journal may omit details. Species, count and payment vary. Check Quests and Time remains. These jobs differ from the questline ladder.

## The shapes you will see

1. House hunt. Wild Animal (M0B00Y06) and Unwanted Houseguest (M0B00Y07) place beasts in generated buildings. The journal names the job and deadline; follow the assigned property, not a later dungeon lead.
2. Dungeon hunt. Hunt for a Lycanthrope (M0B00Y00) sends you underground. Kill the assigned foe, then report back. An injury message alone does not satisfy the kill task.
3. Repeated attackers. A Rat Infestation (M0C00Y14) and Pack of Giants (M0B20Y02) require multiple kills. Remain at the assigned site for further spawns; check completion feedback before returning.
4. Protection and escort. Standard Protection (M0B21Y19) moves from a guarded house through investigation to an escort. Read letters and journal updates for the next contact and safe destination.
5. Capture exception. Runaway Pet (M0B00Y17) uses injury followed by the supplied bell. Keep the animal alive. Its journal distinguishes capture from killing; do not apply the hunt rule here.

## Quick path

1. Check the offer's gate and objective; prepare suitable weapons and healing.
2. Record destinations, deadline and return contact.
3. Travel to the named site and select the quest instance when offered.
4. Complete the required kills, protection, escort or tool interaction.
5. Read new entries and letters before leaving; follow any changed destination.
6. Return to the hall for ordinary hunts, or the named final contact for exceptions.

## What gets players stuck

Use this fix order:

1. Recheck the offer, building and active objective. Confirm the private instance; a public room can lack quest targets.
2. Inspect the 3D map, secret doors, containers and dressing. Keep quest objects separate from sale loot.
3. For slow spawns, stay at the site and read updates. Finish hunt targets; for capture, stop attacking when the tool becomes usable. A fast kill cannot be assumed reversible.
4. After leaving, return through the same quest-instance option. Recheck Time remains and the return journey; leaving is not completion.
5. If blocked, record the quest ID, site and last entry for a report. Reload and sold-item recovery are unverified online.

## Rewards and standing

See quest rewards: tier and gear choice depend on the quest and guild rank/character level. Gold has no universal amount. Online failure costs no faction standing; deliberate branches can still change standing. Offline failure differs.

- Quest rewards
