docs.title: The Hour That Was Not
docs.summary: Meet the Order of the Hour, break the Brass Remnant beneath an Abyss Dungeon, and choose who receives your account.
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Reach character level 12 online with a registered account.
> - Receive Prior Anselm Vey's letter outdoors in town by day.
> - Choose your recipient before descending through the Abyss Dungeon.
> - Break the Brass Remnant, then return to the Prior; entering the Orrery alone is insufficient.

Checked against e4f093166. Spoilers follow.

## Line facts

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Giver | Prior Anselm Vey of the Order of the Hour |
| Opens when | Character level 12; online; registered account |
| Steps | Two: QLHR01–QLHR02 |
| Tier | 4 throughout |
| Where it starts | Courier letter; generated temple |
| Feature/event needs | Shared Abyss Dungeon and Brass Remnant receipt; no extra step needs |
| What it unlocks | Witness of the Hour at the witnessed final step; no main-quest ending |

## How the line starts

Stand outdoors in town by day for the courier. A new line begins at most once per character hour, with no other first letter already travelling. Check Quests for level, registration or setup holds. If a required site cannot be generated, let setup retry from a suitable town. The journal names the Prior's temple and town; do not assume an Order affiliation identifies a fixed address.

The opening level belongs to this questline. It does not summon an Abyss Dungeon or replace the shared event's discovery and admission rules. Consult Abyss Dungeons before your expedition.

## Step table

| Step | Quest | Objective | Outcome effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Brass at Dusk | Meet the Prior at his temple | Standard pay; introduction |
| 2 | The Orrery of Endings | Choose a power, break the Remnant, report | Recipient rewards; witnessed title; completion |

## Walkthrough

### 1. Brass at Dusk

Read the first letter and travel to the named temple in its named town. Speak to Prior Anselm Vey. This step introduces the Hour and its Orrery of Endings beneath the Abyss Dungeons; it does not yet ask you to defeat the Remnant. The meeting pays the standard outcome and lets the runner prepare the next step.

If the letter is absent, check courier conditions and the Quests tab before searching temples. If you find a temple without the Prior, compare the complete destination with the letter, including the town. His faction does not make every temple a valid meeting place. There is no branch or dungeon instance to resolve here. Visit before the waiting deadline; missing him produces an unpaid failure and the normal retry, rather than completing the introduction through exploration alone.

### 2. The Orrery of Endings

Receive the second letter and visit the Prior at its current temple. Choose which Bay power receives your findings. The first prompt lists three courts and an Another power option; that opens the other three choices. Compare the outcomes below before committing. The choice concerns this account of the Hour, not a main-story ending.

With the assignment active, follow the shared Abyss event, descend past the Orrery and break the Brass Remnant. A closed event or an ordinary quest dungeon cannot substitute for this encounter. Check your objective and account receipt after the fight, then return to the Prior at the journal's temple. He pays the selected outcome only after the deed and report. Party help does not guarantee your own witness, and seeing the Orrery without breaking the Remnant leaves the combat objective unfinished.

## Choices and outcomes

All choices require the same expedition and return. Each court route gains standing with that court; Underking and Blades routes also affect the Order of the Hour. No reversal is scripted.

| Recipient | Payment | Standing effect | Named option |
|---|---|---|---|
| Daggerfall | Standard | Court gain | Lysandus's Remembrance, Amulet |
| Sentinel | Standard | Court gain | Sunfall Scimitar, Saber |
| Wayrest | Standard | Court gain | Eadwyre's Ward, Kite Shield |
| Orsinium | Standard | Court gain | Tusk of the Sixth Stone, War Axe |
| Underking | Greater | Underking gain; Order loss | Numidian Heartplate, Cuirass |
| Blades | Lesser | Blades and Order gains | Akaviri Oath, Katana |

> [!warning] A deliberate branch still matters
> Online failure costs no faction standing. That protection does not cancel the Underking route's Order penalty.

## Rewards and what it unlocks

Both sheets specify tier 4; the final branch sets the payment and named gear option. Equipment fitting can substitute a usable base, and you keep one item from an offer. The source specifies no fixed Renown amount for this line; successful-quest Renown follows the general tracker and cap. See quest rewards.

Witness of the Hour belongs to the final witnessed step. The account service checks the Brass Remnant receipt in the line's eligible window; the journal and title claim can progress separately. Earlier event participation does not by itself prove that claim. This line specifies no next questline unlock and does not choose or finish a classic main-quest ending.

## If it goes wrong

1. Journal: check current temple, recipient, Remnant objective and time remaining.
2. Quests tab: distinguish unfinished combat from an unwitnessed account claim.
3. Held step/event: confirm level, registration and site setup; follow the Abyss event's current admission phase.
4. Instance/party: the Abyss event is shared. A private quest copy cannot replace its deed; check your own receipt.
5. Retry timing: success normally waits one character hour; failure/setup failure waits one character day. Online deadlines charge played time, separately from delivery delays.
6. Report: record step ID, event and claim state through How this guide is checked. Reload or abandon is not a verified repair.

docs.title: Mages Guild fetches
docs.summary: Find generated quest objects, follow building clues, and prepare for spell-dependent recovery jobs.
docs.body:
Checked against e4f093166. This page describes DFO Online.

> [!tip] At a glance
> - Record the object's name, destination and deadline before accepting.
> - Search secret rooms and dressing as well as containers.
> - Keep the quest object until its hand-in is complete.
> - Check whether the job requires a particular spell.

## What every version shares

| Field | Shared shape and variations |
|---|---|
| Giver/guild | Mages Guild questor at a guild hall |
| Typical gate | Membership and rank; some fetches admit non-members |
| Where it sends you | Generated dungeon or building; clues can change the destination |
| Time limit | Offer-specific; online deadlines charge played time — read the journal's Time remains |
| Reward shape | Gold, an item or another scripted outcome; eligible success can add gear and Renown |
| Instance | Choose Your instance when offered; private quest dungeons are full-size and admit your party |

## How to read the offer

Record region, site, object, contact, deadline and spell/tool requirements; the journal may omit details. Check Quests and Time remains. Prepare access tools, but distinguish opening routes from performing a required spell.

## The shapes you will see

1. Loose dungeon ingredient. Grab an Ingredient (N0C00Y11) and Retrieve an Ingredient (N0B00Y04) place a specific object underground. The journal names the assignment and destination. Return that object, not ordinary ingredients.
2. Object carried by a foe. Mummy Wrappings (N0B00Y06) attaches wrappings to the quest mummy after an injury trigger. Inspect the corpse and carry the quest wrappings back. Combat alone does not complete hand-in.
3. Building search. Missing Book (N0C00Y10) uses an informant and a thief whose location changes with the time of day. Follow clues among the house, tavern and shop; return the book.
4. Spell-dependent task. Open a Chest (N0B00Y16) requires Open after meeting the merchant. Cast the Sleep spell (N0B00Y08) requires Sleep. Follow the journal's action; neither is an ordinary fetch.
5. Chained research. Azimuthal Vectors (N0B00Y17) can involve a scholar, clues and several dungeons. Read journal stages and letters for the next site.

## Quick path

1. Check membership/rank and required spells or tools.
2. Record the object, site, deadline and recipient; leave carrying space.
3. Follow the named contact or travel to the generated destination.
4. Enter the quest instance when offered and search methodically.
5. Collect the specific object or perform the requested spell; read updates.
6. Carry the object to the named recipient and confirm completion before selling loot.

## What gets players stuck

Work through these checks in order:

1. Re-read the latest objective. Confirm town, building, contact schedule and instance before searching again.
2. Inspect the 3D map, secret doors, containers and dressing. Check locked routes.
3. Confirm the actual quest item is in your inventory. Do not sell it; generic loot with a similar name may not count.
4. Read combat feedback. Injury can place an item on a carrier; inspect the corpse after a fast kill. For slow progress, check contact timing or missing spells.
5. If you left, re-enter the same quest instance. Check Time remains before another trip or hand-in.
6. Report the ID, destination and last entry if blocked. Online reload, replacement-item and sold-item recovery are unverified.

## Rewards and standing

Quest rewards explains payment: tier and gear choice depend on the quest and guild rank/character level. The carried object may be the objective, not payment. Online failure costs no faction standing; branch consequences remain. Offline failure differs.

docs.title: The Old Coil
docs.summary: Sail Hamid's packet lanes, face Sethrakul at sea, and choose between a sailor's offering and a scale trophy.
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Reach character level 8 online with a registered account.
> - Meet Hamid al-Rasheen at the tavern named in his letter.
> - Make qualifying port arrivals under sail while the packet-lanes step runs.
> - Follow the live serpent sighting, then compare the final blood/scale rewards.

Checked against e4f093166. Spoilers follow.

## Line facts

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Giver | Hamid al-Rasheen, a Sentinel packet captain |
| Opens when | Character level 8; online; registered account |
| Steps | Three: QLOC01–QLOC03 |
| Tier | 3 throughout |
| Where it starts | Courier letter; generated tavern |
| Feature/event needs | Sailing and shared Sea Serpent; no explicit naval step need in this line |
| What it unlocks | Satakal's Witness at the witnessed final step; no further line specified |

## How the line starts

Receive Hamid's letter outdoors in town by day. First letters are paced at most one new line per character hour, with no other first letter in flight. Check Quests for level, registration or a held step. Failed site setup retries later; use a suitable town. Hamid's Sentinel affiliation is not a fixed destination: read the generated tavern and town in each letter.

The line needs actual sailing, although its registry has no naval hold like the separate sea introduction. The serpent follows a shared event clock; receiving Hamid's letter does not summon it. See the sea serpent.

## Step table

| Step | Quest | Objective | Outcome effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | The Sailors' Tale | Meet Hamid at the named tavern | Standard pay; sailing assignment |
| 2 | The Packet Lanes | Make port twice under sail | Standard pay at sea; serpent assignment |
| 3 | The Shed Skin | Slay Sethrakul; report and choose | Blood/scale rewards; witnessed title; completion |

## Walkthrough

### 1. The Sailors' Tale

Read Hamid's invitation and travel to the tavern it names. Speak to him for the sailors' account of Satakal and Sethrakul, the Old Coil. This first step is a meeting, not a serpent kill or a sailing quota. The conversation pays the standard outcome and lets the runner prepare the packet-lanes assignment.

If the captain is absent, compare the tavern and town together rather than searching every inn in Sentinel. The quest generates his meeting place. If the first letter has not arrived, return to courier conditions and the Quests tab rather than sailing out to trigger it. The waiting deadline applies to this conversation; missing it produces an unpaid failure. There is no branch here, and a party member meeting Hamid does not replace checking completion on your own quest copy.

### 2. The Packet Lanes

Read the journal when this step starts; the assignment appears directly. Make port twice under sail, with sufficient travel between arrivals as described in the journal. Use actual sailing and port arrival, rather than treating a purchased passage or repeated nearby docking as equivalent. Earlier voyages do not replace actions during the running step.

Hamid meets you from his packet when the second qualifying arrival registers. The script pays the standard outcome there and ends the step, so you do not need an inland tavern report for this assignment. If it stays active, inspect the port objective before travelling back to the first meeting place. Plan a real route between ports and check that each arrival counts. No reward branch occurs here. The script's sailing-season failure wording is not a separate Starfall-style opening gate for this line.

### 3. The Shed Skin

Receive Hamid's next letter and note its return tavern before setting out. Follow the current harbor sighting and event phase to fight Sethrakul at sea. Bring companions where possible; the quest does not turn this shared encounter into a private instance. A sighting, joining the fight or sailing past the site is not the serpent-slain objective.

After the kill registers, check your own journal and account receipt, then visit Hamid at this step's tavern. He asks whether to return the blood to the sea for Satakal or keep the scale. This prompt resolves the offering; no additional journey to a fixed harbor is scripted. Compare the table before answering. Both choices complete the line, but their payment, standing and named equipment differ. If he still asks for the kill, inspect progress before expecting the final choice.

## Choices and outcomes

| Final choice | Payment | Other effect |
|---|---|---|
| Blood offering | Lesser | People of Sentinel standing gain; Walkabout Charm, Cloth Amulet option |
| Keep scale | Greater | Sethrakul's Scale, Round Shield option |

No reversal task is scripted.

## Rewards and what it unlocks

Tier 3 sheets specify standard early payments and the final branch above. Named rewards obey equipment fitting and one-item claim rules. Successful quests can earn general online Renown, with no line-specific amount promised. See quest rewards.

Satakal's Witness requires the final service witness. A local quest update is separate from the account's serpent receipt and title check; a kill predating the line does not automatically qualify. Neither branch specifies a subsequent questline unlock.

## If it goes wrong

1. Journal: check sailing arrivals, serpent objective, current tavern and deadline.
2. Quests tab: inspect waiting steps and pending witnesses separately.
3. Held step/event: confirm registration and site setup; follow the serpent's current sighting window.
4. Instance/party: the serpent is shared; check each player's progress and receipt.
5. Retry timing: success normally waits one character hour; failure/setup failure waits one character day. Online deadlines charge played time. Failure costs no faction standing.
6. Report: send step ID and event/claim state through How this guide is checked. Reload/abandon recovery is unverified.

## Next

- Quest browser · Line ladder · Quest rewards
- The sea serpent

docs.title: Temple errands
docs.summary: Distinguish exorcisms, relic recovery, healing, delivery and investigations before accepting a generated temple job.
docs.body:
Checked against e4f093166. This page describes DFO Online.

> [!tip] At a glance
> - Record the patient, recipient or target and every named destination.
> - Plan the return or delivery before accepting a tight clock.
> - Keep relics and medicine for their assigned recipient.
> - Read investigation updates before deciding whom to fight.

## What every version shares

| Field | Shared shape and variations |
|---|---|
| Giver/guild | Temple questor; some jobs belong to a particular deity's temple |
| Typical gate | Membership/rank for many jobs; non-member errands also exist |
| Where it sends you | Generated houses, contacts, remote sites or dungeons |
| Time limit | Offer-specific, sometimes tight or multi-stage; online deadlines charge played time — read the journal's Time remains |
| Reward shape | Scripted gold, religious object or gear; eligible success can add gear choice and Renown |
| Instance | Choose Your instance when offered; private quest dungeons are full-size and admit your party |

## How to read the offer

Record temple, region, building, contact, item and deadline. Identify the action: kill, investigate, heal, recover or deliver. Note the final recipient; deliveries can end away from the temple. Keep offer details alongside Quests; new entries can replace directions.

## The shapes you will see

1. Haunting or exorcism. The Haunted House (C0B00Y00) requires killing the assigned undead. The Possessed Child (C0B00Y02) uses contacts and a religious object. Follow the journal's house and leads; the child is not a hunt target.
2. Relic recovery. The Relic (C0B10Y15) places a talisman and lich in a dungeon; return the talisman, with defeating the lich affecting standing. The Stolen Item (C0C00Y12) uses a house contact. Follow the recovery objective.
3. Healing. The Healing (C0C00Y10) sends you between a patient and healer. Follow journal updates, obtain the remedy and carry it to the patient. Using it yourself is not hand-in.
4. Delivery. A Delivery (C0B10Y07) supplies a religious object for a remote recipient, with possible attackers. Deliver it before expiry; defeating attackers does not complete delivery.
5. Heretic investigation. The Heretic (C0B00Y01) moves through contacts, letters and evidence. Read journal stages and letters for the next lead. Investigate before attacking.

## Quick path

1. Check temple eligibility and prepare healing, access tools and suitable combat equipment.
2. Record the objective, destinations, recipient and deadline.
3. Collect or retain any supplied medicine, relic or letter.
4. Visit the named site; choose the quest instance when offered.
5. Perform the required interaction and read every new direction.
6. Reach the final recipient or return questor and confirm completion.

## What gets players stuck

Use this fix order:

1. Re-read the offer and newest entry. Confirm the exact temple, building, person and instance.
2. Search the 3D map for secret doors and unexplored rooms; inspect containers and dressing for missing relics.
3. Check inventory: retain quest medicine and relics; ordinary loot may not substitute.
4. Finish hunt kills; pause for investigation feedback before further attacks. Fast kills and slow triggers do not prove completion.
5. After leaving, return through the quest-instance option. Check Time remains before travel. Deadlines differ from requested waits.
6. Report the ID, site and last entry if blocked. Online reload and sold-item recovery remain unverified.

## Rewards and standing

See quest rewards: tier and gear choice depend on the quest and guild rank/character level. Payment varies. Success and deliberate branches can affect standing; online failure itself costs none. Offline failure differs. Failure protection does not erase branch or crime consequences.

## Next

- Questline ladder and courier letters for separate invitation-led lines.

docs.title: The Thirteenth of Frostfall
docs.summary: Hold fallen stars and decide the coven spindle's fate.
docs.gate: Level 6; online; registered account; Starfall event
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Begin at character level 6, registered online, during Starfall.
> - Ask a Wyrd Sister, or hold a star for Morwen's note.
> - Meet Morwen at the open-air coven.
> - Compare spindle choices; Heart-Star is optional.

Checked against e4f093166; spoilers follow.

## Line facts

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Giver | Morwen, Wyrd Sister of Glenmoril |
| Opens when | Character level 6; online; registered account; Starfall staged |
| Steps | Four: QLTF01–QLTF04 |
| Tier | 3 throughout |
| Where it starts | Letter/note; Glenmoril Coven |
| Feature/event needs | starfall on steps 1/3; ordered receipts |
| What it unlocks | Starwarden at step 3; spindle resolution |

## How the line starts

Check Festivals and Starfall and Quests. A Sister or raven brings the invitation. Ordinary couriers need town, outdoors, daylight; new lines wait one character hour and any pending first letter. Check event/site holds.

> [!online] Seasonal hold
> Steps 1/3 pause without failure when Starfall ends and resume when it returns. Steps 2/4 need no Starfall.

## Step table

| Step | Quest | Objective | Outcome effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Music in the Woods | Hold a star; meet Morwen | Standard pay |
| 2 | The Coven on the Bluff | Kill Spinner; bring spindle | Thread branch |
| 3 | Three Stars | Hold three more stars | Standard/Heart-Star bonus; title |
| 4 | What the Thread Is Worth | Resolve spindle's fate | Final branch; completion |

## Walkthrough

### 1. Music in the Woods

Once the line is active, speak to a Wyrd Sister at a tavern door for Morwen's letter. That conversation is optional: if you hold a fallen star first, her raven brings a note instead. Follow the event's current indication to a fallen star and complete its hold. Seeing the fall alone is insufficient; check your objective and account receipt.

Travel to the revealed Glenmoril Coven after holding the star. Morwen's meeting triggers on arrival at this open-air site, rather than through an indoor NPC marker. The meeting pays the standard outcome and advances the line. If you arrive before holding a star, finish that objective first. If Starfall ends, check the seasonal hold before treating the paused step as a failure. No reward branch occurs here.

### 2. The Coven on the Bluff

Receive the raven's letter and follow its revealed Bluff Coven destination. Arrival brings out the Spinner and her sisters at the open-air site. Defeat the Spinner to receive the spindle directly; searching a corpse is not required. Killing all three sisters is an optional objective. The Spinner's death still costs Sisters of the Bluff standing, separately from your later reward choice.

Bring the spindle to Glenmoril Coven and meet Morwen on arrival. Choose whether to sell a length of thread or deliver it whole. Selling pays more; keeping it whole gains Glenmoril standing. If the ambush vanished before the Spinner died, the script can call it again on a later arrival. Check inventory and journal before retrying. Once the spindle registers, the step stops its waiting timer for the return.

### 3. Three Stars

With this step active during Starfall, hold three more fallen stars. The star from the first assignment does not replace these new holds. Follow live omens and gather windows rather than returning to a remembered fall location. Each qualifying hold needs your account receipt; party company does not make another player's receipt yours. Check progress after each event.

The Heart-Star is an optional bonus if held while this step runs. It improves payment and adds a named ring option, but is not required to finish. Do not delay an otherwise complete objective expecting a later bonus: the step ends automatically when its hold count is reached. Morwen's raven brings payment without a return trip. If the festival ends first, the runner holds this star-dependent step for the next eligible event.

### 4. What the Thread Is Worth

Receive Morwen's letter and return to Glenmoril Coven. Arrival starts the final decision: burn the spindle in Hircine's fire, sell it to the Mages Guild, or take it to Arkay's priests. Burning resolves the quest there. The other choices give you the spindle and a journal entry naming the person, building and town for delivery.

For the Guild or Arkay route, carry the spindle to that named recipient and speak to them. Choosing a destination alone does not complete either delivery. These town sites are generated; the Arkay route requires its specified temple, not any priest. Compare the rewards below before answering, since no reversal is scripted. If setup is held, check required buildings. This step has no Starfall need, but its own waiting deadline still matters.

## Choices and outcomes

| Step / outcome | Pay | Other effect |
|---|---|---|
| 2: sell thread | Greater | No sheet standing gain |
| 2: whole thread | Lesser | Glenmoril standing gain |
| 3: ordinary / Heart-Star | Standard / greater | Heart: Heart-Star Ring, Ring option |
| 4: burn | Lesser | Glenmoril gain; Morwen's Hunt-Charm, Amulet |
| 4: Guild | Greater | Starglass Rod, Staff |
| 4: Arkay | Standard | Order of Arkay gain; Thread-Cutter, Dagger |

## Rewards and what it unlocks

Tier 3 follows quest rewards. Starwarden needs ordered star witnesses at step 3. Its Soul Cake purse pays once per account with the title during that account's festival. No next line is specified.

## If it goes wrong

1. Journal: check holds, spindle, destination/deadline.
2. Quests tab: distinguish objectives from pending witnesses.
3. Held step/event: check Starfall on steps 1/3 and site setup elsewhere.
4. Instance/party: covens are open-air; check your receipts.
5. Retry timing: success waits one character hour; failure/setup failure one character day. Seasonal holds differ. Deadlines charge played time; failure costs no standing. Spinner-kill standing applies.
6. Report: send step/claim state via How this guide is checked. Reload/abandon is unverified.

## Next

- Quest browser · Line ladder · Quest rewards
- Festivals and Starfall

docs.title: The Smith's Secrets
docs.summary: Set a gem, try the Reforge, and report to local armorers through an introduction to improving gear.
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Reach character level 4; both steps need Loot Rarity.
> - Receive the armorer's note outdoors in a town by day.
> - Bring your own gem and a piece with an available socket.
> - Complete each improvement while its quest is active, then report to its named armorer.

Checked against e4f093166; this guide describes DFO Online.

## Line facts

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Giver | An armorer, generated separately for each step |
| Opens | Character level 4; no separate online or registration gate in the line |
| Steps | Two: QLIG01–QLIG02 |
| Tier | 1 throughout |
| Start | Courier note; local armory and armorer |
| Feature needs | Loot Rarity for both steps; forced on online |
| Unlocks | Next lesson, then line completion; equipment systems are already available |

## How the line starts

Wait outdoors in town during daylight. The note starts the line. Another line's undelivered first letter can delay yours.

Check Quests if nothing arrives. Loot Rarity must be available before the first step starts. A missing local armory or suitable person can prevent setup; move to a larger town for the retry. The second step starts through the journal, with a newly generated armorer.

## Step table

| Step | Quest | Objective | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | A Stone in the Setting | Socket a gem and report | Payment; reforge lesson follows |
| 2 | Tempered Again | Reforge a piece and report | Payment; line complete |

## Walkthrough

### 1. A Stone in the Setting

Read the note for the armorer's name, shop and town before doing the work. Set a gem in an available socket while this quest runs, then speak to that armorer. The quest listens for the socketing action. A piece that already had a gem before the assignment is not proof that you performed the lesson. You supply the gem; the letter does not give you a starter stone.

Use the socket controls in your pack or at the Reforge. Choose a piece you can work on and identify it first. The assignment accepts any gem rather than demanding a particular kind or grade. Setting it has no separate service charge, but the stone becomes part of the item. Check the journal after setting it: once the report objective opens, return to the named shop. Speaking early only produces a reminder. The report pays and advances the line.

### 2. Tempered Again

Read the new journal entry before returning to the first armorer. This step creates another local armorer, so the report can belong to a different person and town. Visit a Mages Guild's Identify service for the Reforge. Bring an identified, unworn Magic or Rare piece with an eligible affix, plus Welkynd Shards and gold. Review the service's requirements before spending anything; the quest does not supply the materials or require a particular item base.

Perform a reforge while this step is active. Reforging rerolls an eligible line, so the result can be less useful than the old value. The quest checks that you used the operation, not that you obtained a stronger piece. Socketing another gem or choosing Hone does not perform this task. Once the journal records the reforge, speak to this step's armorer at the named armory. That report pays and completes the introduction.

## Choices and outcomes

There is no quest branch. Your gem and reforge selections affect equipment, not the line's outcome. Successful reports advance it; expiry is an unpaid failure.

> [!warning] Keep a gem deliberately
> Ordinary unsetting destroys the stone. Use the Reforge's paid Extract service if you want it returned intact.

## Rewards and unlocks

Both sheets specify standard payment and tier 1; the scripts award gold. The final sheet adds The Armorer's Temper, a named Cuirass option subject to equipment fitting. You keep one item from a gear offer. Successful quests can also earn online Renown XP under its normal limits. See quest rewards for claim rules. Completion introduces improvements without unlocking exclusive access to them.

## Recovery ladder

1. Read the journal's current armorer, address and objective.
2. Check Quests for a hold, wait or retry; confirm Loot Rarity.
3. Use an armory town for setup and daytime outdoor mail delivery.
4. Check socket availability, identification, equipment state and materials; report after the action.
5. No private dungeon is required.
6. Success normally waits one character hour; failure/setup retries after one character day. Online deadlines charge played time.
7. Report the quest ID and objective. Reload/abandon repair is unverified.

## Next

- Quest browser · Line ladder · Quest rewards
- Loot rarity · Sockets and reforging

docs.title: The Harbormaster's Word
docs.summary: Sail between ports, deliver a cargo contract, and force a ship to surrender through the sea introduction.
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Reach character level 5; every step needs Naval Combat.
> - Receive notes outdoors in a town by day; prepare a ship for the actual work.
> - Sail to another port, then complete a delivery contract from the harbormaster's board.
> - Make an enemy ship strike its colors and report to the final step's named harbormaster.

Checked against e4f093166; this guide describes DFO Online.

## Line facts

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Giver | A harbormaster; local tavern contacts for first and final reports |
| Opens | Character level 5; no separate account gate in the line |
| Steps | Three: QLIS01–QLIS03 |
| Tier | 2 throughout |
| Start | Courier note; first contact generated at a local tavern |
| Feature needs | Naval Combat and Come Sail Away enabled for the sea check |
| Unlocks | Next sea lesson, then completion; no exclusive ship-access unlock |

## How the line starts

Wait outdoors in town by day. Check Quests for a hold or retry. Naval Combat is enabled online; the runner also checks Come Sail Away. Another undelivered first letter can delay yours. Use a tavern town for setup retries.

## Step table

| Step | Quest | Objective | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Under Sail | Reach another port under sail; report | Payment; cargo lesson |
| 2 | A Hold Full | Finish a board delivery contract | Bonus at delivery; combat lesson |
| 3 | Strike Your Colors | Force a ship's surrender; report | Payment; line complete |

## Walkthrough

### 1. Under Sail

Record the harbormaster's name, tavern and town for your return. Take a ship from a port and sail into a different harbor. Walking between coastal towns and buying passenger travel do not perform the sailing action. Use your own vessel or arrange one through a Shipyard; the invitation does not grant a free hull. Consult the ship guide before leaving.

The arrival must register as a voyage, with enough distance sailed between ports. Follow the journal's distance instruction rather than shuttling around the same quay. Watch for progress after berthing. If unfinished, check that you sailed from another port and the harbor recognized your arrival. Return to the named tavern contact once the report opens. That conversation pays and advances the line.

### 2. A Hold Full

At the helm beside a quay, open the harbormaster's board and accept a delivery contract. Choose a reachable destination, transport the assigned cargo and complete delivery. Carrying ordinary trade goods does not finish a board contract. The objective listens for the contract system to confirm success. Read the next note before choosing work so you know the quest is running.

This step has no final tavern conversation. The quest bonus arrives when delivery completes, in addition to the contract's payment. Check Quests before travelling back to the original giver. If the step remains active, inspect the contract status rather than assuming that arriving at any port is sufficient. A sailing arrival and a completed cargo contract are separate events. Finish the contract while this step runs.

### 3. Strike Your Colors

Read the final note for its new harbormaster, tavern and town; the first giver's address may differ. Prepare for a naval fight and seek the hostile ships described by the assignment. Make a ship strike its colors through your own ship's guns. Being present when someone else wins is not the required action. Check your vessel and supplies before sailing.

Watch for the surrender objective to complete. Cargo runs and land battles cannot substitute. The script does not require a trophy, prize or wreck boarding for the report. Once surrender is recorded, return to this step's named harbormaster and speak to them. The conversation pays and completes the line. Use the ship guide for wider naval risks and preparation beyond this introduction.

## Choices and outcomes

No quest branch is scripted. Success advances the sequence; expiry pays nothing.

## Rewards and unlocks

Sheets specify tier 2 and standard payment; scripts award gold. The final Storm-Captain's Coat Cuirass option is subject to fitting. Keep one item per gear offer; online success can earn capped Renown XP. See quest rewards. Completion grants no ship.

## Recovery ladder

1. Read the journal's current objective and return address.
2. Check Quests; confirm Naval Combat and Come Sail Away.
3. Use a tavern town for setup and daytime outdoor mail.
4. Check arrival, delivery or surrender progress; no private dungeon is involved.
5. Success normally waits one character hour; failure/setup retries after one character day. Online deadlines charge played time.
6. Report quest ID and objective. Reload/abandon repair is unverified.

## Next

- Owning a ship

docs.title: The Merchant's Road
docs.summary: Collect and deliver quest loads for stable masters and merchants through an introduction to hauling.
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Reach character level 3 and receive the stable master's note outdoors in town by day.
> - Find the giver at the named tavern, rather than assuming the local Stable is the quest destination.
> - Collect the actual quest sack and carry it to the person named in the journal.
> - A wagon is optional for these quests; buying one does not complete either delivery.

Checked against e4f093166; this guide describes DFO Online.

## Line facts

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Giver | A stable master; a new local contact for each step |
| Opens | Character level 3; no online or registered-account gate in the line |
| Steps | Two: QLIR01–QLIR02 |
| Tier | 1 throughout |
| Start | Courier note; local tavern contact and remote General Store |
| Feature needs | No step needs switch; no wagon ownership check |
| Unlocks | Next hauling assignment, then completion; no wagon granted |

## How the line starts

Wait outdoors in town by day for the note. Check Quests if another line's undelivered first letter delays yours.

Setup needs a local tavern contact and a remote General Store merchant. Failed setup retries later; be in a substantial town. No feature holds either step. The second assignment enters the journal directly with a fresh local stable master.

## Step table

| Step | Quest | Objective | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | A Wagon's Load | Collect the local sack; deliver it to the remote buyer | Buyer pays; next haul follows |
| 2 | The Long Haul | Collect a remote sack; return it to this step's stable master | Stable master pays; line complete |

## Walkthrough

### 1. A Wagon's Load

Read the note for the stable master's tavern and town, then speak to that person to collect the load. This is a quest item, not a request to buy an equivalent collection of supplies. After collection, check the updated journal for the buyer's name, General Store and destination town. Record the full address before travelling, since a shop name alone can be misleading in a generated assignment.

Carry the sack to the named buyer and speak to them while you have it. Arriving in town without the load is not enough. A wagon can help with carrying goods, but this script does not require one: the delivery checks the quest sack and buyer interaction. You can carry the load yourself if your capacity allows. Keep it available for the hand-in rather than selling or discarding it. Payment comes from the buyer at the destination, so no return to the first stable master is required.

### 2. The Long Haul

Read this step's journal as a new assignment. The stable master is generated for this quest, often near the town where the previous delivery ended; do not assume the first giver is waiting for your return. Note both addresses: the remote merchant holding the load and the local tavern where this step's stable master receives it. The route now goes out to collect goods and back to the named recipient.

Travel to the listed General Store and speak to the named merchant. The sack is already paid for; collecting the quest item does not require purchasing replacement stock from the shop's trade inventory. Check that the journal records collection before leaving. Bring that sack back to the stable master at the current tavern and speak while carrying it. The return conversation awards payment and finishes the introduction. Neither a wagon purchase nor an unrelated merchant transaction replaces the two scripted interactions.

## Choices and outcomes

There is no branch. Your transport choice does not change the scripted payment outcome. Delivering the correct load succeeds; expiry is an unpaid failure.

> [!warning] Keep the quest load
> These assignments check their own sack. Ordinary goods of the same apparent kind do not substitute for it, and replacing a lost quest item is not a verified recovery method.

## Rewards and unlocks

Sheets specify tier 1 and standard payment; scripts award gold. The final The Carter's Gauntlets Gauntlets option is subject to fitting. Keep one item per gear offer; online success can earn capped Renown XP. See quest rewards. Completion grants no wagon or exclusive trade service.

## Recovery ladder

1. Read the journal's pickup and delivery addresses.
2. Check Quests for a wait or retry; confirm you carry the quest sack.
3. Use a tavern town for setup and daytime outdoor mail delivery.
4. Follow the named contacts; no private dungeon or hauling counter is involved.
5. Success normally waits one character hour; failure/setup retries after one character day. Online deadlines charge played time.
6. Report quest ID, item state and addresses. Reload/abandon repair is unverified.

## Next

- Quest browser · Line ladder · Quest rewards
- Wagons and hauling

docs.title: A Seat at the Table
docs.summary: Win a tavern card hand, then a King's Gambit game, and report to the regulars who invited you.
docs.gate: Level 2 · King's Gambit for second step
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Reach character level 2 and receive a regular's invitation outdoors in town by day.
> - Win a hand of Hold'em or Iliac Hand while the first step runs.
> - Enable The King's Gambit for the second step; it is your own setting online.
> - Report each win to the regular named in that step's journal.

Checked against e4f093166; this guide describes DFO Online.

## Line facts

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Giver | A tavern regular; generated separately for each quest |
| Opens | Character level 2; no separate online or registered-account gate in the line |
| Steps | Two: QLIT01–QLIT02 |
| Tier | 1 throughout |
| Start | Courier-delivered playing-card invitation; local tavern |
| Feature needs | First step has none; second needs The King's Gambit enabled |
| Unlocks | Next game lesson, then completion; no exclusive table access |

## How the line starts

Wait outdoors in town by day for the invitation. The card starts the line. Another undelivered first letter can delay yours; check Quests.

Use a tavern town for setup retries. The second quest enters the journal directly with another regular. The King's Gambit defaults on but remains your setting online. Disabling it holds the second step; the first can still proceed.

## Step table

| Step | Quest | Objective | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | A Hand of Cards | Win a qualifying card hand; report | Payment; Gambit lesson follows |
| 2 | The King's Gambit | Win a Gambit game; report | Payment; line complete |

## Walkthrough

### 1. A Hand of Cards

Read the invitation for the regular's name, tavern and town. Visit a tavern card table and play Hold'em or Iliac Hand while this quest is active. The tracked event is a hand whose main pot you win. Merely sitting down, watching another player, or leaving a hand unfinished does not meet that objective. You can play against locals or other players; the quest does not require beating the particular regular who sent the invitation.

Choose a stake you can afford while learning. The quest's later payment does not guarantee that your table play will be profitable. Watch the journal for the win to be recorded before travelling back. Once the report objective opens, speak to the invitation's named regular at the listed tavern. Winning alone does not end this step: that conversation pays and advances the line. A reminder from the regular means the required win has not yet been recorded.

### 2. The King's Gambit

Check Quests after the first report and read the new contact's address. This step creates another regular, so returning to the previous table's giver can leave you speaking to the wrong person. If the step is waiting on The King's Gambit, enable that feature before looking for its assignment. Ordinary card wins do not replace a Gambit victory. With the feature off, tables offer the other card games instead.

Play a complete King's Gambit game against a tavern regular or another player. Protect your king and defeat the opposing king; opening the board or winning an ordinary card hand is not the tracked event. Perform the win while this step runs, then check the journal for the report objective. Return to the regular named in this quest and speak to them. That conversation awards payment and completes the introduction. The script asks for a victory, without requiring a particular opponent or army composition.

## Choices and outcomes

There is no quest branch. Choosing a game, opponent or stake affects your play, not a permanent story outcome. Success advances the line; expiry produces an unpaid failure.

> [!tip] Check the kind of win
> The quests count different events: a card-hand win first, a Gambit-game win second. Complete the current objective before returning to its regular.

## Rewards and unlocks

Sheets specify tier 1 and standard payment; scripts award gold. The final The Regular's Lucky Charm jewel option has base Mark, subject to fitting. This is equipment, not Marks currency. Keep one item per gear offer; online success can earn capped Renown XP. See quest rewards. Completion grants no exclusive table access.

## Recovery ladder

1. Read the journal's game, regular and address.
2. Check Quests for a hold, wait or retry; enable Gambit for its step.
3. Use a tavern town for setup and daytime outdoor mail delivery.
4. Record the required win, then report. No private dungeon is involved.
5. Success normally waits one character hour; failure/setup retries after one character day. Online deadlines charge played time.
6. Report quest ID, game and objective. Reload/abandon repair is unverified.

- Tavern games

docs.title: The Herald's Call
docs.summary: Win Arena ladder bouts in Daggerfall and collect the Herald's introductory purses.
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - Play online at character level 6 or higher.
> - Receive the Herald's broadsheet outdoors in a town by day.
> - Visit the Arena's Herald in Daggerfall and choose the Ladder.
> - Win a ladder bout for the first quest, then three more while the second quest runs.
> - Quest purses pay on the qualifying wins; no separate return conversation is scripted.

Checked against e4f093166; this guide describes DFO Online.

## Line facts

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Giver | The Arena's Herald |
| Opens | Character level 6, online; no additional registration gate in this line |
| Steps | Two: QLIA01–QLIA02 |
| Tier | 2 throughout |
| Start | Courier broadsheet; bouts at the Arena in Daggerfall |
| Feature needs | No step needs switch; online Arena ladder access for the actions |
| Unlocks | Next challenge, then introduction complete; no rated-rank unlock specified |

## How the line starts

Wait outdoors in town by day for the broadsheet. Another undelivered first letter can delay yours. Check Quests for the online gate or wait.

These scripts place no local person or building. The invitation can find you elsewhere; the bouts are at Daggerfall's Arena. The second challenge enters the journal directly after the step delay. Wait for it before earning its wins.

## Step table

| Step | Quest | Objective | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | First Blood | Win a ladder bout | Automatic quest purse; next challenge |
| 2 | A Name in the Sand | Win three ladder bouts during this step | Automatic quest purse; line complete |

## Walkthrough

### 1. First Blood

Read the broadsheet and confirm First Blood is running before entering a bout. Go to the Arena in the city of Daggerfall and use the Herald at its gate to open the Ladder. Choose a ladder opponent and win your own bout. The quest counts the ladder victory event; a duel in the shared world, a player-versus-player Arena match, or watching someone else's bout does not perform that event. Practice in the pit also does not count.

Read the Arena's bout information before entering, since it uses its own match rules. The quest does not require a rated victory or a particular season rating. When the qualifying win is recorded, the script awards its gold and ends the step automatically. There is no generated quest NPC to find afterward for a report. Check Quests after the result to distinguish a completed first lesson from the next challenge waiting to begin.

### 2. A Name in the Sand

Wait for the second quest's journal entry before starting its work. This step counts three ladder wins made while it runs. The victory that completed First Blood does not carry forward into that total, and wins earned before the new assignment starts do not satisfy it. Use the Herald's Ladder again and keep checking the quest objective as you progress, rather than treating your overall Arena history as the quest's counter.

You need wins, not merely entries or finished matches. Losses and draws do not provide the victory event, and rated player matches remain separate from the ladder task. The script specifies no particular opponent names or requirement for consecutive wins. Once the required wins are recorded, the quest pays automatically and completes the line. You do not need to search for a tavern contact or click a separately generated Herald. Read the completion state and inspect any waiting gear offer before leaving the Arena.

## Choices and outcomes

There is no branch. Winning advances the introduction; expiry is an unpaid failure. Only ladder victories count toward success.

> [!online] Ladder progress and rating are separate
> The introductory quests count ladder bouts. Rated play has its own account and season rules; completing this line does not promise a rating increase or season prize.

## Rewards and unlocks

Sheets specify tier 2 and standard payment; scripts award gold on the win task. The final The Crowd's Favor Bracelet option is subject to fitting. Keep one item per gear offer; online success can earn capped Renown XP. See quest rewards. No account title, fixed rank or exclusive rated access is specified.

## Recovery ladder

1. Read the current journal's win requirement.
2. Check Quests for online status, delays or retries.
3. Receive mail outdoors in town by day; no local building is generated.
4. Confirm your own Ladder victory; practice, spectating and player bouts do not count.
5. No quest-dungeon instance is involved.
6. Success normally waits one character hour; failure retries after one character day. Online deadlines charge played time.
7. Report quest ID, mode and result. Reload/abandon repair is unverified.

## Next

- Quest browser · Line ladder · Quest rewards
- The Arena

The quest counts the ladder victory event; a duel in the shared world, a player-versus-player Arena match, or watching someone else's bout does not perform that event. Practice in the pit also does not count.

2-a-name-in-the-sand.title: 2. A Name in the Sand
2-a-name-in-the-sand.excerpt: Wait for the second quest's journal entry before starting its work. This step counts three ladder wins made while it runs. The victory that completed First Blood does not carry forward into that total, and wins earned before the new assignment starts do not satisfy it. Use the Herald's Ladder again and keep checking the quest objective as you progress, rather than treating your overall Arena history as the quest's counter.

choices-and-outcomes.title: Choices and outcomes
choices-and-outcomes.excerpt: There is no branch. Winning advances the introduction; expiry is an unpaid failure. Only ladder victories count toward success.

rewards-and-unlocks.title: Rewards and unlocks
rewards-and-unlocks.excerpt: Sheets specify tier 2 and standard payment; scripts award gold on the win task. The final The Crowd's Favor Bracelet option is subject to fitting. Keep one item per gear offer; online success can earn capped Renown XP. See quest rewards. No account title, fixed rank or exclusive rated access is specified.

docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - The first-session answers come first; the later sections follow the stages you meet them in.
> - Each answer is one sentence, followed by the page that explains it.
> - Where online play differs from offline Daggerfall Unity, the linked page names the effective online rule.

## First session

### Is DFO Online free?
The client is free and open source, and Daggerfall itself has been free since 2009; you supply the game data. See What DFO Online is and Playing in the browser.

### Do I need to own Daggerfall to play?
Yes — the game reads the original Daggerfall data files, which are not bundled, and the official site points to free sources. See Playing in the browser.

### Which files does the game ask for?
It asks for the ARENA2 folder of your own Daggerfall install (under DF/DAGGER/ARENA2 in a Steam copy), or a zip of it on a phone, and it remembers the pick. See Your first launch.

### Does it run on Mac, Linux or a phone?
The browser client runs in a current desktop browser or on a phone, and the optional desktop app ships for Windows, macOS (Apple silicon) and Linux. See Playing in the browser.

### Do I need a registered account?
You can play as a guest, but professions, the market, player guilds, Marks, festival rewards and several questlines need a registered account, so register before you invest. See Your account.

### What happens when I die, and do I lose my items?
You respawn at a safe point with half health and lose one tenth of the gold you carry, while an ordinary death keeps your items; the Open Zone and a revenant's theft are separate exceptions. See Dying online.

### How does saving work, and is my progress safe?
Offline saves are browser-storage slots or desktop files, an online character is held by the account service and saves as you go, and loading during online play is disabled. See Saving and returning.

### How do I make my first money?
Early gold comes from introduction quests (100–400 gold a step), bounties and the loot you sell at any counter, and banking the leftovers protects it. See Making money.

### Where should I stand for questline letters?
A letter reaches you only outdoors in a town by day, one new line starts at most once per character hour, and a step that needs a building waits for a town that has it. See Courier letters.

### Which guild should I join, and what does it cost?
An NPC guild hall takes an application when your standing and guild skills qualify and the source names no joining fee, while a player guild costs 10000 gold and Renown 10 to found. See The NPC guilds and Player guilds.

### Can I respec later?
Firmament refunds are free below Renown 10 and cost 10 Marks a star after that, a whole-sky respec is 10000 gold, a specialisation change is 1,000 Marks, a skill swap is 100,000 gold, and a mastery can never be undone. See The Firmament, Craft specialisations and Masteries and specialisations.

### Can other players attack me?
Not in ordinary play; player damage happens in duels you accept, Arena bouts, guild sieges and the Wrothgarian Open Zone. See Meeting other players and The Open Zone.

### How do I report a bug or a player?
/bug opens the private issue form, /report  reports conduct, and the Discord or issue tracker carry anything the in-game forms miss. See Keys and commands.

### How much time does the game ask, and what is the endgame?
The source sets no completion time; Renown runs to 50, questlines open through level 12, and the late game is Elite Gates, Abyss Dungeons, Arena seasons, the Open Zone, the Eltheric Ocean and Legacy. See The questline ladder and Catching up.

### What does the Draft badge mean?
Draft means the page has been checked against the game's source but not yet read end to end by the maintainer for sense or contradictions. See How this guide is checked.

## Modes, mods and getting unstuck

### What is the difference between offline and online?
Offline is DFO's single-player game on this device; online adds an account, the shared ruleset, other players, Marks, Renown, the market, guilds, events and the account-held character. See Offline and online.

### Do I need to decide a mode before creating a character?
Yes. The front door asks Online or Offline first, and a character belongs to one of those worlds; an offline DFO character can be brought online once, and an online character copied to offline. See Offline and online.

### Can I use Daggerfall Unity or Nexus mods?
No. DFO has no mod support and does not load DFU mods, Nexus mods or load orders; the Features rows are the game's own systems and settings, and online their scope is fixed for everyone. See Mods, saves and wipes.

### Can I import my Daggerfall or Daggerfall Unity save?
Not yet. DFO characters are created in DFO; the only transfers are its own offline-to-online and online-to-offline doors, not saves from another game. See Mods, saves and wipes.

### Will my character be wiped at launch or between seasons?
The source and the official site state no wipe schedule. What resets is seasonal standing in the Arena and city control, not the character; character deletion is the permanent, player-triggered act. See Mods, saves and wipes.

### How do I play with a friend?
Add the player as a friend, form a party, meet or use party travel, and remember that kills, quest sharing, shared containers and mentor mode have separate rules. See Play with a friend.

### Why can't I hit anything?
Check weapon skill, fatigue, weapon condition, target armour, range and the enemy's tells before blaming the character; online combat uses PCAAO's hit and damage rules. See Combat maths.

### Where do I store gold, loot and materials safely?
Gold belongs in the bank; ordinary death only takes part of carried gold. Homes, wagons, ship holds, profession Stores and guild vaults hold different goods and have different risks; the Open Zone is the exception. See Safe storage.

### Why do guards and guilds treat me differently?
Three separate tracks are at work: People reputation, legal standing in each region, and faction standing with a guild or temple. One does not repair another. See Standing and reputation.

### I am stuck in a quest, or an NPC is missing. What do I do?
Use the recovery ladder before assuming a bug: re-read the journal, check a held step, try /unstuck, look for the NPC in the right place and time, then restart or report. See Stuck and recovery.

### I know Daggerfall or Daggerfall Unity. What changed?
Fifteen online deltas matter first: walked travel, PCAAO combat, telegraphed attacks, the forced ruleset, no mid-session load, death as respawn, Marks, Renown, immediate guild promotions and online quest behaviour. See Coming from Daggerfall or Daggerfall Unity.

## Character creation

### Does race change my attributes?
No; attributes come from your class plus a roll and then your bonus points, while race sets your look, some defences and online weapon bonuses. See Choosing a race.

### Which class should I choose?
Choose by the skills and role you want to play; compare the options in Classes.

### Can I make my own class?
Yes; the custom builder lets you set skill tiers, health, attributes, advantages and disadvantages. Read Custom classes.

### What should a warrior, mage, thief or hybrid prioritize?
Each style asks for a different balance of combat, magic and utility skills; see Choosing a playstyle.

### What should I double-check before entering the world?
Review the creation summary, your class skill tiers and any custom-class restriction, because the final summary does not show your biography answers and the source provides no general undo. See Choices that are hard to undo.

### What does Layered Gearing do?
It presents worn armour on your character model; see Appearance and Layered Gearing.

## Playing online

### Why does online play force some settings?
Shared-world systems override local switches so everyone in a room meets the same world and balance; see Online rules at a glance.

### What key swings my weapon?
The default is the right mouse button, but the Controls screen shows your current binding. See Keys and commands.

### What key uses a weapon technique?
The default technique action is the mouse's back side button, and you can rebind it in Controls. See Keys and commands.

### Why does Enter open chat?
Online, Enter opens chat; press Y to free the mouse cursor instead. See Keys and commands.

### Where do I change key bindings?
Open Settings › Controls › Key bindings; see Keys and commands.

### How do I find the available chat commands?
Type /help; other in-game lists include /lang, /emotes and /breach help. See Keys and commands.

### Why did my command not appear in chat?
Unknown slash commands are refused rather than sent as ordinary text, and a line beginning // sends text that begins with a slash. See Keys and commands.

## Progress and events

### What is the difference between character level and Renown?
They are separate tracks: character level follows your skills, while Renown is the online ladder to 50 that adds health and spell points and opens systems. See Renown.

### When do I unlock the Firmament?
The Written in the Stars introduction opens at character level 3, and the tree itself is in the pause menu's Growth tab. See The Firmament.

### Why did I stop earning Marks or Renown?
Account ceilings, service windows and event receipts use different scopes; check Caps, timers and resets.

### When does a daily cap reset?
Many account caps use UTC days, while service rate limits reset each clock hour; see Caps, timers and resets.

### How often can I fight the same Arena opponent for rating?
Rated pairs are limited to five counted bouts per UTC day and ten per season. See Arena seasons and the Royal Tourney.

### Is the Royal Tourney part of the Arena season?
No; it runs through a proclaimed seat week and has its own pair limit. See Arena seasons and the Royal Tourney.

### What unlocks ordinary elite enemies?
Elite spawns begin at level 3 and Renown 5 in your own world. See Elite Gates and the Elite Breach.

### Does level 12 unlock the Abyss Dungeon itself?
No; level 12 opens The Hour That Was Not, and the shared dungeon has its own spawn cycle. See Abyss Dungeons.

### How do I start the Elite Breach commands?
Use /breach, and /breach help lists the options. See Elite Gates and the Elite Breach.

### What can happen to my items in the Open Zone?
Eligible carried items and cart contents can be left in shared remains after PvP death. See The Open Zone.

### Is Project Legacy forced on every online character?
No; it is player-owned. See Legacy.

### How much gold can an heir inherit?
The estate is one quarter of carried gold, capped at 9,900. See Legacy.

### Is there a level requirement for the Eltheric Ocean?
The source sets no universal character-level gate for it, but past Veilhaven's peace the sea is an online open-PvP zone with four-times-stronger foes and death's drop. See The Eltheric Ocean.

### Where can I see recent changes?
This sync's player-facing changes are on What changed.

### What does an unfamiliar handbook term mean?
Look it up in the Glossary.

docs.title: Thieves Guild work
docs.summary: Read theft and smuggling offers, protect the assigned goods, and recognise when a quiet job changes direction.
docs.body:
Checked against e4f093166. This page describes DFO Online.

> [!tip] At a glance
> - Record the object, contacts, destination and deadline before accepting.
> - Keep assigned goods for delivery; they are not your payment.
> - Read demands and new directions before continuing a fight.
> - Guild employment does not protect you from the watch.

## What every version shares

| Field | Shared shape and variations |
|---|---|
| Giver/guild | Thieves Guild work in the General Populace pool; giver recorded as thief |
| Gate | Member jobs have rank requirements; initiation is separate |
| Where | Generated houses, sites and contacts; some destinations appear after starting |
| Time | Offer-specific deadlines; online these charge played time |
| Reward shape | Scripted gold or items; eligible success can add gear and Renown |
| Instance | Choose Your instance when offered; private quest dungeons are full-size and admit your party |


## How to read the offer

Record region, building, object, recipient, return contact and deadline. Check Quests and Time remains. Smuggling may exchange cargo for something you must carry back. Names, defenders and payment vary.

Membership starts through an invitation; see thievery and NPC guilds. These jobs differ from the questline ladder.

## The shapes you will see

1. House theft. Valuable Artwork (O0B10Y05) and The Jewel Heist (O0B10Y06) place an object in a generated house. Find that object and return it; defeating defenders alone does not finish the job.
2. Exchange and return. A Hot Stone (O0B00Y00) and Arms Supply (O0B00Y01) exchange supplied goods for gems. Visit the assigned contact, then carry the proceeds to the giver.
3. Changing delivery. Drugs Delivery (O0B00Y12) introduces a note and alternate contact. Read the note and current entry before choosing your recipient.
4. Compromised heist. Antique Ivory (O0B00Y11) can lead from theft to a safehouse after trouble. Follow the changed destination. Injury-triggered demands make persuasion and quiet violence choices to read, rather than a reason to attack everyone.


## Quick path

1. Check membership, rank and the offered action.
2. Record destinations, contacts, goods and deadline; prepare access tools.
3. Collect supplied goods or visit the assigned property.
4. Choose the quest instance when offered and find the specific object.
5. Read new notes, demands and journal entries before acting.
6. Complete every exchange and reach the final recipient with the assigned goods.


## What gets players stuck

Use this fix order:

1. Confirm the latest destination, named building and instance. Generated sites have no universal map pin; ask for directions.
2. Search rooms, secret doors, containers and dressing. Separate the quest object from sale loot; do not keep it as a trophy.
3. Check combat feedback before further attacks. Some demands trigger on injury; a fast kill is not proof that every stage ran.
4. Recheck the deadline and changed contacts. If necessary, leave and re-enter through the same instance option.
5. Treat guards and witnesses as a legal problem: the law still applies. Report a blocked quest with its ID, site and last entry; online reload and sold-item recovery remain unverified.


## Rewards and standing

See quest rewards for variable payment and eligible gear. Ordinary online failure has no faction penalty; scripted choices and crimes remain separate. Arms Supply penalises surrendering or retaining goods.

docs.title: Dark Brotherhood contracts
docs.summary: Identify the assigned execution target, follow town or dungeon leads, and distinguish contracts from the one-time initiation.
docs.body:
Checked against e4f093166. This page describes DFO Online.

> [!tip] At a glance
> - Record the target, destination, deadline and reporting contact.
> - Kill the assigned target; unrelated casualties do not replace it.
> - Follow town leads before searching every building.
> - Keep witnesses, guards and legal consequences in your plan.

## What every version shares

| Field | Shared shape and variations |
|---|---|
| Giver/guild | Brotherhood questor; invitation contact for initiation |
| Gate | Member contracts have rank requirements; the prospect test is one-time |
| Where | Generated dungeon, palace or town buildings |
| Time | Offer-specific deadline; online deadlines charge played time |
| Reward shape | Gold or another scripted outcome; eligible success can add gear and Renown |
| Instance | Your instance when offered; private quest dungeons are full-size and admit your party |


## How to read the offer

Record region, site, target description, deadline and return contact. Names and enemy types vary. Follow the assigned target, not a townsperson with a similar role. Check Quests and Time remains.

Joining needs an invitation and successful initiation; see thievery and NPC guilds. Do not assume a one-time assignment returns after refusal or failure.

## The shapes you will see

1. Dungeon execution. A Fateful Song (L0B10Y01) assigns a bard in a generated dungeon. Kill the quest target and report back; exploring the dungeon without the kill is insufficient.
2. Variable opponent. A Knight Without Honor (L0B20Y02) selects different combat classes. Follow the assigned site and completion feedback.
3. Palace contract. An Anonymous Job (L0B30Y09) and Concerns of a Noble (L0B40Y04) use generated palaces. Complete the execution there and return to the Brotherhood contact.
4. Town investigation. Taking on the Thieves Guild (L0B50Y11) involves local leads and possible target locations. Question the named contact and follow the location information before hunting the mark.
5. Initiation exception. The Acceptance Test (L0A01L00) is one-time. Follow the apothecary, supplied poison and decanter interactions, including replacing the decanter. Killing guards does not substitute for those steps.


## Quick path

1. Check eligibility and whether this is initiation or member work.
2. Record the target, destinations, contact and clock.
3. Prepare combat, access tools and a route back.
4. Follow contacts to the assigned site; select the quest instance when offered.
5. Perform the required execution or initiation interactions; read updates.
6. Return to the named contact and confirm completion.


## What gets players stuck

Fix order:

1. Recheck the target, current lead, building and instance. Generated locations are not fixed landmarks.
2. Ask for directions; search unexplored rooms and secret doors underground.
3. Confirm kill feedback. If a fast kill gives no update, do not assume another unrelated kill will repair it; preserve the last entry for reporting.
4. For initiation, check supplied items and required interactions. Poison and the decanter are quest objects, not ordinary loot to sell or consume.
5. Check the deadline and return contact. Guards and witnesses remain subject to the law; a contract is no legal immunity.
6. Report the ID, site and last completed action if blocked. Online reload, replacement items and one-time retry recovery are unverified.


## Rewards and standing

Quest rewards separates payment, eligible gear, Renown and standing. No universal purse applies. Ordinary online failure costs no faction standing; scripted consequences and crimes remain separate.

docs.title: Knightly order quests
docs.summary: Distinguish traitor hunts, monster clearing and rescues, then report the right result to your order.
docs.body:
Checked against e4f093166. This page describes DFO Online.

> [!tip] At a glance
> - Record the order, destination, target and deadline.
> - Read whether the job needs a kill, several kills or a conversation.
> - Speak to a rescue target before returning to the hall.
> - Treat order standing and immediate payment as separate benefits.

## What every version shares

| Field | Shared shape and variations |
|---|---|
| Giver/guild | Knightly order questor |
| Gate | Member jobs depend on rank; some work admits non-members |
| Where | Generated dungeons or local houses; rescues add a person to find |
| Time | Assignment-specific deadline; online deadlines charge played time |
| Reward shape | Scripted outcome and standing; eligible success can add gear and Renown |
| Instance | Choose Your instance when offered; full-size private quest dungeons admit your party |


## How to read the offer

Record order, region, site, target, action and return contact. Enemy type, destination, eligibility and reward vary. Check Quests and Time remains. Read rescue instructions before assuming an escort route.

See NPC guilds for joining and rank. Non-member work does not establish membership. These jobs differ from the questline ladder.

## The shapes you will see

1. Traitor hunt. Retribution (B0B00Y01) and the non-member The Traitor (B0C00Y05) place a nightblade in a generated dungeon. Defeat the assigned foe, then report back.
2. Monster hunt. Killing a Giant (B0B40Y09) and More Trouble with Orcs (B0B20Y07) require the designated dungeon kill. Clearing unrelated enemies is not the objective.
3. Dragon hunt. The Dragonslayer (B0B70Y16) assigns a dragonling. Prepare for it and follow the generated dungeon.
4. Rescue. The Princess (B0B00Y00) places a person and vampire underground. Speak to the person, read updates and report back; the kill alone is insufficient.
5. Local infestation. The Infested House (B0C00Y13) admits non-members and requires multiple beasts. Stay at the assigned house for further attackers and confirm the required kills before returning.


## Quick path

1. Check the order and the offer's membership or rank requirement.
2. Record destination, objective, deadline and reporting contact.
3. Prepare weapons, healing and tools for locked or difficult routes.
4. Enter the named site through the quest-instance option when offered.
5. Complete the assigned kills or speak to the rescue target.
6. Read updates and return to the questor for confirmation.


## What gets players stuck

Use this fix order:

1. Confirm the exact generated site and instance. A public room may lack the quest target; ask for directions to a named house.
2. Check the 3D map, secret doors and unexplored rooms before declaring a person missing.
3. Re-read the action. Rescues need contact; infestations need more than the first kill. Check feedback after a fast kill rather than assuming the stage completed.
4. Keep any letters or quest objects apart from sale loot. A similarly named ordinary item is not a substitute.
5. Check Time remains, then revisit through the same instance option if necessary. Report the quest ID, destination and last entry if blocked. Online reload and item recovery remain unverified.


## Rewards and standing

See quest rewards for eligible gear and Renown. Several scripts pay no gold. The Dragonslayer explicitly improves order standing. Rank gifts are separate services. Ordinary online failure costs no faction standing; scripted consequences remain distinct.

docs.title: Noble work
docs.summary: Plan deliveries, exchanges and discreet violence for nobles while watching changing deadlines and hidden standing costs.
docs.body:
Checked against e4f093166. This page describes DFO Online.

> [!tip] At a glance
> - Record every recipient and whether you must return with an exchanged item.
> - Recheck the clock after each handover.
> - Payment can accompany a loss of standing with another faction.
> - Read refusal and surrender choices before committing.

## What every version shares

| Field | Shared shape and variations |
|---|---|
| Giver/guild | Noble questor; social work |
| Gate | Character level or reputation; some offers restrict gender, adult content or repeat acceptance |
| Where | Generated contacts, palaces and dungeons; some places appear only after starting |
| Time | Often tight, sometimes separate delivery legs; online deadlines charge played time |
| Reward shape | Scripted gold or objects; eligible success can add gear and Renown |
| Instance | Your instance when offered; full-size private quest dungeons admit your party |


## How to read the offer

Record patron, region, contacts, cargo, deadline and final recipient. Check whether delivery ends the task or starts another leg. Recheck Quests and Time remains after exchanges: another clock may start.

Read refusal prompts before deciding; the family has no universal safe-refusal rule. Distinguish generated work from named story invitations and the questline ladder.

## The shapes you will see

1. Direct delivery. A Peace Offering (R0C10Y13) uses a palace contact; Contraband Goods (R0C10Y11) uses another generated recipient. Carry the assigned object and confirm hand-in.
2. Exchange and return. Gold Smuggling (R0C10Y02) exchanges a gold bar for an item the patron wants back. Keep the return cargo and read demands from attackers before surrendering it.
3. Chained delivery. A Special Substance (R0C10Y17) and An Item on Loan (R0C10Y18) add another item, recipient and clock. Record the new destination.
4. Discreet violence. Deadly Diplomacy (R0C10Y05) assigns a dungeon opponent. Complete the kill, then find the named payment contact.
5. Recovery. The Heirloom (R0C10Y06) places a trinket underground. Recover that object; ordinary jewellery does not replace it.


## Quick path

1. Read eligibility, objective and refusal choices before accepting.
2. Record every named contact, destination, item and clock.
3. Plan the route and leave space for exchanged goods.
4. Visit the contact or enter the quest instance when offered.
5. Deliver, recover or defeat the assigned target; read updates.
6. Follow each new leg and reach the stated final recipient.


## What gets players stuck

Use this fix order:

1. Recheck the latest leg, recipient and clock; the first handover may not finish the job.
2. Confirm the generated site and instance. Ask for directions; search secret rooms and dressing underground.
3. Check inventory for assigned cargo. Keep it apart from sale loot.
4. Read injury-triggered demands before further attacks. A fast kill may bypass feedback; report missing progress rather than assuming another kill repairs it.
5. Check reputation consequences before blaming a bug. An Item on Loan explicitly lowers Thieves Guild standing on successful delivery.
6. Report the ID, site and last entry if blocked. Online reload and sold-item recovery remain unverified.


## Rewards and standing

Quest rewards explains payment and eligible gear. Online protection removes the ordinary failure penalty; explicit scripted reputation changes still apply, including expiry consequences. Paid success can harm another faction. No universal purse or safe refusal is established.
