docs.title: Commoner work
docs.summary: Follow local leads, find missing people, clear beasts from named buildings and deliver the actual quest goods.
docs.body:
Checked against e4f093166. This page describes DFO Online.

> [!tip] At a glance
> - Note the person, exact building, deadline and reporting contact.
> - Ask directions instead of searching every house in town.
> - Follow new leads before treating a missing person as a dungeon rescue.
> - Keep supplied goods for their recipient; similar loot may not count.

## What every version shares

| Field | Shared shape and variations |
|---|---|
| Giver/guild | Ordinary people; giver commonly recorded as peasant |
| Gate | Character level or reputation; some offers restrict gender, adult content or repeat acceptance |
| Where | Generated local buildings, remote houses, contacts or dungeons |
| Time | Assignment-specific, sometimes listed as variable; online deadlines charge played time |
| Reward shape | Scripted gold, an object or another outcome; eligible success can add gear and Renown |
| Instance | Choose Your instance when offered; private quest dungeons are full-size and admit your party |


## How to read the offer

Record town, building, person, object, deadline and return contact. Identify the action: investigate, rescue, kill, deliver or obtain a remedy. Local trouble can lead out of town. Check Quests and Time remains.

Use talking to people for directions. One unhelpful answer does not prove a building is missing. These jobs differ from the questline ladder.

## The shapes you will see

1. Missing-person investigation. Missing Person Case (A0C00Y16) uses local contacts and a hiding place. Follow named leads and report what you learn.
2. Rescue from a house. The Abducted Child (A0C10Y02) places the child at a remote house with possible assassins. Find and speak to the child, then return to the giver.
3. Beasts indoors. The Exterminator (A0C00Y07) creates repeated attackers at the assigned building. Stay for the required kills and return only after completion feedback.
4. Delivery. The Delivery Boy (A0C00Y14) stays local; The Courier (A0C00Y15) uses a remote recipient. Carry the supplied item and confirm delivery.
5. Purchase or remedy. The Birthday Present (A0C01Y09) involves a merchant and gift; The Cure (A0C00Y11) follows a patient and healer. Bring spending money and follow recipient instructions.


## Quick path

1. Read the offer and check any eligibility or purchase requirement.
2. Record the objective, named places, people and deadline.
3. Ask for directions and locate the assigned building.
4. Choose the quest instance when offered; investigate or search there.
5. Complete the conversation, kills, purchase or delivery; read updates.
6. Follow changed leads and reach the named final contact.


## What gets players stuck

Work through this fix order:

1. Re-read the latest lead. Confirm town, building and instance.
2. Ask several people for directions. Underground, check the 3D map, secret doors and unexplored rooms; there is no fixed pin.
3. Confirm the quest item, not similar loot. Inspect containers and dressing.
4. Check combat feedback: infestations need repeated kills, rescues need contact, and a fast kill does not prove every trigger ran.
5. Recheck the clock and final recipient. If blocked, report the quest ID, site and last entry; online reload and sold-item recovery are unverified.


## Rewards and standing

See quest rewards for payment and eligible gear. Ordinary online failure costs no faction standing; scripted outcomes remain separate. The Abducted Child lowers Dark Brotherhood standing on successful rescue.

docs.title: Merchant work
docs.summary: Plan merchant deliveries, recover assigned property and read changing instructions before fighting or handing goods over.
docs.body:
Checked against e4f093166. This page describes DFO Online.

> [!tip] At a glance
> - Record the shop, recipient, goods and deadline before accepting.
> - Keep assigned property separate from goods you intend to sell.
> - Check opening hours and the named person's location before another journey.
> - Read surrender or rescue prompts before continuing an attack.

## What every version shares

| Field | Shared shape and variations |
|---|---|
| Giver | Merchant questor; social work rather than a guild-rank ladder |
| Gate | Offer selection can depend on character level, reputation and other social restrictions |
| Where | Generated shops, houses, contacts and dungeons |
| Time | Assignment-specific deadline; online deadlines charge played time |
| Completion | Delivery, recovery, investigation or bringing someone back |
| Instance | Choose Your instance when offered; private quest dungeons are full-size |

## How to read the offer

Write down region, town, building, person, object, deadline and reporting contact. Identify whether the merchant wants an object returned, a delivery made or a person protected. Check Quests and Time remains after new letters arrive; the original destination may no longer be your next stop.

Use shops and prices for counter types and selling. A quest conversation and an ordinary sale are different interactions. The questline ladder describes the separate The Merchant's Road introduction.

## The shapes you will see

1. Delivery with trouble. Smuggling (K0C00Y03) supplies cargo for a remote contact. A letter and a guard can change the situation. Read the current directions and any demand before surrendering the goods.
2. Missing property. A Rare Book (K0C00Y08) places a specific book in a dungeon. Recover it and return to the merchant; an ordinary book from a shelf does not replace it.
3. Exchange of loyalties. An Object Lesson (K0C00Y00) combines a planted letter, recovered property and a competitor's counteroffer. Your recipient affects standing; possession alone does not settle the job.
4. Protecting or recovering a person. The Recompense (K0C00Y09) distinguishes bringing the assigned opponent back alive from killing them. Stop for injury feedback. The Lost Child (K0C00Y05) requires contact with the child and a return to the giver.
5. Investigation. A Mix-Up (K0C00Y06) moves among witnesses, evidence and generated buildings. Read letters and follow the latest lead rather than searching every shop.

## Quick path

1. Read the objective and record every contact and clock.
2. Plan access to the named shop or house and leave carrying space.
3. Collect supplied goods or visit the assigned site.
4. Select the quest instance when offered; complete the required interaction.
5. Read changed directions and reach the final recipient before selling anything.

## What gets players stuck

1. Recheck the exact building, person and instance. A closed shop or a witness who moved is not proof of a missing destination; ask for directions and check the time.
2. For dungeon property, inspect the 3D map, secret doors, containers and dressing.
3. Confirm you carry the quest object, not similar loot. Check the deadline before another outward or return trip.
4. Read combat feedback and legal consequences. Merchant employment does not suspend the law.
5. Report the ID, site and last entry if blocked. Online reload and sold-item recovery remain unverified.

## Rewards and standing

Quest rewards explains variable payment and eligible gear. Ordinary online failure costs no faction standing; explicit branch changes and legal consequences remain separate. There is no universal merchant purse.

docs.title: Coven work
docs.summary: Carry coven ingredients, escort people and follow remote contacts while separating recovery jobs from dangerous deliveries.
docs.body:
Checked against e4f093166. This page describes DFO Online.

> [!tip] At a glance
> - Record the coven, remote sites, requested objects and return contact.
> - Bring back the assigned ingredients, not ordinary substitutes.
> - Read delivery and rescue instructions before attacking.
> - Treat a cure effect as a specific branch, not a promise from every witch.

## What every version shares

| Field | Shared shape and variations |
|---|---|
| Giver | Coven questor |
| Gate | Offer-specific eligibility; no universal cure entitlement |
| Where | Generated remote buildings, contacts and dungeons |
| Time | Offer-specific deadline; online deadlines charge played time |
| Completion | Return ingredients, deliver an object, escort someone or defeat a designated foe |
| Instance | Your instance when offered; private quest dungeons are full-size |

## How to read the offer

Record region, destination, object, recipient, deadline and return coven. Remote sites make the return journey part of your preparation. Check Quests and Time remains before setting out again. Keep letters and supplied items until the task confirms completion.

An accusation, feud or supernatural problem does not establish the required action. Check whether you must recover evidence, remove an enemy or deliver something. The checked coven examples do not establish a general exorcism procedure or a separate coven-feud ladder. Follow the actual offer rather than importing the steps from temple errands.

## The shapes you will see

1. Ingredient circuit. A Great Errand (Q0C10Y00) places different ingredients in separate dungeons. Return with each assigned object and confirm each hand-in; clearing one dungeon does not finish the circuit.
2. Combat ingredient. The Daedra's Heart (Q0C4XY04) gives a heart to a quest foe through an injury trigger. Inspect the defeated carrier and return the heart. Generic monster loot is not the assignment.
3. Escort and rescue. Public Relation (Q0C00Y03) escorts a child to a remote house before reporting back. The Imprisoned Witch (Q0C00Y07) requires the supplied clothing when contacting the captive.
4. Dangerous delivery. A Treacherous Gift (Q0C0XY02) changes the recipient into an enemy. Killing that enemy changes the return outcome. Read feedback before treating the transformation as an instruction to kill.
5. Recovery or removal. The Libel (Q0C00Y01) requires a document from a remote temple; Problems with Vampires (Q0C00Y06) requires the designated dungeon kill. These objectives need different completion checks.
6. Special mixture. A Special Mixture (Q0C00Y04) supplies a quest potion for a mage. Using it invokes cure actions and changes the delivery outcome; it is not ordinary sale stock.

## Quick path

1. Identify the action and record all remote destinations.
2. Retain supplied objects and prepare access tools and healing.
3. Travel to the named contact or quest instance.
4. Complete each ingredient, escort, delivery or combat step.
5. Read updates, return to the correct coven and confirm completion.

## What gets players stuck

1. Confirm the remote building and instance before searching nearby sites.
2. Check secret doors and unexplored rooms on the 3D map; inspect dressing and carriers for ingredients.
3. Separate quest objects from loot. Recheck the clock before another dungeon or return journey.
4. Read prompts before killing or consuming anything. Coven work can have standing, disease or legal consequences.
5. Report the ID, site and last entry if blocked. Online reload and replacement-item recovery are unverified.

## Rewards and standing

See quest rewards for eligible gear and variable payment, and cures for curse routes. Ordinary online failure protection does not erase explicit scripted consequences. The Covens' Hoard is a separate questline.

docs.title: Vampire clan work
docs.summary: Follow clan letters, resolve rivalries and protect clan interests without assuming every assignment requires a kill.
docs.body:
Checked against e4f093166. This page describes DFO Online.

> [!tip] At a glance
> - Check your vampire state and clan assignment before looking for work.
> - Read the letter to expose its contact or destination.
> - Keep proof and research until the intended recipient accepts them.
> - Stop at intimidation feedback; killing can spoil that outcome.

## What every version shares

| Field | Shared shape and variations |
|---|---|
| Giver | Vampire clan contact introduced by quest mail |
| Gate | Vampire/clan prerequisites; initiation differs from member work |
| Where | Generated contacts and dungeons; no fixed clan-job itinerary |
| Time | Letter and assignment clocks vary; online deadlines charge played time |
| Completion | Conversation, delivery, proof, escort, intimidation or kill |
| Instance | Choose Your instance when offered; private quest dungeons are full-size |

## How to read the offer

Open the letter, then record the clan contact, region, site, target, proof, reporting person and deadline. Several scripts add conversation topics or reveal a dungeon only after reading or meeting someone. Carrying unread mail is not the same as following its lead.

Check Quests and Time remains. Vampire letters belong to curse and clan systems; do not assume the separate questline ladder describes their arrival. Lycanthropy and vampirism explains the curse and changed guild access. A cure request is a different decision from clan service.

## The shapes you will see

1. Initiation. The Rite of Acceptance (P0A01L00) reveals a dungeon through its letter, requires a vampire kill and then a meeting with the clan contact. Do not treat the first letter as completed initiation.
2. Letter delivery. The Vampire's Letter (P0B00L01) moves from a clan contact to another recipient, then back for payment. Reading the introduction and delivering the assigned letter are separate steps.
3. Rival removal. Territorial Battles (P0B00L03) puts proof on a rival ancient vampire. Recover and return that proof. An Old Enemy (P0B00L04) instead requires the assigned vampire kill and a report.
4. Protecting secrecy. Deadly Knowledge (P0B00L06) involves research and an alternate Mages Guild interest. This is a Masquerade concern in practical terms: who receives dangerous knowledge matters. Read the competing offer before choosing your recipient.
5. Intimidation. Intimidation (P0B10L07) rewards injuring and sparing the designated knight. Killing the knight changes the outcome and costs clan favour.
6. Chaperoning. The Chaperone (P0B10L10) takes a clan member to another vampire contact with possible attackers along the way. Reach that contact; fighting attackers alone does not finish the escort.

## Quick path

1. Confirm the relevant vampire and clan prerequisites.
2. Read the letter and note the objective and clock.
3. Meet the named contact before following newly revealed sites.
4. Enter the quest instance when offered and perform the assigned action.
5. Preserve proof, read branch prompts and report to the final contact.

## What gets players stuck

1. Recheck unread letters, current objective, exact building and instance.
2. Search secret doors and unexplored rooms on the 3D map; inspect the proof carrier's inventory.
3. Keep quest proof separate from sale loot. Ordinary boots or research-like objects may not substitute.
4. Recheck tight clocks and injury feedback. Clan favour and the law are separate concerns.
5. Report the ID, site and last entry if blocked. Online reload and sold-item recovery remain unverified.

## Rewards and standing

Quest rewards explains eligible gear and payment. Some scripts award no object. Online ordinary failure protection does not cancel explicit expiry or branch penalties; the clan scripts contain both. No fixed site or universal reward applies.

docs.title: Daedric quests
docs.summary: Read each Prince's request, follow its generated targets and contacts, and check artifact or branch consequences before committing.
docs.body:
Checked against e4f093166. This page describes DFO Online.

> [!tip] At a glance
> - Treat each Prince's request as its own assignment.
> - Record the target, destination, reporting contact and deadline.
> - Read refusals and counteroffers before choosing.
> - Distinguish the promised artifact from ordinary loot and gear rewards.

## What every version shares

| Field | Shared shape and variations |
|---|---|
| Giver | One named Prince; a mortal contact can handle completion |
| Gate | Access to that Prince's offer; the index alone does not establish summoning availability |
| Where | Generated dungeons, buildings and contacts |
| Time | Request-specific deadline; online deadlines charge played time |
| Reward | Named artifact or branch-specific outcome, not a universal purse |
| Instance | Your instance when offered; private quest dungeons are full-size |

## How to read the offer

Write down the Prince, requested action, region, site, target, object, deadline and final contact. A kill request may pay through a librarian or another intermediary. Do not return to the original encounter merely because you have defeated someone underground.

Check Quests and Time remains after letters or demands. Read refusal prompts carefully: refusing can end an offer rather than postpone it. This page does not establish that a refused request returns. One Prince and one request can still contain several stages and competing outcomes.

## The shapes you will see

1. Kill and report. Lady Azura's Quest (T0C00Y00) requires the assigned dungeon target and then the librarian contact. The scripted reward is Azura's Star; unrelated kills do not meet the condition.
2. Remote reward contact. Clavicus Vile's Quest (V0C00Y00) separates the dungeon kill from a contact in a generated tavern. Record both destinations before travelling.
3. Delivery or combat branch. Hermaeus Mora's Quest (W0C00Y00) includes an injury-triggered offer involving a magic item and a changed target location. Read the prompt and current objective before continuing to attack or delivering anything.
4. Moving target. Molag Bal's Quest (20C00Y00) can move its mage to another dungeon after injury. Read the quest map to reveal the hideout. A missing opponent can indicate a new stage rather than a failed spawn.
5. Counteroffer. Nocturnal's Quest (40C00Y00) introduces alternative artifacts and a betrayal branch. That branch changes standing and later events. An attractive item is not evidence that the original request is complete.

## Quick path

1. Read the request and any refusal consequences before accepting.
2. Record the action, contacts, generated sites and deadline.
3. Prepare access tools and equipment suitable for the assigned target.
4. Enter the quest instance when offered; pause for injury-triggered choices.
5. Follow new letters or locations and reach the stated completion contact.

## What gets players stuck

1. Confirm the latest target location, building and instance before retracing a dungeon.
2. Inspect the 3D map, secret doors and unexplored rooms. Look for maps and quest objects among dressing and containers.
3. Keep assigned objects apart from sale loot. Check the clock before following a second destination.
4. Read branch and legal consequences before attacking a town contact. Ordinary failure protection does not make every choice harmless.
5. Report the ID, site and last entry if blocked. Online reload, artifact replacement and refusal recovery remain unverified.

## Rewards and standing

See quest rewards for special-reward exceptions and loot rarity for Artifact as a separate category. Using Oghma Infinium, Mora's reward, consumes the book and opens attribute advancement: treat that as a lasting character choice. Reversal is unverified. Ordinary online failure costs no faction standing; explicit branches can still change it.

docs.title: Curse cure quests
docs.summary: Follow hunter letters and distinguish confirmed vampire and werebeast cure actions from leads, delays and choices that keep the curse.
docs.body:
Checked against e4f093166. This page describes DFO Online.

> [!tip] At a glance
> - Establish whether you have an infection or a completed curse.
> - Read the hunter letter and record each newly named contact.
> - Treat a revealed coven or map as a lead, not confirmation of a cure.
> - Read irreversible choices before attacking or transferring the curse.

## What every version shares

| Field | Shared shape and variations |
|---|---|
| Entry | Curse-related hunter letter; vampire and werebeast scripts differ |
| Prerequisite | Relevant completed curse; ordinary infection treatment is separate |
| Where | Generated contacts and dungeons; a werebeast branch reveals a named coven |
| Time | Several clocks and contact windows; online deadlines charge played time |
| Outcome | Explicit cure action, retained curse or further information |
| Instance | Choose Your instance when offered for the assigned destination |

## How to read the offer

Read the letter, then record region, contact, destination, token or vial, deadline and the choice you are being asked to make. Check Quests and Time remains after each conversation. A contact can disappear when a window closes; do not assume every wait is a deadline or every clock starts together.

Lycanthropy and vampirism distinguishes infection treatment from completed-curse removal. A disease-stage remedy is not evidence that an established curse will disappear. These letters are separate from the introductions in the questline ladder; no immediate letter arrival is promised.

## The shapes you will see

The cure category contains two scripts. These are branches within them, not additional quests.

1. Vampire bloodline investigation. Cure for Vampirism ($CUREVAM) introduces vampire contacts and a token. Follow the Keeper of the Bloodline lead to distinguish the actual bloodfather from another ancient vampire.
2. Vampire cure or loyalty. In $CUREVAM, killing the bloodfather invokes the cure. Another choice lets you stay loyal and keep vampirism. Killing the other ancient vampire changes standing without invoking the cure.
3. Werebeast bloodline route. Cure for Lycanthropy ($CUREWER) leads through a priest, an alchemist's vial and the last descendant. Confirming the transfer invokes the cure and legal consequences. Read this choice before giving the vial to the child; it affects another person.
4. Werebeast research route. $CUREWER also offers dungeon documents leading toward Glenmoril Coven. Reading the documents reveals further locations. Those reveal tasks do not themselves invoke a cure. Follow the resulting offer; do not assume arriving at the coven completes treatment.

## Quick path

1. Confirm your current infection or curse state.
2. Read the relevant letter and record the contacts and windows.
3. Follow conversations before searching newly revealed destinations.
4. Retain tokens, documents and vials for their specific interactions.
5. Read the final choice, then check the resulting curse state and journal.

## What gets players stuck

1. Recheck prerequisites, unread mail, latest contact and exact building. A cure quest is not ordinary clan work.
2. Confirm the quest instance. Search the 3D map, secret doors and dressing for documents; generic loot is not a substitute.
3. Check contact windows and the clock before another trip. Hunters and disappearing contacts can be scripted events.
4. Confirm identity before killing. Neither a dead ancient vampire nor a revealed coven proves a cure occurred.
5. Report the ID, site and last entry if blocked. Online reload, replacement tokens and reversal of completed choices are unverified.

## Rewards and standing

The practical outcome is your curse state. Quest rewards explains ordinary payment separately. Online failure protection does not erase scripted standing or legal changes, and the sources establish no universal potion, shrine interaction or guaranteed kinder route.

docs.title: Keys and commands
docs.summary: DFO's default keyboard and mouse bindings, the chat channels and commands you can use, and where to rebind actions.
docs.body:
> [!tip] At a glance
> - These are DFO Online's shipped defaults; your Controls screen shows your current bindings.
> - Rebind actions under Settings › Controls › Key bindings.
> - Enter opens online chat; press Y to free the mouse cursor.
> - Use /help, /lang, /emotes or /breach help for lists from inside the game.

## Common default keys

| Key or button | Default action |
|---|---|
| Esc | Open the pause menu when no overlay is open; close/back out of overlays |
| W / S | Move forward / backward |
| A / D | Move left / right |
| Left / Right Arrow | Turn left / right |
| Space | Jump; also float up while swimming or levitating |
| C / Left Shift | Crouch / run |
| R / T | Rest / transport |
| Left mouse / right mouse | Activate the center object / swing weapon |
| Middle mouse (wheel button) | Party ping: marks a point for your party (mark 5 s, route 12 s) |
| F3 | Toggle auto-run |
| Mouse back / forward side button | Weapon technique / toggle first- and third-person view |
| Z / H | Ready weapon / switch hand |
| Backspace / Q /  | Cast / recast / abort spell |
| U | Use magic item |
| I / F5 / F6 | Status / character sheet / inventory |
| L / N / M / V | LogBook / NoteBook / AutoMap / TravelMap |
| F | Social interaction |
| Enter | Open online chat (offline, Enter frees the mouse cursor) |
| Y | Free the mouse cursor |
| E / Tab | Interact / QuickDial |
| P / J | Quick Loot All / Quick Loot Open |
| 1 / 2 / 3 / 4 | QuickUse1 / QuickUse2 / QuickSpell / QuickOffHand |
| 5–0 | Hotbar slots 5–10 |
| F8 | Screenshot |
| F9 / F11 | Offline quick save / quick load; loading during online play is disabled. See Saving and returning. |
| Left Alt (hold) | Interaction-mode wheel: Steal, Grab, Info or Talk |

Several actions share a key by context. For example, Space's float action applies while swimming or levitating; the Controls screen is the authority for the context and your active binding.

## Other shipped actions

| Action | Default key |
|---|---|
| Look up / look down / centre view | Insert / Delete / Home |
| Torch toggle / drop / throw | O / G / X |
| Mount horse / summon horse | Comma / Period |
| SaddlePanel / ShipHold | F2 / F4 |
| FollowPaths ashore / Spyglass aboard ship | K |
| Float up / down | Page Up / Page Down |
| Switch shoulder | B |
| Auto perspective | Numpad + |
| Legacy family view | Numpad / |
| Choose act at a gathering spot / more sail at the helm | Up Arrow |
| Open Professions off the helm / less sail at the helm | Down Arrow |
| Boat disembark | Quote (') |
| Boat light toggle | Semicolon (;) |
| Boat sail toggle | End |
| Boat trim left / right | Left / right bracket ([ / ]) |
| Boat trim modifier | Backslash (\) |
| Boat time scale up / down / reset | Numpad  / Numpad - / Numpad Enter |

Sneak (held, without crouching), TravelView, WalkMode and DebugOverlay ship unbound. C remains the default Crouch action, which also sneaks. TravelView is the separate Overworld view; V is TravelMap. A controller has separate mappings. You can rebind any supported action in Controls; do not assume a key described in an older guide is free.

## Chat channels

Use a slash command or the chat tabs to select a channel:

| Channel | Commands |
|---|---|
| World | /world, /g |
| Region | /region, /r |
| Local | /local, /l, /say, /s |
| Party | /party, /p |
| Guild | /guild, /gu |
| Trade | /trade, /tr |
| Looking for group | /lfg |
| Language channel | /lc (after joining one with /lang) |
| Local, out of character | /ooc |

Trade and LFG are opt-in channels: /join trade or /join lfg adds the tab, /leave removes it, and saying something on one joins it. Local chat is nearby in-character speech; /ooc sends a nearby out-of-character line. /lang [code|off] joins or leaves a language channel.

## Useful commands

- /help lists commands. /lang lists language channels, and /emotes lists available gestures.
- /roll or /dice makes a dice roll; /me describes an action, /rp sends a roleplay line, and /wave, /bow and /nod are gesture commands.
- /ready explains party resting online; /leader travels to your party leader; /travel gets you ready for the leader's journey (the leader uses it to call the journey off). /mentor shows whether you are mentoring your party; mentoring switches on by itself.
- /mail or /mailbox opens mail. /find or /who finds players; /search [name] searches a name.
- /unstuck leaves by the door you came in, or outdoors takes you to the nearest town; /unstuck cancel stops it.
- /block, /unblock and /blocked manage your block list. /report  [category][: note] reports player conduct; /rules shows the Code of Conduct.
- /bug opens a private report form. It is different from /report.
- /breach opens Elite Breach commands; /breach help prints their help.

Unknown slash commands are refused rather than broadcast as ordinary chat; start a line with // to send text that begins with a slash. /event is a developer's live-event command, not a player utility.

## Common mistakes

- Treating an old guide's suggested rebind key as unassigned can collide with a shipped mod action; check your live Controls list first.
- Sending a slash typo as chat will not broadcast it as text.
- Mixing up /bug and /report sends a private issue report when you meant to report a player, or vice versa.

## Next

- The glossary

docs.title: Privateer's Hold tutorial
docs.summary: Use the fixed opening to learn controls, read the journal, find the exit and move into your first town.
docs.body:
Checked against e4f093166. This page describes DFO Online.

> [!tip] At a glance
> - Check your controls and inventory before exploring.
> - Open the journal to review active quests and keep notes.
> - Find and activate the exit; dismissing guidance does not move you outside.
> - Finish public-room exploration before leaving the Hold online.

## What the opening shares

| Field | Shared shape and variations |
|---|---|
| Index entry | Tutorial (TUTOR); its old pages are replaced in DFO |
| Place | Privateer's Hold; no generated quest destination |
| Entry | DFO's welcome tour and later contextual guidance |
| Progress | Learn controls and explore; no tutorial kill quota |
| Time | No delivery deadline for the welcome tour |
| Exit | Physically leaving uses the dungeon exit |

## How to read the offer

Read opening guidance, then check controls and settings. DFO's tour shows your bound actions. The quest browser retains the vendored TUTOR entry, but the live startup list does not start that script. Its former world-quest handoff starts separately; finishing old tutorial pages is not a prerequisite.

Press L for the journal's active quests or N for its notebook by default. Record what you want to revisit. Reread guidance under Menu → Tutorials. Read state belongs to your device, so a second character may not see already-read pages automatically.

## The shapes you will see

The category has one example ID, TUTOR. Its old sequence covers these subjects; DFO now teaches them through its catalogue rather than running that sequence.

1. First controls and equipment. The old script introduces inventory, attacks, rest and magic. DFO's welcome tour covers movement, interaction, bars, compass and menu. Check equipment and practise your actions; see your first minutes.
2. Dungeon exploration. The old sequence introduces doors, loot and interactive objects. Learn activation before attacking an object. This page supplies no room-by-room route or guaranteed treasure location.
3. Exit transition. TUTOR used a location trigger to advance after departure. In DFO, find the actual exit regardless of which guidance you have read; see leaving the Hold.
4. Town orientation. The old city-entry stage introduced conversations, shops and work. DFO supplies contextual tutorials for its systems. Neither a shop purchase nor a guild assignment is an exit condition.

## Quick path

1. Read the opening guidance and check your current bindings.
2. Inspect your pack and ready equipment suited to your skills.
3. Explore while watching health and fatigue; review the journal as needed.
4. Find and activate the dungeon exit when ready to leave.
5. Continue toward town and use directions to find services and work.

## What gets players stuck

1. If a control does nothing, inspect its current binding and active menu before following a classic shortcut.
2. If exploration stalls, check the 3D map, unexplored passages and secret doors. An internal door is not the exit.
3. Separate ordinary loot from future quest goods. The tutorial has no required fetch object in the index; selling treasure is not an exit condition.
4. For missing guidance, check the Tutorials menu and popup setting. Do not wait for the retired script's timed pages or city-entry prompt.
5. Online, the public Hold refuses re-entry after departure; your private instance is separate. Record the script ID and last prompt if blocked. Reload recovery is unverified.

## Rewards and standing

The old script awards no gold purse or artifact; DFO's tour is guidance. See quest rewards for employment. In town, check shop hours and the law before entering buildings or resting.

docs.body: music in the woods the thirteenth of frostfall fixed place letter letter gold star8 (2026-10-20; bible/11-multiplayer/starfall.md section 7): the thirteenth of frostfall, step 1 of 4. the port's own script on dfu's machine (systems/questlines/qllines.js). started by the line's runner while the starfall runs (`needs: ['starfall']`), never offered by a questor: the letter is the offer. a wyrd sister at a tavern's door hands it over - the witches' festival's vendors are glenmoril's own (`ql act wyrd-met 1`, said as her window opens: scenes/witcheshost.js) - and if the player holds a fallen star before meeting one, morwen saw its thread burn and her raven brings a note instead (audit star8 t1: not a courier's clock - online rest8 cuts a delay to the short wait, two real minutes of play, and a raven on a clock would beat every sister). one or the other, never both. witnessed (net/questlineclaims.js `star`, the j1 receipt): it waits on a fallen star held (`ql act star-held 1`), then on the player at the glenmoril coven (`permanent glenmorilcoven`, the lycanthropy cure's own place - $curewer). a coven is an open-air place in daggerfall - one block of the wilds (witcaa00.rmb), no building and no dungeon, so no quest marker to stand a person on - and dfu's own quests meet one as this does, by the player's arrival (`pc at`, s0000007's). morwen meets the player at its fire. lore: canon - the witches' festival on the 13th of frostfall (text.rsc 8392), the music in the woods (q0c4xy04.qrc: "the witches must be celebrating"), the glenmoril witches who summon hircine alone (faction.txt 419, `summon: 4`), mephala's summoning day the festival's own (systems/daedrasummoning.js). the port's own: the covens' rite that sings a star down and binds it in black thread, morwen of glenmoril, her sisters at the taverns' doors, her raven.
